ability.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}}
First attested in the 1300s. From {{inh|en|enm|abilite||suitability, aptitude, ability}}, from {{der|en|fro|ablete|ableté}}, from {{der|en|la|habilitās||aptness, ability}}, from {{m|la|habilis||apt, fit, skillful, able}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|able|ity}}.

abortion.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-}}
From {{bor|en|la|abortiō|abortiōnem|t=miscarriage, abortion}}, from {{m|la|aborior|t=to miscarry}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|abort|ion}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ǣwyrp|lit=throwing out, rejection}}.

achievement.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:achevement<ety:inh<fro:achevement>>|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|frm|achevement}} (compare Modern {{cog|fr|achèvement}}), from {{der|en|fro|achevement}}, from the verb {{m|fro|achever}}, {{m|fro|achiever|t=to finish}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|achieve|ment}}. The heraldic sense may be influenced by {{m|en|hatchment}}.

accommodation.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:accommodation|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|fr|accommodation}}, from {{der|en|la|accommodātiō||adjustment, accommodation, compliance}}, from {{m|la|accommodō||adapt, put in order}}. Superficially {{suffix|en|accommodate|ion}}. The sense of "lodging" was first attested in 1600.

abstract.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:abstract}}
From {{inh|en|enm|abstract}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|abstractus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|abstrahō||draw away}}, formed from {{m|la|abs-||away}} + {{m|la|trahō||to pull, draw}}. The verbal sense is first attested in 1542.

absorb.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|frm:absorber<ety:inh<fro:assorbir<ety:inh<la:absorbeō>>>>}}
From {{der|en|frm|absorber}}, from {{der|en|fro|assorbir}}, from {{der|en|la|absorbeō|t=swallow up}}, from {{af|la|ab-|t1=from|sorbeō|t2=suck in, swallow|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*srebʰ-||to sip}}. Compare {{cog|fr|absorber}}.

abuse.text:
{{wikidata lexeme|L7463}}
From {{inh|en|enm|abusen}}, then from either {{der|en|fro|abus||improper use}}, or from {{der|en|la|abūsus||misused, using up}}, perfect active participle of {{m|la|abūtor||make improper use of, consume, abuse}}, from {{m|la|ab||away}} + {{m|la|ūtor||to use}}.<ref name=WI3>{{R:MW3 1976|page=8}}</ref> Equivalent to {{prefix|en|ab|use}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ə

academic.text:
{{etymon|en|:der<conj:and>|la-med:acadēmicus|fr:académique|tree=1}}
From both the {{der|en|la-med|acadēmicus}} and the {{der|en|fr|académique}}, from {{der|en|la|academia}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἀκαδημικός}}, from {{m|grc|Ἀκαδημία}} or {{m|grc|Ἀκαδήμεια}}, the name of the place where Plato taught; compare {{m|en|academy}}.<ref name=WI3>{{R:MW3 1976}}</ref> {{surf|en|academy|-ic}}.

accomplish.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*pleh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|accomplisshen}}, {{m|enm|acomplissen}}, from {{der|en|fro||acompliss-}}, extended stem of {{m|fro|acomplir}} (Modern French {{m|fr|accomplir}}),<ref>{{R:MED Online|accomplisshen|v|MED286|20 October 2019|date=2018}}</ref> from {{der|en|la-vul||*(ac)complīre}}, from {{der|en|la|compleo|complēre|t=fill up/out, complete|pos=whence English {{m|en|complete}}

access.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|accesse}}, {{m|enm|acces}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|acces||attack, onslaught}} or from its source {{der|en|la|accessus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|accēdō||approach; accede}}, from {{m|la|ad||to, toward, at}} + {{m|la|cēdō||move, yield}}. {{doublet|en|accessus}}. First attested in the early 14th century. The sense "entrance" was first attested about 1380.

====Pronu

accumulate.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:accumylaten<ety:bor<la:accumulātus>>|tree=1}}
First attested c. 1487; from {{inh|en|enm|accumylaten}}, {{bor+|en|la|accumulātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|accumulō||to amass, pile up}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), formed from {{m

accuse.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:acusen<ety:bor<fro:acuser>>|tree=1}}
First attested around 1300. From {{inh|en|enm|acusen}}, from {{der|en|fro|acuser}}, from {{der|en|la|accūsō||to call to account, accuse}}, from {{m|la|ad|t=to}} + {{m|la|causa|t=cause, lawsuit, reason}}. Akin to {{m|en|cause}}. Displaced native {{cog|en||[[bewray#Etymology|bewray]]}} and {{noncog|ang|sċyldan}}.

accounting.text:
* First attested in the late 14th century.
* {{suffix|en|account|ing}}

accommodate.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|la:accommodātus|tree=1}}
First use appears c. the 1530s, {{bor+|en|la|accommodātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|accommodō}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|ad-||to, towards, at}} + {{m|la|commodō||to provide, lend; to make fit

advertisement.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:advertissement|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|frm|advertissement||statement calling attention}}, compare {{cog|fr|avertissement||warning}}. See [[advertise]]. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|advertise|ment}}.

acknowledge.text: Recorded since 1553, a blend of {{der|en|enm|aknowen||to recognize, acknowledge}} and {{m|enm|knowelechen||to discover, reveal, acknowledge}}. The former verb is from {{der|en|ang|oncnāwan|oncnāwan, ācnāwan|to know, recognize, acknowledge}}, from {{m|ang|on}} + {{m|ang|cnāwan||to know}}. The latter is related to the noun at hand in {{m|en|knowledge}}. For the formation compare {{cog|la|agnōscō}} a

acquire.text: From {{inh|en|enm|acqueren}}, from {{der|en|fro|aquerre}}, from {{der|en|la|acquirō}}; {{m|la|ad-}} + {{m|la|quaerō|t=to seek for}}. See {{m|en|quest}}.

adapt.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:*adapten<ety:der<la:adaptō>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|*adapten}} (attested in {{cog|enm|adapted|pos=past participle}}), from {{der|en|la|[[adaptō|adaptāre]]||to fit to}}, from {{m|la|ad-||to}} + {{m|la|[[apto|aptāre]]||to make fit}}, from {{m|la|aptus||fit}}; see [[apt]].

adequate.text:
{{etymon|en|:lbor|la:adaequātus|tree=1}}
{{lbor|en|la|adaequātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|adaequō||to make equal to}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), further from {{m|la|ad||to, towards, at}} + {{m|la|aequō||to make equal, equalize}}, from {{m|la|aequus||equa

adopt.text: From {{der|en|frm|adopter}}, from {{der|en|la|adoptō}}; {{compound|la|ad|optō|nocat=1|t2=to choose, desire}}, equivalent to {{af|en|ad-|opt}}.

advertise.text: From {{inh|en|enm|advertisen}}, from {{der|en|xno|advertir||to inform}}, {{m|xno|avertir}}, {{der|en|frm|advertir}}, {{m|fr|avertir||to warn, give notice to}}, with the French {{m|fr|-iss-}} infix assimilated to {{m|en|-ise}}, {{m|en|-ize}} and probably influenced by the noun {{m|en|advertisement}}. Compare also {{m|en|advert}}.

acquisition.text: From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|acquisicion}}, from {{der|en|la|acquisītiō}}, from {{m|la|acquīrō|acquīrō, acquīrere}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|acquire|ition}}.

adjust.text: From {{inh|en|enm|ajusten}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|adjuster}}, or {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|ad||to, up to, towards}} + {{m|la|iustus||correct, proper, exact}}; Equivalent to {{pre|en|ad|just}}. Probably influenced in sense by {{der|en|fro|ajouster}} (cf. modern {{m|fr|ajouter}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*adiuxtāre}}, from {{der|en|la|iuxta}}. The Middle English originally meant "to corr

administer.text: From {{inh|en|enm|administren}}, from {{der|en|fro|aminister}}, from {{der|en|la|administrare||to manage, execute}}, from {{m|la|ad||to}} + {{m|la|ministrare||to attend, serve}}, from {{m|la|minister||servant}}; see {{m|en|minister}}.

alien.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂el- (other)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|alien}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|fro|alien}}, {{m|fro|aliene}}, from {{der|en|la|aliēnus|t=belonging to someone else”, ''later'' “exotic, foreign}}, from {{der|en|la|alius|t=other}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂élyos}}. Related to {{cog|en|else}}.

advocate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*wekʷ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|advocat}}, {{m|enm|advoket}}, from {{der|en|fro|advocat}}, from {{der|en|la|advocātus||an advocate}}, from the [[substantivization]] of the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|advoco|advocāre|to call for}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=substantive|pos1=noun-forming suffix}}), from a [[calque]] of {{noncog|grc|παράκλητος}}

aggregate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ger-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|aggregat|aggregat(e)|t=a sum, unit, complex, aggregate}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la-new|aggregātum||an aggregate}}, [[substantivize]]d from the {{glossary|nominative}} {{glossary|neuter}} {{glossary|singular}} of {{m|la|aggregātus}}, the  {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|aggregō||to flock together}}, from {{m|

affection.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|affection}}, {{m|enm|affeccion}}, {{m|enm|affeccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|affection}}, from {{der|en|la|affectiōnem}}, from {{m|la|affectiō}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|affect|ion}}.
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}

afford.text: From {{inh|en|enm|afforthen}}, {{m|enm|aforthen}}, {{m|enm|avorthien}}, from earlier {{m|enm|iforthen}}, {{m|enm|iforthien}}, {{m|enm|ȝeforthien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|forþian}}, {{m|ang|ġeforþian|t=to further, accomplish, afford}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*furþōną}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*furþą|t=forth, forward}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|a|forth}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|forða|t=to forward oneself, s

agency.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|la-med:agēntia|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|la-med|agentia}}, from {{der|en|la|agēns}} (present participle of {{m|la|agere||to act}}), {{m|la|agentis}} (cognate with {{cog|fr|agence}}, see also {{m|en|agent}}).

aim.text:
The verb is from {{inh|en|enm|amen}}, {{m|enm|aimen}}, {{m|enm|eimen||to guess at, to estimate, to aim}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|esmer}}, {{m|fro|aesmer}}, {{m|fro|asmer}}, from {{der|en|la|ad-}} plus {{m|la|aestimare||to [[estimate]]}}, the compound perhaps being originally formed in {{cog|la-med|-}} ({{m|la|adaestimare}}), perhaps in Old French.
The noun is from {{inh|en|enm|ame}}, from {{de

alarm.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|alarme}}, {{m|enm|alarom}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|alarme}}, itself from {{der|en|roa-oit|-}} {{m|it|[[all'arme]]!|t=[[to arms]]!, to the weapons!}}, ultimately from {{der|en|la|arma|t=arms, weapons}}.

alliance.text: From {{inh|en|enm|alliaunce}}, from {{der|en|fro|aliance}} ({{der|en|fr|alliance|nocat=1}}). Equivalent to {{af|en|ally|-ance}}. Compare with {{noncog|grc-dor|ἁλία|t=assembly}}. See also {{af|en|al-#Etymology_2}}.

ally.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leyǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|allien}}, {{m|enm|alien|t=to form an alliance, associate, join; to become an ally; to introduce (someone) as an ally; to marry; to become related (to someone); to attack, engage in combat; to combine; (''cooking'') to combine ingredients, especially to bind them together}}{{nb...|alie, alleye, allie, ally, allye, aly, alye, alyȝe|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R

alone.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:allone|:afeq|all|one|:afeq|al-|one|tree=1}}

From {{inh|en|enm|allone}}, from earlier {{m|enm|[[all]] [[oon]]|lit=all one}}, contracted from the {{der|en|ang|-}} phrase {{m|ang|[[eall]] [[ān]]|t=completely alone}}, equivalent to {{af|en|al-<t:all>|one|nocat=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|alane|t=alone}}, {{cog|stq|alleene|t=alone}}, {{cog|fy|allinne|t=alone}}, {{cog|nl|alleen|t=alon

ambiguous.text:
{{etymon|en|:lbor|la:ambiguus|tree=1}}
From {{lbor|en|la|ambiguus||moving from side to side, of doubtful nature|notext=1}}, from {{m|la|ambigere||to go about, wander, doubt}}, from {{m|la|ambi-||around, about, on both sides}} + {{m|la|agere||to drive, move}}.

analysis.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|la-med:analysis|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|la-med|analysis}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἀνάλυσις}}, from {{m|grc|ἀναλύω|t=to unravel, investigate}}, from {{m|grc|ἀνα-|t=thoroughly}} + {{m|grc|λύω|t=to loosen}}.

alternative.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:alternatif|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|frm|alternatif}}, from {{der|en|la-med|alternātīvus|t=alternating}}, from the participle stem of {{der|en|la|alternō|t=interchange, alternate}}. {{surf|en|alternate|-ive}}. Compare {{m|en|alternate}}.

ambulance.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:ambulance|:afeq|-ance|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|fr|ambulance}}, which replaced {{m|fr|hôpital ambulant||moving hospital}} via the suffix {{m|fr|-ance}}, from {{der|en|la|ambulō||to walk; to go about}}.{{ref|name=Etymonline|{{EtymOnLine}}}}

amuse.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:*amusen<ety:bor<fro:amuser<ety:af<a-><muser>>>>|tree=1}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|*amusen|t=to mutter, be astonished, gaze meditatively on}}, from {{der|en|fro|amuser|t=to stupefy, waste time, be lost in thought}}, from {{m|fro|a-}} + {{m|fro|muser||to stare stupidly at, gape, wander, waste time, loiter, think carefully about, attend to}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} and obscure origi

ancient.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|auncyen}}, from {{der|en|fro|ancien}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*anteānus}}, composed of {{der|en|la|ante||before}} + {{m|la|-ānus|pos=adjective-forming suffix}}. The non-etymological {{glossary|excrescent}} /t/ is by analogy with the common ending {{m|en|-ent}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|anchient|aunchient|auncient|auntient|awncient|awntient|ancyent||obsolete}}
* {{alt|e

ancestor.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:auncestre|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|enm|ancestre}}, {{m|enm|auncestre}}, {{m|enm|ancessour}}; the first forms from {{der|en|fro|ancestre}} (modern French {{m|fr|ancêtre}}), from the {{der|en|la|-}} nominative {{m|la|antecessor||one who goes before}}; the last form from {{der|en|fro|ancessor}}, from Latin {{m|la|antecessōrem}}, accusative of {{m|la|antecessor}}, from {{suffix|la|ante

ankle.text:
{{etymon|en|id=skeletal joint|:inh|enm:ancle|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|ankel}}, {{m|enm|ancle}}, {{m|enm|ankyll}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ancol}} (compare {{m|ang|anclēow|t=ankle}} > Modern {{cog|en|anclef}}, {{m|en|ancliff}}, {{m|en|ancley}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*ankul}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ankulaz|t=ankle}}; akin to {{cog|is|ökkla}}, {{m|is|ökli}}, {{cog|da,sv|ankel}}, {{cog|nl|enkel}}, {{m|n

amend.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mend-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|amenden}}, from {{der|en|fro|amender}}, from {{der|en|la|ēmendō||free from faults}}, from {{m|la|ex||from, out of}} + {{m|la|mendum||fault}}. Compare [[aphetic]] {{m|en|mend}}. {{doublet|en|emend}}.

arbitrary.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:arbitrarie<ety:der<la:arbitrārius>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|arbitrarie}}, {{der|en|la|arbitrārius|t=arbitrary, uncertain}}, from {{m|la|arbiter|t=witness, on-looker, listener, judge, overseer}}.

annual.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:annuel|tree=1}}
First attested around 1382 as {{inh|en|enm|annuel}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|annuālem}}, {{m|la|annuālis}}, related to {{der|en|la|annālis}}, adjective form of {{m|la|annus|t=year}}. Used to categorize plants since 1710.

anticipate.text: {{bor+|en|la|anticipātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|anticipō||to anticipate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|ante-|t=before}}, + {{m|la|capiō||to take|pos=''cip-'' when prefixed}} + {{m|la|-ō|id=compound verb|pos=verb-forming suffix}}. See {{m|en|capable}}.

anxiety.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂enǵʰ-}}
{{bor+|en|la|ānxietās}}, from {{m|la|ānxius||anxious, solicitous, distressed, troubled}}, from {{m|la|angō||to distress, trouble}}, akin to {{cog|grc|ἄγχω||to choke}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|anxious|ety|id2=forming nouns}}. See {{l|en|anger}}; {{l|en|angst}}.

apartment.text: From {{bor|en|fr|appartement}}, from {{der|en|it|appartamento}}, from {{der|en|es|apartamiento|t=separation, seclusion}}, equivalent to {{af|en|apart|-ment}}. See {{m|en|apart}} and {{m|en|-ment}}.

apparent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|apparaunt}}, {{m|enm|aparaunt}}, from {{der|en|fro|aparent}}, {{m|fro|aparant}}, in turn from {{der|en|la|appārēns|appārēns, appārentis}}, present participle of {{m|la|appāreō}}.

appeal.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:apel//appel<ety:der<fro:apel>>|tree=1|id=noun}}
From {{inh|en|enm|apel}}, {{m|enm|appel|t=formal accusation brought in court; a challenge to trial by combat; an appeal to a higher court or authority; plea (for mercy, protection, etc.); pealing (of bells)}}{{nb...|apeel, apele, appele, appelle, pele|otherforms=1}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=ap(p)ēl|pos=n|id=MED1902}}</ref> from {{d

appearance.text: {{bor+|en|frm|apparence}}, from {{der|en|la|apparentia|}}, from {{m|la|appareo|}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|appear|ance}}. {{doublet|en|apparence|apparency}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|hīew||the way something looks or seems}} and {{m|ang|ætīewednes||act of appearing or coming into view}}.

appreciate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=before}}
Originated 1645–55; from {{bor|en|la-med|appreciātus||valued or appraised}}, later variant of {{der|en|la-lat|appretiātus||appraised}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|appretiō}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix|nocat=1}}), from {{af|la|ad-|pretium|-ō|alt1=a(d)|t1=toward|alt2=preti(um)|t2=price|i

appropriate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*preyH-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|appropriaten}}, from {{af|enm|appropriat|-en|t1=appropriated|id2=infinitival|nocat=1}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|appropriātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|appropriō||to make one's own}}, from {{m|la|ad||to}} + {{m|la|propriō||to make one's own}}, from {{af|la|proprius|-ō|t1=one's own, private|pos2=firs

article.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|article}}, from {{der|en|fro|article}}, from {{der|en|la|articulus|t=a joint, limb, member, part, division, the article in grammar, a point of time}}, from {{der|en|la|artus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂értus||that which is fit together; juncture, ordering}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*h₂er-||to join, fit (together)}}. {{doublet|en|articulus}}.

arise.text: From {{inh|en|enm|arisen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ārīsan||to arise, get up; rise; spring from, originate; spring up, ascend}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*uzrīsaną||to rise up, arise}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|a|rise}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|arise}}, {{m|sco|aryse||to arise, rise up, come into existence}}, {{cog|gml|errīsen||to stand up, arise}}, {{cog|goh|irrīsan||to rise up, fall}}, {{cog|got|𐌿𐍂𐍂𐌴𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽

array.text: From {{inh|en|enm|arrayen}}, from {{der|en|xno|arraier}} (compare {{cog|fro|arraier}}, {{m|fro|areer||to put in order}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*arrēdō||to put in order, arrange, array}}, from {{m|la|*rēdum||preparation, order}}, from {{der|en|frk|*raid}} or {{m|frk|*raidā||preparation, order}} or {{der|en|got|𐌲𐌰𐍂𐌰𐌹𐌸𐍃||ready, prepared}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*raidaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*raidiz||ready}}

artificial.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:artificial<t:man-made><ety:bor<fro:-<ety:bor<la:artificiālis>>>>|text=++|tree=+}}
Displaced native {{ncog|ang|cræftlīċ}}, with the earliest attestation {{abbr|c.|circa}} 1425.<ref>{{cite-web |en-US |url=https://languagelog.ldc.upenn.edu/nll/?p=74288 |title=Artificial |work={{w|Language Log}} |date=2026-09-25 |accessdate=2026-09-25 |publisher={{w|University of Pennsylvania}} |firs

assert.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ser- (bind)}}
From {{der|en|la|assertus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|asserō||declare someone free or a slave by laying hands upon him; hence free from, protect, defend; lay claim to, assert, declare}}, from {{m|la|ad||to}} + {{m|la|serō||join, range in a row}}.

Akin to {{cog|gmh|borte|t=border, trim}}, {{cog|de|Borte|t=ribbon, trimming}}. {{doublet|en|bordure}}. More at {{m|en|board}}.

boost.text: {{unk|en}}. The verb is first recorded 1815; the noun, 1825. Compare {{cog|sco|boost||to move; drive off; shoo away}}, {{m|sco|bost}}, {{m|sco|boast||to threaten; scold}}, {{cog|enm|boosten}}, {{m|enm|bosten||to threaten}}. Possible {{dbt|en|boast|nocap=1}}.

breed.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:breden<id:breed>|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|breden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|brēdan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*brōdijaną|t=to brood}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰreh₁-|t=warm}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|brede}}, {{m|sco|breid}}, {{cog|stq|briede}}, {{cog|fy|briede}}, {{cog|nds|bröden}}, {{cog|nl|broeden}}, {{cog|de|brüten}}.

* a Celtic root found in {{cog|sco|bogill||goblin, bugbear}} and obsolete {{cog|cy|bwg||ghost, hobgoblin}}; compare Welsh {{m|cy|bwgwl||threat, fear}} and {{cog|mga|bocanách||supernatural being}}.

bubble.text: Partly {{onom|en|title=imitative}}, also influenced by {{m|en|burble}}. Compare {{cog|dum|bobbe||bubble}} > {{cog|nl|bubbel||bubble}}, {{cog|nds|bubbel||bubble}}, {{cog|da|boble||bubble}}, {{cog|sv|bubbla||bubble}}. The word was first used in its economic sense in association with the collapse of the {{w|South Sea Company}} in 1720, based on the metaphor of an inflated soap bubble bursting.

Perhaps of {{der|en|cel|-}} origin, from a hypotheti

breakfast.text: From {{inh|en|enm|brekefast}}, {{m|enm|brekefaste}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|break|fast}} {{gloss|''literally'', "to end the nightly fast"}}, likely a variant of {{inh|en|ang|fæstenbryċe}}, {{gloss|''literally'', "fast-breach"}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|breekvasten|t=breakfast}}.

bulk.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰelǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|bulk}}, {{m|enm|bolke|t=a heap, cargo, hold; heap; bulge}}, borrowed from {{der|en|non|búlki|t=the freight or the cargo of a ship}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bulkô|t=beam, pile, heap}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰelǵ-|t=beam, pile, prop}}. Compare {{cog|is|búlkast|t=to be bulky}}, {{cog|sv|-}} dialectal {{m|sv|bulk|t=a bunch}}, {{cog|da|bulk|t=bump, knob}}

buck.text:
{{etymon|en|id=he-goat|:inh|enm:bukke<id:he-goat>|tree=1|text=1}} {{doublet|en|puck|t1=billy goat}}.

Currency-related senses hail from [[American English]], a {{clipping|en|buckskin|nocap=1}} as a unit of trade among [[Native American|Native Americans]] and [[Europeans]] in frontier days (attested from 1748).

The idea of rigidly standing implements is instilled by {{sl|en|nl|bok|t=sawhorse|notex

From {{suffix|en|cabin|et}}, influenced by {{der|en|fr|cabinet}}.
In sense of “a government group”, compare {{m|en|salon}}, also named for a room used to gather.

{{root|en|ine-pro|*kh₂em-}}
From {{der|en|fr|campagne}}, from {{der|en|it|campagna||field, military operation}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|campānia||open country, battlefield}}, from {{der|en|la|campus||field}}. {{doublet|en|campania|campagna|champagne}}.

canvas.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|canevas}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|canevas}} (compare {{cog|fro|chanevas}}, {{m|fro|chenevas}}) from a root derived from {{der|en|la|cannabis}}, from {{der|en|grc|κάνναβις}}. {{ety|en|:inh|enm:candle|tree=1}}

{{root|en|ine-pro|*kh₂em-}}

The most common modern use is an ellipsis of ''century of years''.

{{ety|en|id=stop|:inh|enm:cesen<ety:bor<frm:cesser<ety:der<la:cessō>>>>|tree=1}}

civil.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|cyvyl}}, {{m|enm|civil}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|civil}}, from {{der|en|la|cīvīlis|t=relating to a citizen}}, from {{m|la|cīvis|t=citizen}} ultimately from proto-Indo-European {{m|ine-pro|*ḱey-}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|hīwen|t=household}}, {{m|ang|hīrǣden|t=family}}. More at {{l|en|hind#Etymology 3|hind}}; {{l|en|hird}}.

{{sense|polite}} Compare typologically {{m|en|urbane}

clause.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|clause}}, {{m|enm|claus}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|clause}}, from {{der|en|la-med|clausa}} (Latin diminutive {{m|la|clausula||close, end; a clause, close of a period}}), from {{der|en|la|clausus}}, past participle of {{m|la|claudere||to shut, close}}. See {{m|en|close}}, its doublet.
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-}}

classic.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:classique}}
From {{bor|en|fr|classique|}}, from {{der|en|la|classicus|classic(us)|t=relating to the classes of Roman citizenry, especially the highest}}, from {{m|la|classis}}. {{surf|+suf|en|class|ic}}. {{piecewise doublet|en|classy}}.

circuit.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|circuit}}, from {{der|en|fro|circuit}}, from {{der|en|la|circuitus||a going round}}, from {{m|la|circuire||go round}}, from {{m|la|circum||around}} + {{m|la|ire}}.

{{en-noun}}

# The [[act]] of [[moving]] or [[revolving]] around, or as in a [[circle]] or [[orbit]]; a [[revolution]]
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1904|title=Popular Science Monthly Volume 64|page=33
|passage

chop.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|choppen}}, {{m|enm|chappen|t=to chop}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin, possibly {{onom|enm|nocat=1|nocap=1}} (cf. {{ncog|sv|tjoff}}), or a variant of {{m|en|chap|t=to become cracked}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|chap|t=to chop}}. Compare also {{cog|stq|kappe}}, {{m|stq|kapje|t=to hack; chop; lop off}}, {{cog|nl|kappen|t=to chop, cut, hew}}, {{cog|nds-de|kappen|t=to cut off; clip}}, {

choice.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵews-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|chois}}, from {{der|en|fro|chois|t=choice}}, from {{m|fro|choisir|t=to choose, perceive}}, possibly via assumed {{der|en|la-vul|*causīre|t=to choose}}, from {{der|en|got|𐌺𐌰𐌿𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽|t=to make a choice, taste, test, choose}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kauzijaną}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*keusaną|t=to choose}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵews-|t=to choose}}. Akin to {{cog

chronic.text:
{{etymon|en|:from|chronical<ety:der<fro:cronike<ety:inh<la:chronicus>>>>|tree=+}}

From {{m|en|chronical}}, from {{der|en|fro|cronike}}, from {{der|en|la|chronicus}}, from {{der|en|grc|χρονικός||of time}}, from {{m|grc|χρόνος||time}}. {{surf|en|chron-|-ic}}.

classical.text:
{{ety|en|:af|classic|-al<id:adjectival suffix>|:afeq|class|-ical|:afeq|class|-ic|-al<id:adjectival suffix>}}
See ''[[classic#Etymology|classic § Etymology]]'' for history. {{surf|en|class|-ical}} or {{suffix|en|classic|al}} or {{suffix|en|class|-ic|-al}}

cinema.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:cinéma|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|fr|cinéma}}, clipping of {{m|fr|cinématographe}} (term coined by the {{w|Lumière brothers}} in the 1890s), from {{der|en|grc|κίνημα|t=movement}} + {{m|grc|γράφω|t=write, record}}. Compare {{cog|de|Kino|t=cinema}}, ultimately from the same Greek source.

clarify.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kelh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|clarifien}}, from {{der|en|fro|clarifiier}}, from {{der|en|la|clarifico|clārificō, clārificāre}}; {{m|la|clārus|t=clear}} + {{m|la|facio|faciō, facere|t=make}}. Semantically {{suf|en|clear|ify}}.

clock.text:
{{ety|en|id=chronometer|:inh|enm:clokke|tree=1}}
First use appears c. 1370. From {{inh|en|enm|clokke}}, {{m|enm|clok}}, {{m|enm|cloke||clock}}, from {{der|en|dum|clocke||bell, clock}}, from {{der|en|odt||*klokka}}, from {{der|en|la-med|clocca||bell, clock, cloak}}, probably of {{der|en|cel|-}} origin, from {{der|en|cel-pro|*klokkos||bell}} (compare {{cog|cy|cloch||bell}}, {{cog|sga|cloc||bell, clo

[[Image:Silver tetradrachm MET DP139641.jpg|thumb|right|An Ancient Greek coin, circa 315–308 BC, made of silver]]
[[File:England, Anne, 1702-1714 - Guinea - 1969.204 - Cleveland Museum of Art.tif|thumb|An English coin, 1703, made of gold]]

From {{inh|en|enm|coyn}}, from {{der|en|fro|coigne||wedge, cornerstone, die for stamping}}, from {{der|en|la|cuneus|

cloth.text: From {{inh|en|enm|cloth}}, {{m|enm|clath}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clāþ|t=cloth, clothes, covering, sail}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*klaiþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*klaiþą|t=garment}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gleyt-|t=to cling to, cleave, stick}} (compare {{cog|sq|ngjit|t=to stick, attach, glue}}), a form of {{m|ine-pro|*gleh₁y-|t=to smear; to stick}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|clath|t=cloth}}, {{cog

cognitive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵneh₃-}}
From {{der|en|la-med|cognitīvus}}, from {{der|en|la|cognitus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|cognōscō|t=to get to know}} + {{m|la|-īvus|pos=adjective suffix}}.

club.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:clubbe}}
{{inh+|en|enm|clubbe}}, from {{der|en|non|klubba}}, {{m|non|klumba||cudgel}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*klumpô||clip, clasp; clump, lump; log, block}}. Doublets of {{cog|en|clump}}, {{m|en|cloud}}, {{cog|la|globus}}, {{m|la|glomus}}; and perhaps related to {{cog|gml|kolve||bulb}}, {{cog|de|Kolben||butt, bulb, club}}.

clothes.text: From {{inh|en|enm|clothes}}, {{m|enm|cloþes|pos=plural of {{m|enm|cloth}}, {{m|enm|cloþ|t=cloth, garment}}}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clāþas|t=clothes|pos=plural of {{m|ang|clāþ|t=cloth}}}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|cloth|es<id:plural>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|clathes}}, {{m|sco|claes|t=clothes}}, {{cog|nl|klederen}}, {{m|nl|kleren|t=clothes}}, {{cog|de|Kleider|t=clothes}}, {{cog|da|klæder|t=clothes}}, {

clue.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*glew-}}
Variant of {{m|en|clew|t=a ball of thread or yarn}}, from {{inh|en|enm|clew}}, {{m|enm|clewe}}, {{m|enm|clowe}}, {{m|enm|clue}}, {{m|enm|clwe}}, {{m|enm|clyw}}, {{m|enm|clywe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clēowen}}, {{m|ang|clīewen}}, {{m|ang|clīowen}}, {{m|ang|clīwen}}, {{m|ang|clȳwe}}, {{m|ang|clȳwen|t=ball, sphere; skein}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kliuwīn|t=ball, clump}}, from

closet.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|closet}}, from {{der|en|fro|closet}}, from {{suffix|fro|clos|t1=[[private]] [[space]]|-et|pos2={{lg|diminutive}} suffix|nocat=1}}, from {{der|en|la|clausum}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|close|et}}, but generally applied in French solely to small open-air enclosures.<ref>''Oxford English Dictionary''. "closet, ''n.''"</ref>
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-}}

clothing.text: From {{inh|en|enm|clothing}}, {{m|enm|clathing}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*clāþung}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*klaiþungu|t=clothing}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|clothe|ing<id:gerund noun>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|clathing}}, {{m|sco|claithing|t=clothing}}, {{cog|stq|Klodenge|t=clothing}}, {{cog|fy|klaaiïng|t=clothing}}, {{cog|nl|kleding|t=clothing}}, {{cog|de|Kleidung|t=clothing}}, {{cog|da|klædning|t=cloth

click.text:
{{ety|en|id=sharp sound}}
{{onom|en|title=Imitative}} of the "click" sound; first recorded in the 1500s. Compare {{cog|stq|klikke||to click}}, {{cog|dum|clicken}} (Modern Dutch: {{m|nl|klikken||to click}}), Old High German {{m|goh|klecchen}} (Modern German: {{m|de|klecken}}, {{m|de|klicken||to click}}), Danish {{m|da|klikke||to click}}, Swedish {{m|sv|klicka||to click}}, Norwegian {{m|no|klikke||t

client.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱlew-|*ḱley-|id2=incline}}
From {{inh|en|enm|client}}, from {{der|en|xno|clyent}}, {{der|en|fro|client}}, from {{der|en|la|cliēns}}, akin to {{m|la|clinare|t=to lean}}.

clip.text:
{{etymon|en|id=fasten|:inh|enm:clippen<ety:inh<ang:clyppan<t:to hug, embrace, cherish, clasp>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|clippen}}, {{m|enm|cleppen}}, {{m|enm|cluppen|clüppen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|clyppan|t=to hug, embrace, cherish, clasp}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*klumpijaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*glemb-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*glembʰ-|t=lump, clump, clod, clamp}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|kleppa}}, {{m

clinic.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:clinique|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|fr|clinique}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|clīnicus||a bed-ridden person, one baptized on a sick-bed, a physician}}, from {{der|en|grc|κλῑνικός||pertaining to a bed}}, from {{m|grc|κλῑ́νη||bed}}, from {{m|grc|κλῑ́νω||to lean, incline}}.

coincide.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱh₂d-}}
From {{bor|en|fr|coïncider}}, from {{der|en|la-med|coincido|coincidere}}, from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|incido|incidere}}, from {{m|la|in-||into, to}} + {{m|la|cado|cadere|to fall, fall down, drop}}.

collection.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|colleccioun}}, {{m|enm|collection}}, from {{der|en|fro|collection}}, from {{der|en|la|collēctiō|collēctiō, collēctiōnem}}, from {{m|la|collēctus}}, from {{m|la|colligō||collect together}}, composed of {{prefix|la|con|legō|gloss2=bring together, gather, collect|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-||to gather, collect}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en

combat.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:combat|tree=+}}
16th century, {{bor+|en|frm|combat|nocap=1}}, deverbal from {{der|en|fro|combatre}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*combattere}}, from {{der|en|la|com-||with}} + {{m|la|battuere||to beat, strike}}.

combine.text:
{{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}}
From {{inh|en|enm|combynyn}}, from {{der|en|frm|combiner}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|combīnō|combīnāre|t=unite, yoke together}}, from {{der|en|la|con-|t=together}} + {{m|la|[[binus|bīnī]]|t=two by two}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=1824744922}}</ref>

commence.text: From {{inh|en|enm|commencen}}, {{m|enm|comencen}} (also as contracted {{m|enm|comsen}}, {{m|enm|cumsen}}), from {{der|en|xno|comencier|comencer}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*cominitiāre}}, formed from {{der|en|la|com-}} + {{m|la|initiō}} (whence English {{l|en|initiate}}).

commercial.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:commercial|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|fr|commercial||of, or pertaining to commerce}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|commercialis}}, from {{der|en|la|commercium}}. {{surf|en|commerce|-ial}}.

commit.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:committen<id:commit>|id=dedicate}}
{{inh+|en|enm|committen}}, itself borrowed from {{der|en|la|committō||to bring together, join, compare, commit (a wrong), incur, give in charge, etc.}}, from {{m|la|com-||together}} + {{m|la|mittō||to [[send]]}}. See {{m|en|mission}}.

committee.text:
{{ety|en|:af|commit|-ee<id:object of action>}}
From {{suffix|en|commit|ee}}, or else revival of {{der|en|xno|commite}}, past participle of {{m|fro|commettre||to commit}}, from {{der|en|la|committere}}, from {{m|la|con-||with}} + {{m|la|mittere||to send}}.  The OED3 prefers the first etymology.

communicate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}}
{{af|en||lang1=la|alt1=commūnicāt-|pos1=[[past participial]] {{lg|stem}} of {{m|la|commūnicō|t=share, impart; make common}}|-ate|id2=verb|pos2=verb-forming suffix|type=adap}}, from {{af|la|commūnis|-icō|t1=common|nocat=1}}. Compare {{cog|fr|communiquer}} and its older (and now obsolete) {{w|English}} [[cognate]] from {{w|Middle French}}, {{m|en|communique}}.<ref>

communication.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:comunicacioun}}
{{inh+|en|enm|comunicacioun}}, {{m|enm|communicacion|t=discussion, association}}, from {{der|en|fro|communicacion}}, from {{der|en|la|commūnicātiōnem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|commūnicātiō||imparting, communicating}}, from {{m|la|commūnicō||to share, to impart}}. Morphologically {{suf|en|communicate|ion}}.

compare.text: From {{inh|en|enm|comparen}}, from {{der|en|fro|comparer}}, from {{der|en|la|comparare||to prepare, procure}}, from {{m|la|compar||like or equal to another}}, from {{m|la|com-}} + {{m|la|par||equal}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|metan}} (“to compare,” also “to measure”).

compatible.text: {{inh+|en|enm|compatible}}, fron {{der|en|xno|compatible}}, from {{der|en|la-med|compatibilis||in ''compatibile beneficium'', a benefice which could be held together with another one}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|compator||to suffer with}}, from {{m|la|com-||together}} + {{m|la|pati||to suffer}}; see [[passion]].

compensate.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|compēnsātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|compensō||to weight together one thing against another, balance, make good}}, {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} for more.

compensation.text: From {{inh|en|enm|compensacioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|compensacion}}, from {{der|en|la|compensātiōnem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|compensātiō}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|compensate|ion}}.

competition.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|compétition}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|competitio|competītiō, competītiōnem}}, from {{der|en|la|competō}}, from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|petō}}. {{surf|en|compete|-ition}}.

component.text: {{bor+|en|la|componens|compōnēns, compōnēntis}}, present participle of {{m|la|compōnō||assemble, put together}}.

compose.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tḱey-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|composen}}, from {{der|en|fro|composer||to compose, compound, adjust, settle}}, from {{m|fro|com-}} + {{m|fro|poser}}, as an adaptation of {{der|en|la|componere||to put together, compose}}, from {{m|la|com-||together}} + {{m|la|ponere||to put, place}}.

comprise.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰed-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|comprisen}}, from {{der|en|fro|compris}}, past participle of {{m|fro|comprendre}}, from {{der|en|la|comprehendere}}, contr. {{m|la|comprendere}}, past participle {{m|la|comprehensus||to comprehend}}; see {{m|en|comprehend}}. Compare {{m|en|apprise}}, {{m|en|reprise}}, {{m|en|surprise}}.

compromise.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}}
From {{der|en|frm|compromis}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}}, {{der|en|la-lat|compromissum||a compromise, originally a mutual promise to refer to arbitration}}, prop. neuter of {{uder|en|la|compromissus}}, past participle of {{m|la|compromittere||to make a mutual promise to abide by the decision of an arbiter}}, from {{m|la|com-||together}} + {{m|la|promittere||to pro

concede.text: From {{inh|en|enm|}}, from {{der|en|fro|conceder}}, from {{der|en|la|concēdō||give way, yield}}, from {{m|la|con-||wholly}} + {{m|la|cēdō||to yield, give way, to go, grant}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ked-||to go, yield}}.

conceive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}}
From {{inh|en|enm|conceyven}}, from {{der|en|fro|concevoir}}, {{m|fro|conceveir}}, from {{der|en|la|concipio|concipiō, concipere|to devise, to conceive}}.

concentrate.text: (early 17th century) From a [[Romance language]], see {{cog|fr|concentrer}}, {{cog|it|concentrare|concentràre}}, {{cog|es|concentrar}}; alternatively from {{bor|en|la-med|-}}/{{der|en|la-new|concentrō}} + {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}. Compare also earlier {{doublet|en|concentre|notext=1}} and {{cog|de|konzentrieren}}. {{surf|en|con-|center|-ate|pos2=centr- in compounds|id3=verb

concept.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:concept<ety:der<la:conceptus<id:noun>>>|tree=1}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|concept|}}, from {{der|en|la|conceptus||a thought, purpose, also a conceiving, etc.}}, from {{m|la|concipiō||to take in, conceive}}. {{doublet|en|conceit|concetto}}. See [[conceive]].

concern.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*krey-}}
{{bor+|en|frm|concerner}}, from {{der|en|la-med|concerno|concernō, concernere|I distinguish, have respect to}}, from {{der|en|la|concernō||to mix, sift, or mingle together, as in a sieve}}, combined form of {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|cernō||distinguish}}.

conclude.text: From {{inh|en|enm|concluden}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|conclūdō|conclūdere|t=to shut up, close, end}}.

conclusion.text: From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|conclusion}}, from {{der|en|la|conclūsiō}}, from the past participle stem of {{m|la|conclūdō|conclūdere|to conclude}}, from {{affix|la|con-|claudō|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-|*kleh₂u-|key, hook, nail}}. {{surf|en|conclude|-sion}}.

concrete.text: {{bor+|en|la|concrētus}}, past participle of {{m|la|concrescō}} (to curdle) from {{m|la|con-}} (with, together) + {{m|la|crescō}} (to grow, rise).

condemn.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:condempnen|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|condempnen}}, from {{der|en|fro|condamner}}, from {{der|en|la|condemnāre||to sentence, condemn, blame}}, from {{m|la|com-}} + {{m|la|damnāre||to harm, condemn, damn}}, from {{m|la|damnum||damage, injury, loss}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|fordemen}} (from {{cog|ang|fordeman||condemn, sentence, doom}} > Modern English {{m|en|fordeem}}.

condition.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}}
From {{der|en|enm|condicioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|condicion}} (French {{m|fr|condition}}), from {{der|en|la|condicio}}. An unetymological change in spelling due to a confusion with {{m|la|conditio}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hād||state, condition}}.

conduct.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}}
From {{der|en|la-lat|conductus|t=defense, escort}}, from {{der|en|la|conductus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|condūcō|t=bring together}}; see also {{m|en|conduce}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|þēaw}}. {{doublet|en|conduit}}.

confer.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}}
From Early Modern English {{m|en|conferre}}, from {{uder|en|frm|conférer}}, from {{uder|en|fro|conferer}}, from {{uder|en|la|cōnferō}}. Compare {{cog|nl|confereren}}, {{cog|de|konferieren}}, {{cog|da|konferere}}, {{cog|sv|konferera}}. {{doublet|en|collate}}. See also [[infer]], [[relate]] and [[refer]], [[delate]] and [[defer]], as well as [[prelate]] and [[prefer]] amon

confident.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeydʰ-}}
From {{der|en|frm|confident}}, from {{der|en|la|confidens||confident, i.e. self-confident, in a good or bad sense, bold, daring, audacious, impudent}}, present participle of {{m|la|confidere||to trust fully, confide}}. See {{m|en|confide}}.

confirm.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰer-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|confirmen}}, {{m|enm|confermen}}, from {{der|en|fro|confermer}}, from {{der|en|la|confirmo|cōnfirmāre|to make firm, strengthen, establish}}, from {{m|la|con-||together}} + {{m|la|firmo|firmāre|to make firm}}, from {{m|la|firmus||firm}}.

conflict.text: From {{der|en|la|cōnflīctus}}, from {{pre|la|com-|flīctus|nocat=1}}, past participle of {{m|la|conflīgō||to strike together}}, from {{pre|la|com-|flīgō|t2=strike|nocat=1}} (whence {{af|en|con-}}).

conform.text: From {{inh|en|enm|conformen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|-}} and {{der|en|xno|conformer}}, from {{der|en|la|conformāre||to mould, to shape after}}.

congress.text:
From {{der|en|la|congressum|alt=congress(um)}}, the past participle of {{m|la|congredior||to go, come together}}, itself from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|gradior||to go, step}}. The verb is from the noun.

Compare typologically {{m|en|coven}}, {{m|en|convent}}, {{m|en|convention}}, omitting several steps, from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|veniō}}, {{m+|ru|сход}}, {{m|ru|схо́дка}}, akin to {{m|ru|сходи́ться}}

conscious.text: First use appears c. 1573 in the sense of "aware of wrongdoing".[https://web.archive.org/web/20220714064352/https://www.lexico.com/definition/conscious] From {{bor|en|la|cōnscius||conscious, conscious of guilt}}, itself from {{m|la|con-}} (a form of {{m|la|com-|t=together}}) + {{m|la|scio|scīre|t=to know}} + {{m|la|-us}}.

consensus.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sent-|id=perceive}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|cōnsēnsus||agreement, accordance, unanimity}}, from {{m|la|cōnsentiō||feel together; agree}}; see {{m|en|consent}}.

consequence.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{inh|en|enm|consequence}}, from {{der|en|fro|consequence}},<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> from {{der|en|la|consequentia}}. While analysable as {{pre|en|con|sequence}}, its adjective form has a different origin.

consequent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|conséquent}},<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> from {{der|en|la|consequens|consequens, consequentem}}, present participle of {{m|la|consequi||to follow}}, from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|sequi||to follow}}. Compare {{cog|fr|conséquent}}.

constant.text: From {{inh|en|enm|constant}}, from {{uder|en|fro|constant}}, from {{uder|en|la|constantem}}, accusative of {{m|la|constans}}, from {{m|la|consto|cōnstāre|to stand firm}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|singal}}.

constitute.text: From {{inh|en|enm|constituten}}, from {{der|en|la|cōnstitūtum}}, neuter of {{m|la|cōnstitūtus}}, past participle of {{der|en|la|cōnstituō|t=to put in place; set up; establish}}, from {{m|la|con-||with}} + {{m|la|statuō||to put up; establish}}.

constitution.text:
{{PIE word|en|ḱóm}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|constitucioun}}, {{m|enm|constitucion|t=edict, law, ordinance, regulation, rule, statute; body of laws or rules, or customs; body of fundamental principles; principle or rule (of science); creation}}<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=constitūciǒun|pos=n|id=MED9433}}</ref> from {{der|en|fro|constitucion}} (modern {{cog|fr|constitution}}), a [[

parts: t2=to draw, bind or tie tight
constrain.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:constreinen<ety:bor<fro:constreindre<ety:der<la:cōnstringō>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|constreinen}}, from {{der|en|fro|constreindre}}, from {{der|en|la|cōnstringō}}, from {{prefix|la|cōn|stringō|t1=with, together|t2=to draw, bind or tie tight|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*streyg-||to stroke, to shear, stiff}}.

consultant.text: From {{der|en|fr|consultant}}, present participle of {{m|fr|consulter}}, from {{der|en|la|consulto|cōnsultāre|t=to deliberate, consult}}, frequentative of {{m|la|consulo|cōnsulere|t=to consult, deliberate, consider, reflect upon, ask advice}}, from {{m|la|com-|t=together}} + {{m|la|-sulere}}, of uncertain origin.

consumption.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:consumpcioun<ety:bor<fro:consumpcion<ety:der<la:cōnsūmptiō>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{pre|en|con-}} {{der|en|la|sūmptus}} {{suf|en||-ion}}, from {{inh|en|enm|consumpcioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|consumpcion}}, from {{der|en|la|cōnsūmptiō}}, from {{suf|la|cōnsūmō|tiō|nocat=1}}, from {{af|la|con-|gloss1=with, together|sūmō|gloss2=take; consume|nocat=1}}. Equivalent to {{compound|en|consum

contact.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}}
From {{der|en|la|contactus}}, from {{m|la|contingō|t=to touch on all sides}}, from {{m|la|tangō|t=to touch}}. Used in English since the 17th century.

contemporary.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|la-med:contemporārius}}
From {{bor|en|la-med|contemporārius}}, from {{der|en|la|con-|t=with, together}} + {{m|la|temporārius}}, an adjective derived from {{m|la|tempus|t=time}}.

contend.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}}
From {{inh|en|enm|contenden}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|contendre}}, from {{der|en|la|contendere||to stretch out, extend, strive after, contend}}, from {{m|la|com-||together}} + {{m|la|tendere||to stretch}}; see {{m|en|tend}}, and compare {{m|en|attend}}, {{m|en|extend}}, {{m|en|intend}}, {{m|en|subtend}}.

contrast.text: From {{bor|en|fr|contraster}}, from {{der|en|la|contrāstō|contrāstāre|to resist", "to withstand}}, from {{m|la|contrā||against}} + {{m|la|stō|stō, stāre|to stand}}.

contribute.text:
{{PIE word|en|tréyes}}
From {{der|en|la|contribūtus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|contribuō||to bring together; to unite}}, from {{prefix|la|con|tribuō|t1=together|t2=to bestow|nocat=1}}, from {{m|la|tribus||tribe}}, derived from {{m|la|trēs||three}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*trēs}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*tréyes}}.

controversy.text:
{{etymon|en|id=debate|:inh|enm:controversie<ety:bor<fro:controversie<ety:inh<la:contrōversia>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|controversie}}, from {{der|en|fro|controversie}}, from {{der|en|la|contrōversia||debate, contention, controversy}}, from {{m|la|contrōversus||turned in an opposite direction}}.

convene.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|convenir}}, from {{der|en|la|convenio|convenio, convenire|come together}}, from {{affix|la|con-|gloss1=with, together|veniō|gloss2=come|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʷm̥yéti}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*gʷem-}}.

convenient.text: From {{inh|en|enm|convenient}}, from {{der|en|la|conveniēns||fit, suitable, convenient}}, present participle of {{m|la|convenio|conveniō, convinīre|t=to come together, suit}}; see {{m|en|convene}} and compare {{m|en|covenant}}.

conversation.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|conversacioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|conversacion}} and its etymon, {{der|en|la|conversātiōnem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|conversātiō|t=conversation}}, from {{m|la|conversor|t=abide, keep company with}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|wordlaþu}}. {{dbt|en|conversazione}}.
Morphologically {{suffix|en|converse|ation}}.

convey.text: From {{inh|en|enm|conveien}}, from {{der|en|fro|conveier}} ({{cog|fr|convoyer}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*convio}}, from Classical {{der|en|la|via||way}}. Compare {{m|en|convoy}}.

convict.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyk-|id=contain}}
From {{inh|en|enm|convicten}}, from {{der|en|xno|convicter}}, from {{der|en|la|convictus}}, the past participle of {{m|la|convincō||to convict}}. {{doublet|en|convince}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|forwyrċan||to convict, condemn}}.

conviction.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyk-|id=contain}}
From late {{inh|en|enm|conviction}}, from {{der|en|xno|conviction}}, from {{der|en|la|convictiō}}, from {{m|la|convictus}}, the past participle of {{m|la|convincō||to convict}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|convict|ion}}.

convince.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyk-|id=contain}}
{{bor+|en|la|convincō|t=to refute, prove}}, from {{m|la|con-}} + {{m|la|vincō|t=to conquer, vanquish}}. {{doublet|en|convict}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|oferreċċan}}.

cooking.text: From {{suffix|en|cook|ing}}. The noun and adjective follow from the verb. The use of the word ''cooking'' to describe cheap bitter was popularized by the title character of the BBC sitcom ''Oh No, It’s Selwyn Froggitt'' (1974-1978). It refers to [[cooking sherry]], a kind of [[sherry]] used in cooking but not suitable for drinking on its own.

cooperate.text: Originated 1595–1605 from {{der|en|la-lat|cooperātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la-lat|cooperor||to work with}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} for more. Equivalent to {{af|en|co-|operate}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|efnwyrċan}}.

coordinate.text:
From {{bor|en|la-med|coōrdinātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la-med|coōrdinō||arrange together}}, from {{af|la|co-|ōrdinō|nocat=1}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|co|ordinate}}. See {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}} for more. See also [[ordain]] and [[ordinate]].

cop.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}}
{{unc|en}}. Perhaps from {{inh|en|enm|*coppen}}, {{m|enm|*copen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|copian|t=to plunder; pillage; steal}}; or possibly from {{der|en|frm|caper|t=to capture}}, from {{der|en|la|capiō|t=to seize, grasp}}; or possibly from {{der|en|nl|kapen|t=to seize, hijack}}, from {{der|en|ofs|kāpia|t=to buy}}, whence {{cog|fy|keapje}}, {{cog|stq|koopje}}, {{cog|

core.text:
{{ety|en|id=central part|:inh|enm:core}}
From {{inh|en|enm|core}}, {{m|enm|kore}}, {{m|enm|coor|t=apple-core, pith}}, of {{unc|en|title=obscure and uncertain|nocap=1}} origin. Possibly of native English origin, from {{inh|en|ang|*cor}}, related to {{cog|ang|*coruc}}, {{m|ang|*corc|pos=diminutive}} (> {{cog|enm|cork}}, {{m|enm|crok|t=core of an apple or other fruit, heart of an onion}}) and {{nonco

corporate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*krep-}}
The {{glossary|adjective}} is {{etydate|1429|nocap=1}}, the {{glossary|noun}} in 1849; from {{inh|en|enm|corporat|corporat(e)|t=({{ng|if a true adjective}}) corporeal, physical, embodied; ({{ng|participle/participial adjective}}) incorporated; corporated, constituted as a legal corporation|pos=used as the past participle of {{m|enm|corporaten}}}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entr

correspond.text: From {{der|en|frm|correspondre|}}, from {{der|en|la|com-||with}} + {{m|la|respondeo||to match, to answer to}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|co-|respond}}.

cottage.text: Late {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|xno|cotage}} and {{der|en|la-med|cotagium}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor|cot}}, {{m|fro|cote|t=cottage, hut}} + {{m|fro|-age|t=surrounding property}}, from {{der|en|non|kot}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kutą}}, {{m|gem-pro|*kuta-|t=shed}}, probably of non-Indo-European origin, possibly borrowed from {{der|en|fiu-pro|-}}/{{der|en|urj-pro|*kota|t=hut, tent}}, probably akin

cough.text: From {{inh|en|enm|coughen}}, {{m|enm|coghen|t=to cough; to vomit}}{{nb...|coghe, couhen, couwhen, couwe, couwen, couȝen, couȝhen, couȝtthe, couȝwen, coȝen, cowen, cowff, cowghen, cowhen, cowȝen, koghe, kouȝen, kowen|otherforms=1}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*cohhian}} (compare {{cog|ang|cohhetan|t=to bluster; to riot; to cough (?)}}), from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*kuh-|t=to cough}}, ultimately of {{glossary|onom

council.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kelh₁-}}
{{inh+|en|enm|counseil||meeting, conference, commune}}, from {{der|en|fro|conseil||advice, deliberation, thought}}, from  {{der|en|la|cōnsilium||plan, intention, design, purpose}}, from {{m|la|cōnsulō||consult, seek counsel from, take counsel from, deliberate, reflect}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*selh₁-||take, grab}}.

counterpart.text: From {{inh|en|enm|conterpart}}, {{m|enm|countre parte|t=duplicate of a legal document}}, equivalent to {{com|en|counter-|part}}. Compare {{cog|fro|contrepartie}}, itself from {{m|fro|contre||facing, opposite}} (from {{cog|la|contra||against}}) + {{m|fro|partie||copy of a person or thing}} (originally past participle of {{m|la|partīre||to divide}}).

coverage.text:
{{etymon|en|id=reporting|:af|cover<id:place upon>|-age<id:collection>|tree=1}}
From {{af|en|cover|-age}}. {{etydate|1912}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|id=6778557850|pos=n}}</ref> Compare {{cog|enm|coverage|t=a charge for having or stall or booth at a fair}}.

crash.text: From {{inh|en|enm|crasshen}}, {{m|enm|crasschen|}}, {{m|enm|craschen||to break into pieces}}, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from a variant of earlier {{m|enm|*crasken}}, from {{suffix|enm|crasen|t1=to break|k|pos2=formative suffix|nocat=1}}; or from earlier {{m|enm|*craskien}}, {{m|enm|*craksien}}, a variant of {{m|enm|craken||to crack, break open}} (for form development compare {{m|en|break}}, {{m

crawl.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gerbʰ-}}
From {{der|en|enm|crawlen}}, {{m|enm|crewlen}}, {{m|enm|creulen}}, {{m|enm|crallen}}, {{m|enm|*cravelen}}, from {{der|en|non|krafla}} (compare {{cog|da|kravle|t=to crawl, creep}}, {{cog|sv|kravla}}, {{m|sv|kräla|t=to creep, crawl}}), from {{der|en|gem-pro|*krabblōną|*krablōną}} (compare {{cog|stq|krabbelje}}, {{cog|nl|krabbelen}}, {{cog|nds-de|krabbeln}}, {{cog|de|krabb

credit.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-|*dʰeh₁-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|crédit||belief, trust}}, from {{der|en|la|crēditum||a loan, credit}}, neuter of {{m|la|crēditus}}, past participle of {{m|la|crēdere||to believe}}. The verb is from the noun. {{doublet|en|shraddha}}, {{m|en|creed}}.

crisis.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*krey-}}
From {{bor|en|la|crisis}}, from {{der|en|grc|κρίσις|t=a separating, power of distinguishing, decision, choice, election, judgment, dispute}}, from {{m|grc|κρίνω|t=pick out, choose, decide, judge}}.

criterion.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*krey-}}
From {{bor|en|la-new|criterion}}, from {{der|en|grc|κριτήριον|t=a test, a means of judging}}, from {{m|grc|κριτής|t=judge}}, from {{m|grc|κρίνω|t=to judge}}; see ''[[critic]]''.

crush.text:
From {{der|en|enm|cruschen|t=to crush, smash, squeeze, squash}}, from {{der|en|fro|croissir|t=to crush}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|*crusciō|t=to crush}}, from {{der|en|frk|*krustijan|t=to crush, squeeze, squash}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kreustaną|t=to crush, grind, strike, smash}}. 

Cognate with {{cog|gml|tôkrosten|t=to crush, shatter}}, {{cog|sv|krysta|t=to squeeze}}, {{cog|da|kryste|t=to squash}},

crystal.text: From {{inh|en|enm|crystal}}, {{m|enm|cristal}}, {{m|enm|criȝstall}}, representing a merger of {{inh|en|ang|cristalla}} (from Latin {{m|la|crystallus}}) and {{der|en|xno|cristall}}, {{der|en|fro|cristal}} (from Latin {{m|la|crystallum}}). The Latin is derived from {{der|en|grc|κρύσταλλος||clear ice}}, from {{m|grc|κρύος||frost}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*krews-||hard, hard outer surface, crust}}.

culture.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|frm:culture<ety:der<la:cultūra>>|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|frm|culture|t=cultivation; culture}}, from {{der|en|la|cultūra|t=cultivation; culture}}, from {{m|la|cultus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|colō|t=till, cultivate, to grow, worship}} (related to {{m|la|colōnus}} and {{m|la|colōnia}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷel-|t=to move; to turn (around)}}.

cupboard.text: Inherited from {{inh|en|enm|cuppeborde}}, {{m|enm|cupbord}}. {{surf|en|cup|board}}. Phonetic variants show that the /p/ in the original forms had assimilated to the present-day /b/ by the 16th century; the etymological spelling has, however, dominated from the 18th century.

curb.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker- (turn)}}
From {{der|en|frm|courbe||curve, curved object}}, from {{der|en|la|curvus||bent, crooked, curved}}. {{doublet|en|curve}}.

curl.text:
From {{metathesis|en}} of {{der|en|enm|crulle|t=curled, curly}}, of uncertain origin but probably from an unrecorded Old English word or from {{der|en|dum|crul}}, {{m|dum|crulle|t=curl}}, ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kruzlǭ|t=bent or crooked object, curl}}, connected to {{m|gem-pro|*krūsą|t=curl}}, of {{unk|en|title=unknown}} origin.<ref>{{R:nl:Etymologiebank|kroezen}}</ref>

Cognate with {{c

current.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:curraunt<ety:bor<fro:corant<alt:curant>>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|curraunt}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|corant|curant}} ({{cog|fr|courant}}), present participle of {{m|fro|courre|t=to run}}, from {{der|en|la|currō|currere|t=to run}} (present participle {{m|la|currens}}). {{doublet|en|courant}}.

customer.text: From {{inh|en|enm|custumer}}, from {{der|en|fro|coustumier}}, {{m|fro|costumier}} (compare modern French {{m|fr|coutumier}}), from {{der|en|la-med|custumarius||a toll-gatherer, tax-collector|pos=noun}}, from {{m|la|custumarius||pertaining to custom or customs|pos=adjective}}, from {{m|la|custuma||custom, tax}}. More at {{m|en|custom}}. {{surf|en|custom|-er|id2=occupation}}.

daily.text: From {{inh|en|enm|dayly}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dæġlīċ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dagalīk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dagalīkaz|t=daily}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|day|ly|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|dayly}}, {{m|sco|daly|t=daily}}, {{cog|nds-de|dagelk}}, {{m|nds-de|dagelik|t=daily}}, {{cog|nl|dagelijks|t=daily}}, {{cog|de|täglich|t=daily}}, {{cog|da|daglig|t=daily}}, {{cog|sv|daglig|t=dail

damage.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|damage}}, from {{der|en|fro|damage}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*damnāticum}} from Classical {{der|en|la|damnum}}. Compare modern {{cog|fr|dommage}}. Largely displaced native {{inh|en|enm|scath}} (whence {{m|en|unscathed}}). Cognate with {{cog|es|daño}}, {{cog|pt|dano}}, {{cog|it|danno}}, {{cog|fr|dam}}, {{cog|ro|daună}}.

damp.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|dampen|t=to stifle; suffocate}}, from {{inh|en|ang|damp}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dampaz}}.

Akin to Low German {{m|osx|damp}}, {{cog|nl|damp}}, and {{cog|de|Dampf||vapor, steam, fog}}, {{cog|is|dampi}}, {{cog|sv|damm||dust}}, and to {{cog|de|dampf|}} imperative of {{m|de|dimpfen||to smoke}}. Also {{der|en|enm|dampen||to extinguish, choke, suffocate}}.

danger.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*demh₂-}}
From {{der|en|enm|daunger||power, dominion, peril}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} {{m|fro|dangier}}, from {{der|en|fro|dangier}}, alteration of {{cog|fro|dongier}} (due to association with {{cog|la|damnum||damage}}) from {{der|en|la-vul|*dominiārium||authority, power}} from {{der|en|la|dominus||lord, master}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> Displaced native {{noncog|ang|frēcennes}

dangerous.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|daungerous||difficult, severe, domineering, arrogant, fraught with danger}}, {{m|enm|dangerous}}, from {{der|en|xno|}}, from {{der|en|fro|dangereus||threatening, difficult}}, from {{m|fro|dangier}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|danger|-ous}}.

Displaced native {{noncog|ang|frēcne}}.

dark.text:
{{ety|en|id=adjective|:inh|enm:derk}}
From {{inh|en|enm|derk}}, from {{inh|en|ang|deorc}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*derk|t=dark}}, of uncertain origin, but possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰerg-|t=dim, dull}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰer-|t=dull, dirty}}.

deadline.text: According to the ''Oxford English Dictionary'', early usage refers to lines that do not move, such as one used in angling. Slightly later American usage refers to a boundary in a prison which prisoners must not cross. There is only indirect evidence that the sense of "due date" may be connected with this use of the term in prison camps during the American Civil War, when it referred to a physical

deadly.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:dedly|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|dedly}}, {{m|enm|dedlych}}, {{m|enm|dedlich}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dēadlīċ|pos=adjective}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dauþalīk}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dauþalīkaz|t=deadly|lit=deathly}}. {{surf|en|dead|-ly|id2=adjectival}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|dodelk|t=deadly}}, {{cog|fy|deadlik|t=deadly}}, {{cog|nl|dodelijk|t=deadly}}, {{cog|de|tödlich|t=deadly}},

debt.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|dette}}, {{m|enm|dett}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|dete}} ({{cog|fr|dette}}), from {{der|en|la-med|dēbita}}, from {{der|en|la|dēbitum||what is owed, a debt, a duty}}, neuter of {{m|la|dēbitus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|dēbeō||to owe}}, contraction of {{m|la|*dehibeō||I have from}}, from {{m|la|de||from}} + {{m|la|habeō||to have}}. {{dou

decade.text: From {{inh|en|enm|decade}}, from {{der|en|fro|decade}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|decās|decādem|t=(set of) ten}}, from {{der|en|grc|δεκάς}}, from {{m|grc|δέκα||ten}}. In reference to a span of ten years, originally a clipping of the phrase ''decade of'' {{m|en|years}}. {{surf|en|dec-|-ade}}. {{dbt|en|decad|dekad}}.

decay.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱh₂d-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|decaien||to decrease, diminish}} and {{m|enm|decai||deterioration, decline in value}}, from {{der|en|xno|decheoir|decaeir|t=to fall away, decay, decline}}, from {{der|en|la-vul||*dēcadere}}, etymologically restored form of {{der|en|la|dēcidō|dēcidere|t=to fall down, to fail, sink or perish}}, from {{m|la|de-||of, from, away, down}} + {{m|la|cadō|cadere|

decent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deḱ-}}
{{bor+|en|frm|décent}}, or its source, {{der|en|la|decēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|decet||it is fitting or suitable}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*deḱ-||to take, accept, to receive, greet, be suitable}} (compare {{cog|grc|δοκέω||to appear, seem, think}}, {{m|grc|δέχομαι||to accept}}; {{cog|sa|दशस्यति||shows honor, is gracious|tr=daśasyáti}}, {{m|sa|दाशति||makes offering

From {{der|en|enm|decorat||adorned}}, from {{der|en|la|decorātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|decorō||to adorn, distinguish, honor}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|decus||ornament, grace, dignity, honor|pos=''decor-'' in compounds}}, akin to {{m|la|decor||elegance, grace, beauty, orname

deduce.text:

definite.text: From {{bor|en|la|dēfīnītus}}, past participle of {{m|la|dēfīniō}}, whence also English {{m|en|define}}.

demonstration.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|demonstracioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|demonstration}}, from {{der|en|la|dēmōnstrātiō|dēmōnstrātiōnem}}, from {{m|la|dēmōnstrō|dēmōnstrāre|show or explain}}, from {{m|la|dē-||of or concerning}} + {{m|la|mōnstrō|mōnstrāre|show}}.
Morphologically {{suf|en|demonstrate|ion}}.

denote.text: From {{der|en|frm|denoter}}, from {{der|en|la|denotare}}, from {{m|la|de-||complete}} and {{m|la|notare||to mark out}}.

deny.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁eǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|denyen}}, from {{der|en|fro|denoier||to deny, to repudiate}} ({{cog|fr|dénier}}), from {{der|en|la|denegare||to deny, to refuse}}, from {{m|la|de-||away}} and {{m|la|negare||to refuse}}, the latter ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*né||no, not}}. {{doublet|en|denegate}}.

department.text: From {{inh|en|enm|departement|t=ceasing, end}}, from {{der|en|frm|département}}. Later senses borrowed from Modern {{bor|en|fr|département}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> {{doublet|en|département}}.

depress.text: From {{inh|en|enm|depressen}}, from {{der|en|fro|depresser}}, from {{der|en|la|dēpressus}}, perfect participle of {{m|la|dēprimō||to press down, to weigh down}}, from {{af|la|dē-|premō|t1=off, away, down, out|t2=to press|nocat=1}}.

derive.text: From {{inh|en|enm|deriven}}, from {{der|en|fro|deriver}}, from {{der|en|la|dērīvō||to lead, turn, or draw off (a liquid), draw off, derive}}, from {{m|la|dē||away}} + {{m|la|rīvus||a stream}}; see {{m|en|rival}}. Unrelated to {{m|en|arrive}}.

descend.text:
{{word|en|ine|dé}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*skend-}}
The {{glossary|verb}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|descenden|t=to move downwards, fall, descend; to slope downwards; to go from a better to a worse condition, decline, degenerate; to be a descendant, derive from (a source); etc.}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=dē̆scenden|pos=v|id=MED11268}}</ref> from {{der|en|xno|descendere}}, {{m|xno|descendre}}, and {{d

description.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kreybʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|descripcioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|description}} and its etymon, {{der|en|la|dēscrīptiō}}, noun of action of {{m|la|dēscrībō||to describe}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|describe|tion}}.

design.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:designen<ety:der<fro:designer<ety:der<la:designō>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|designen}}, from {{der|en|fro|designer}}, from {{der|en|la|designō||to mark out, point out, describe, design, contrive}}, from {{m|la|de-}} (or {{m|la|dis-}}) + {{m|la|signō||to mark}}, from {{m|la|signum||mark}}. {{doublet|en|designate}}.

desire.text: From {{inh|en|enm|desir}}, {{m|enm|desire|pos=noun}} and {{m|enm|desiren|pos=verb}}, from {{der|en|fro|desirer}}, {{m|fro|desirrer}}, from {{der|en|la|dēsīderō|t=to long for, desire, feel the want of, miss, regret}}, apparently from {{m|la|de-}} + {{m|la|sidus}} (in the phrase ''de sidere'', "from the stars") in connection with astrological hopes. Compare {{m|en|consider}} and {{m|en|desiderate}}.

desk.text: From {{inh|en|enm|deske}}, {{m|enm|desque}}, from {{der|en|la-med|desca}}, modified from {{der|en|roa-oit|desco}}, from {{der|en|la|discus}}. {{doublet|en|dais|disc|discus|dish|disk|diskos}}. See also {{der|en|de|Tisch}}, "table".

desperate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*speh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|desperat|desperat(e)|t=desperate}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|dēspērātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|dēspērō||to be without hope}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}. The {{glossary|noun}} is derived from the {{glossary|adjective}} or from the Latin source through [[substan

detail.text:
{{bor+|en|frm|détail}}, from {{der|en|fro|detail}}, from {{m|fro|detaillier}}, from {{m|fro|de-}} + {{m|fro|taillier||to cut}}.

Compare typologically {{m+|bg|подробност}}, {{m+|cs|podrobnost}}, {{m+|ru|подро́бность}} (akin to {{m|ru|дроби́ть}}).

The [[#Adjective|adjective]] is from {{bor|en|la-cla||dētēct-}}, past participial stem of {{m|la|dētegō|t=to detect}}, {{suffix|en||ive}}.<ref name="OED">{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=7992603044}}</ref> {{surf|en|detect|-ive}}.

From {{bor|en|la-lat|dēviātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|dēviō}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} for more. Compare {{cog|fr|dévier}}.

{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁wegʷʰ-}}
{{bor+|en|la|dēvōtus}}, past participle of {{der|en|la|dēvoveō|t=dedicate by a vow, sacrifice oneself, promise solemnly}}. {{doublet|en|devow}}; see also {{m|en|devout}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|ēstful}}, from {{ncog|ang|ēstful}}.

{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁yaǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|dyner}}, from {{der|en|fro|disner||lunch”, but originally “breakfast}}, (modern {{cog|fr|dîner}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*disiūnō|*disiūnō, *disiūnāre}} from {{der|en|la|dis-}} + {{m|la|iēiūnō||to break the fast}}.

diplomatic.text: From {{bor|en|fr|diplomatique}} and its etymon {{bor|en|la-new|diplōmaticus}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=7747771233}}</ref><ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary|pos=adj}}</ref> {{surf|en|diplomat|-ic}}.

disaster.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eHs-}}
From {{der|en|frm|desastre}}, from {{der|en|it|disastro}}, from {{m|it|dis-}} + {{m|it|astro||star}}, from {{der|en|la|astrum||star}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἄστρον||star}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂stḗr}}.

Displaced native {{cog|enm|adle|adle, audle|disease}} (from {{cog|ang|ādl||disease, sickness}}, see {{l|en|adle}}), {{cog|enm|cothe|cothe, coathe|disease}} (from {{cog|ang|coþu||diseas

dismiss.text:
{{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:dismissen//dismisen<ety:lbor<la:dīmittō<alt:dīmittō, ~mittĕre, ~mīsī, ~missum>>>|:af<surf>|dis-|miss}}
Middle English, from {{der|en|la|dimissus||sent away, dismissed, banished}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|dīmittō||send away, dismiss}}, from {{affix|la|dis-|mittere|gloss2=to send|nocat=1}}.

display.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*pleḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|displayen}}, from {{der|en|xno|despleier}} and {{der|en|fro|despleier}}, {{m|fro|desploiier}}, from {{der|en|la-med|displicare||to unfold, display}}, from {{der|en|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|plicāre||to fold}}. {{doublet|en|deploy}}.

dissolve.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*lewh₁-}}
Recorded since c. 1374 (displacing {{noncog|ang|toliesan}}) as {{inh|en|enm|dissolven}}, from {{der|en|la|dissolvo|dissolvere|t=to loosen up, break apart}} but with the sense from {{der|en|xno|dissoldre}} (variant of {{cog|fro|dissoudre}}), itself from {{m|la|dis-|t=apart}} + {{m|la|solvo|solvere|t=to loose, loosen}}. {{surf|en|dis-|solve}}.

distinction.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:distinccioun<ety:bor<fro:distinction<ety:bor<la:distīnctiō>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|distinccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|distinction}} (attested from the 12th century), borrowed from {{der|en|la|distinctio|distīnctiōnem}}, action noun of {{m|la|distinguō|t=separate, distinguish}}. {{surf|en|distinct#Verb<t:to distinguish>|-ion}}. Attested in English from the late 14th century.

distinguish.text: From {{inh|en|enm|distingwen}}, from {{der|en|fro|distinguer}}, from {{der|en|la|distinguo|distinguere|to separate, divide, distinguish, set off, adorn, literally mark off}}, from {{m|la|di-}}, {{m|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|stinguo|stinguere}}, related to {{cog|en|stink}}. Compare {{m|en|extinguish}}.

distort.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*terkʷ-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|distortum}}, past participle of {{m|la|distorqueō||to twist, torture, distort}}.

distribute.text:
{{PIE word|en|tréyes}}
From {{uder|en|la|distributus}}, past participle of {{m|la|[[distribuo|distribuere]]||to divide, distribute}}, from {{m|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|[[tribuo|tribuere]]||to give, impart}}; see [[tribute]].

distribution.text: From {{uder|en|fro|distribution}}, from {{der|en|la|distributio}}, from {{m|la|distribuere||to distribute}}, itself from {{m|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|tribuere||to assign, allot}} (from {{m|la|tribus}}). {{surf|en|distribute|-ion}}.

doctrine.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deḱ-}}

donate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deh₃-}}
Circa 1845, back-formation from {{m|en|donation}} on the basis of {{l|en|-ate|id=verb|pos=verb-forming suffix}}, chiefly found in {{w|American English}}. Ultimately from {{der|en|la|dono|dōnāre|to give}}.

dot.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|*dot}}, {{m|enm|dotte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|dott|t=a dot, point}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dott}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*duttaz|t=wisp}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Dot}}, {{m|stq|Dotte|t=a clump}}, {{cog|nl|dot|t=lump, knot, clod}}, {{cog|nds|Dutte|t=a plug}}, dialectal {{cog|sv|dott|t=a little heap, bunch, clump}}.

{{en-noun}}

draft.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰregʰ-}}
A phonetic spelling of {{m|en|draught}} (compare {{m|en|laughter}}), from {{inh|en|enm|draught}}, {{m|enm|draght|t=that which is pulled; that which is drawn up, a design}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*dreaht}}, {{m|ang|*dræht}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*drahti}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*drahtu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drahtuz|t=a pulling, drawing}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|dracht}}, {{cog|de

drain.text: {{ety|en|:inh|enm:*dreinen<ety:inh<ang: drēahnian<ety:inh<gmw-pro:*drauhnōn<ety:inh<gem-pro:*drauhnōną<ety:from<gem-pro:*draugiz>>>>>>>>|tree=+|text=++}}  Akin to {{cog|ang|drūgian|t=to dry up}}, {{cog|ang|drūgaþ|t=dryness, drought}}, {{cog|ang|drȳġe|t=dry}}. More at {{m|en|dry}}.

drama.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|la-lat:drāma}}
From {{bor|en|la-lat|drāma}}, from {{der|en|grc|δρᾶμα|t=an act, a theatrical act, a play}}, from {{m|grc|δράω|t=to act, to take action, to achieve}}. {{doublet|en|dorama}}.

drift.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:drift<ety:inh<ang:*drift>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|drift}}, {{m|enm|dryft||act of driving, drove, shower of rain or snow, impulse}}, from {{der|en|ang|*drift||drift}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*driftiz||drift}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰreybʰ-||to drive, push}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|en|drive|t|id2=th}}; cognate with {{cog|frr|drift||drift}}, {{cog|stq|Drift||current, flow, s

driver.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:drivere<ety:af<driven><-ere<id:agent suffix>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|drivere}}, {{m|enm|dryvere}}, {{m|enm|dryvare}}, equivalent to {{af|en|drive|-er|id2=agent noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Drieuwer|t=driver}}, {{cog|nl|drijver|t=driver}}, {{cog|nds-de|Driever|t=driver}}, {{cog|de|Treiber|t=driver}}, {{cog|sv|drivare|t=driver}}.

driving.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|dryvyng}}, {{m|enm|drivende}}, from {{inh|en|ang|drīfende}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*drībandz}}, present participle of {{der|en|gem-pro|*drībaną|t=to drive}}, equivalent to {{af|en|drive|-ing|id2=participial}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|drieuwend}}, {{cog|fy|driuwend}}, {{cog|nl|drijvend}}, {{cog|nds-de|drievend}}, {{cog|de|treibend}}, {{cog|sv|drivande}}.

due.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}}
From {{der|en|enm|dewe}}, {{m|enm|dew}}, {{m|enm|due}}, from {{der|en|fro|deu|deü|due}}, past participle of {{m|fro|devoir||to owe}}, from {{der|en|la|dēbeō|dēbēre|t=to owe}}, from {{prefix|la|dē|habeō|gloss1=from|t2=to have|nocat=1}}.

dull.text: From {{inh|en|enm|dull}}, {{m|enm|dul}} (also {{m|enm|dyll}}, {{m|enm|dill}}, {{m|enm|dwal}}), from {{inh|en|ang|dol|t=dull, foolish, erring, heretical; foolish, silly; presumptuous}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*dol}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*dulaz}}, from earlier {{m|gem-pro|*dwulaz}}, a variant of {{m|gem-pro|*dwalaz|t=stunned, mad, foolish, misled}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*dʰwel-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*dʰe

dump.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|dumpen}}, {{m|enm|dompen}}, probably from {{der|en|non|dumpa|t=to thump}} (whence {{cog|da|dumpe|t=to fall suddenly}}), of uncertain origin, possibly {{onomatopoeic|en|title=imitative}} of falling, similar to {{m|en|thump}}.
