ease.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|ese}}, {{m|enm|eise}}, {{m|enm|aise}}, from {{der|en|xno|ese|t=ease}}, from {{der|en|fro|eise}}, {{m|fro|aise|t=elbow room; opportunity}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} and obscure origin. Apparently related to Provençal {{m|oc|ais}}, {{cog|it|agio}} and {{m|it|asio}},  {{cog|scn|aciu}} and  {{cog|pt|azo}}.<ref name=oed/> Sometimes ascribed to {{der|en|la-vu

eastern.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|esturne}}, {{m|enm|esterne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ēasterne||eastern}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*austrōnijaz||eastern}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*h₂ews-ro-|eastern}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ews-||dawn, east}}. Cognate with {{cog|osx|-}} and {{cog|goh|ōstrōni||eastern}}, {{cog|non|austrœnn||eastern}}.

Morphologically {{af|en|east|-ern}}.

echo.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:eccho|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|eccho}}, {{m|enm|ecco}}, {{m|enm|echo}}, {{m|enm|ekko}}, from {{der|en|la-med|ēccō}}, from {{der|en|la|ēchō}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἠχώ}}, from {{m|grc|ἠχή||sound}}. Possibly from the same {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} root as {{m|en|sough}}.

economy.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyḱ-|*nem-|id2=distribute}}
From {{inh|en|enm|yconomye}}, {{m|enm|yconomy}}, borrowed via {{der|en|fro|yconomie}} or [[w:Medieval Latin|Medieval Latin]]<ref>{{R:MED Online|īconomī(e|n|MED21656}}</ref> from {{der|en|la|oeconomia}}, from {{der|en|grc|οἰκονομία||management of a household, administration}}, from {{m|grc|οἶκος||house}} + {{m|grc|νέμω||distribute, allocate}}. {{surf|

editor.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|la-med:ēditor|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|la-med|ēditor}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|ēditor}},<ref>http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/editor</ref> from {{m|la|ēditus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|ēdō|t=give out, put forth, publish}}.

effective.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|fr:effectif|:afeq|effect<id:noun>|-ive|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|fr|effectif}}, from {{der|en|la|effectīvus|t=productive; effective}}, from {{m|la|efficiō|t=to make; to bring about}}, equivalent to {{af|en|effect|-ive}}.

efficient.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}
1398, “making,” from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|efficientem}}, nominative {{m|la|efficiēns}}, participle of {{m|la|efficere|t=work out, accomplish}} (see {{m|en|effect}}). Meaning “productive, skilled” is from 1787. ''[[efficiency|Efficiency]] apartment'' is first recorded [[wikipedia:1930|1930]], [[American English]]. <ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref>

elbow.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:elbowe|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|elbowe||elbow}}, from {{inh|en|ang|elboga}}, {{m|ang|elnboga||elbow}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*alinabugô||elbow}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|ell|bow|nocat=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|elbuck||elbow}}, {{cog|stq|Älbooge||elbow}}, {{cog|nl|elleboog||elbow}}, {{cog|nds|Ellebage||elbow}}, {{cog|de|Ellbogen}}, {{m|de|Ellenbogen||elbow}}, {{cog|da,nb|a

elegant.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|elegaunt}}, from {{der|en|frm|elegant}}, ultimately from {{der|en|la|ēlegāns}}, collateral form of present participle of {{m|la|ēligere}}, from {{affix|la|ex-|t1=out of, from|legō|t2=choose, select, appoint}}.

elementary.text: From {{inh|en|enm|elementare}}, from {{der|en|la|elementārius||elementary}}, from {{m|la|elementum|t=one of the four [[element]]s of [[antiquity]]; [[fundamental]]s}} + {{m|la|-ārius|pos=adjective-forming suffix}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=elementāre|pos=adj|id=MED13244}}</ref><ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=adj|id=4143542145}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|fr|élémentaire}}. {{surf|en|element|-ary}}.

eliminate.text: {{bor+|en|la|ēlīminātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|ēlīminō||to turn out of doors, banish}}, from {{af|la|ex-|līmen|-ō|alt1=ē-|pos2=''līmin-'' in compounds|t2=a threshold|id3=denominative|pos3=first conjugation verb-forming suffix|nocat=1}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), akin to {{noncog|la|līmes||a boundary}}; see also {{

elsewhere.text: From {{inh|en|enm|elswher}}, from {{inh|en|ang|elles hwǣr}} and {{m|ang|elles hwerġen|t=elsewhere}}; corresponding with {{univ|en|else|where|notext=1}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|alleswār|t=elsewhere}}, whence {{cog|gmh|alleswā}}, {{m|gmh|alswā|t=elsewhere}}.

embrace.text:
[[File:Twoflorencemenkiss.jpg|thumb|{{w|Bartolomeo Cesi}}, ''Two Men in Florence Kissing'' (1600),{{ref|group=n|name=n1|From the collection of the {{w|Uffizi Gallery}}, [[Florence]], [[Italy]].}} a drawing depicting two men embracing ''(sense 1)'']]{{root|en|ine-pro|*mreǵʰ-}}
The verb is derived from {{inh|en|enm|embracen|t=to clasp in one's arms, embrace; to reach out eagerly for, welcome; to enf

emerge.text: {{etydate|late 16th century}}. Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|emerger}}, from {{der|en|la|ēmergō|t=to rise up or out}}, from {{m|la|ē-}} (a variant of {{m|la|ex-||out, forth}}) + {{m|la|mergō|t=to dip, to sink}}

emergency.text:
{{etymon|en|id=urgent situation|:bor|la:emergens<id:emerging>}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la-med|emergentia}}, from {{der|en|la|emergens}}, present participle of {{m|la|emergo|t=to emerge, arise, come forth}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|emergent|cy}} or {{suffix|en|emerge|ency}}. {{doublet|en|emergence}}.

emotion.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:emotion<ety:from<esmouvoir>>|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|frm|emotion}} (modern {{cog|fr|émotion}}), from {{m|fr|émouvoir||excite}}, based on {{der|en|la|ēmōtus}}, past participle of {{m|la|ēmoveō||to move out, move away, remove, stir up, irritate}}, from {{m|la|ē-||out}} (variant of {{m|la|ex-}}), and {{m|la|moveō||move}}.

emphasis.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₂-|id=shine}}
From {{bor|en|la|emphasis}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἔμφασις||significance}}, from {{m|grc|ἐμφαίνω||to present; to indicate}}, from {{m|grc|ἐν-||in}} + {{m|grc|φαίνω||to show}}.

employee.text: From {{suf|en|employ|-ee}}.<ref name="MWO">{{R:MWO}}</ref><ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> {{etydate|early 19th century}}, possibly modeled after {{der|en|fr|employé}}.<ref name="MWO"/><ref>{{R:OED Online|id=7018874683|noformat=1|pos=''n''.<sup>1</sup>}}</ref>

employment.text: From {{m|en|employ}} (itself from {{der|en|frm|employer}}, from {{der|en|frm|empleier}}, from {{der|en|la|implicō||enfold, involve, be connected with}}, itself from {{m|la|in-}} + {{m|la|plicō||fold}}) {{suffix|en||ment}}.

empty.text: From {{inh|en|enm|emty}}, {{m|enm|amty}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ǣmtiġ}}, {{m|ang|ǣmettiġ|t=vacant, empty, free, idle, unmarried|lit=without must or obligation, leisurely}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|-}} {{m|gem-pro|*uz-|t=out}} + {{der|en|gem-pro|*mōtijô}}, {{m|gem-pro|*mōtô|t=must, obligation, need}}, {{m|gem-pro|*mōtiþô|t=ability, accommodation}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*med-|t=measure; to acquire, posse

encounter.text: From {{inh|en|enm|encountren}}, from {{der|en|xno|encountrer}}, {{der|en|fro|encontrer|t=to confront}}, from {{m|fro|encontre|t=against, counter to}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|incontrā|t=in front of}} itself from {{der|en|la|in|t=in}} + {{m|la|contrā|t=against}}.

ending.text:
{{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:endynge}}
From {{inh|en|enm|endynge}}, {{m|enm|endyng}}, {{m|enm|endinge}}, from {{inh|en|ang|endung}}, {{m|ang|ġeendung|t=ending}}, equivalent to {{af|en|end|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|ending|t=ending}}, {{cog|de|Endung|t=ending}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A [[termination]] or [[conclusion]].
# The last part of something.
#: {{ux|en|The book has

endorse.text: Alteration influenced by {{der|en|la-med|indorso|indorsare}} of {{inh|en|enm|endosse}}, from {{der|en|fro|endosser||to put on the back}}, from {{der|en|la|dossum}}, alternative form of {{m|la|dorsum||back}},<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> from which also {{m|en|dorsal||of the back}}. That is, the ‘r’ was dropped in {{m+|la|dossum}}, which developed into Old French and then {{m+|enm|en

energy.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|frm:énergie<ety:der<la-lat:energīa>>|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|frm|énergie}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|energia}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἐνέργεια||activity}}, from {{m|grc|ἐνεργός||active}}, from {{m|grc|ἐν||in}} + {{m|grc|ἔργον||work}}. The sense in physics was {{coin|en|Q25820|in=1802|nocap=1}} in his lectures on Natural Philosophy.

engage.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*wedʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|engagen}}, from {{der|en|fro|engagier|t=to pledge, engage}}, from {{der|en|fro|en-|t=in, under}} + {{m|fro|gage|t=pledge}}, from {{der|en|frk|*wadi|t=pledge}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wadją|t=pledge, guarantee}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wedʰ-|t=to pledge, redeem a pledge; guarantee, bail}}, equivalent to {{af|en|en-|gage}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|weddian|

engine.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|engyn}}, from {{der|en|xno|engine}}, {{der|en|fro|engin||skill, cleverness, war machine}}, from {{der|en|la|ingenium||innate or natural quality, nature, genius, a genius, an invention, (in {{cog|la-lat|-}}) a war-engine, battering-ram}}, related to {{m|la|ingignō||to instil by birth, implant, produce in}}. Compare {{m|en|gin}}, {{m|en|ingenious}}, {{m|

parts: pos2=suffix forming nouns denoting people associated with, concerned with, or engaged in specified activities

enhance.text: From {{inh|en|enm|enhauncen|enhauncen, anhaunsen}}, from {{der|en|xno|enhaucier|anhauncer|t=enhance, raise}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*altiare|*inaltiāre|t=raise}}, derived from {{der|en|la|in|}} + {{m|la|altus|t=high}}. The /h/ in Old French was taken from {{m|fro|haut|t=high}}, where it resulted from {{der|en|frk|-}} influence.

enormous.text: From {{der|en|la|ēnormis}}. An assimilated form of {{af|la|ex-|t1=out of|nocat=1}} + {{m|la|norma|t=rule, norm}} + {{af|en|-ous}}.

entail.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|entaillen}}, from {{der|en|fro|entaillier}}, {{m|fro|entailler|t=to notch|lit=to cut in}}; from prefix {{m|fro|en-}} + {{m|fro|tailler|t=to cut}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|taliare}}, from {{der|en|la|talea}}. Compare late {{cog|la|feudum talliatum|t=a fee entailed, i.e., curtailed or limited}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[imply]], [[require]], or [[invoke]]

enterprise.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰed-}}
From {{der|en|fro|-}} via {{der|en|enm|-}} and {{der|en|frm|entreprise}}, feminine past participle of {{m|fro|entreprendre||to undertake}}, from {{m|frm|entre||in between}} + {{m|fro|prendre||to take}}, from Latin {{m|la|inter}} + {{m|la|prehendō}}, see {{m|en|prehensile}}.

enthusiasm.text: First attested from {{w|1603}}, from {{der|en|frm|enthousiasme}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|enthusiasmus}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἐνθουσιασμός}}, from {{m|grc|ἐν||in}} + {{m|grc|θεός||god}} + {{m|grc|οὐσία||essence}}.

entity.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|la-med:entitās|tree=1}}
From the {{bor|en|la-med|entitās}}, from {{m|la|ēns|t=being}} (stem: {{m|la||ent-}}) + {{m|la|-tās}} (compare {{m|la|essentia}}), see there for more information.

entry.text: {{inh+|en|enm|entre}}, from {{der|en|fro|entree}} (feminine past participle of the verb {{m|fro|entrer}}, Modern {{cog|fr|entrée}}). From {{der|en|la|intrō}}. {{dbt|en|entrada|entrée}}.

episode.text: From {{bor|en|fr|épisode}}, from {{der|en|la-new|*epīsodium}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἐπεισόδιον||a parenthetic addition, episode}}, neuter of {{m|grc|ἐπεισόδιος||following upon the entrance, coming in besides, adventitious}}, from {{m|grc|ἐπί||on}} + {{m|grc|εἰς||into}} + {{m|grc|ὁδός||way}}.

error.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁ers-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|errour}}, from {{der|en|xno|errour}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|error}}, from {{der|en|la|error|t=wandering about|pos=noun}}, derived from the verb {{m|la|errō|t=to wander, to err}}. Cognate with {{cog|got|𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌶𐌴𐌹|t=error}}, {{cog|got|𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌶𐌾𐌰𐌽|t=to lead astray}}. More at {{l|en|err}}. {{surf|en|err|-or<pos:suffix forming nouns of quality, state, or cond

essay.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eǵ-|id=drive}}
Since late 16th century, borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|essay}}, {{m|frm|essai||essay}}, meaning [[w:Essays (Montaigne)|coined]] by [[w:Michel de Montaigne|Montaigne]] at the same time, from the same words with the earlier meanings 'experiment; assay; attempt', from {{der|en|fro|essay}}, {{m|fro|essai}}, {{m|fro|assay}}, {{m|fro|assai}}, from {{der|en|la|exagium||we

essence.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁es-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|essence}}, from {{der|en|frm|essence}}, from {{der|en|la|essentia||the being or essence of a thing}}, from an artificial formation of {{m|la|esse||to be}}, to translate {{der|en|grc|οὐσία||being}}, from {{m|grc|ὤν}}, present participle of {{m|grc|εἰμί||to be, exist}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|understandennes}} (literally, "[[understand]]en[[-ness]]

establish.text:
{{ety|en|tree=1|:inh|enm:establissen<ety:bor<fro:establir>>}}
{{inh+|en|enm|establissen}}, from {{der|en|fro||establiss-}}, stem of some of the conjugated forms of {{m|fro|establir}} (modern {{cog|fr|établir}}), from {{der|en|la|stabilio|stabiliō, stabilīre}}, from {{m|la|stabilis||firm, steady, stable}}.

eventually.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}}
{{etymon|en|:af|eventual|-ly<id:adverbial>|text=+|tree=1}} The third sense is influenced by any of several European languages, including {{cog|cs|eventuálně}}, {{cog|fr|éventuellement}}, {{cog|sv|eventuellt}}.

evidence.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|evidence}}, from {{der|en|fro}}, from {{der|en|la|evidentia||clearness, in Late Latin a proof}}, from {{m|la|evidens||clear, evident}}; see {{m|en|evident}}.

evolution.text:
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|ēvolūtiō|ēvolūtiō, ēvolūtiōnis|the act of unrolling, unfolding or opening (of a book)}}, from {{m|la|ēvolūtus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|ēvolvō||unroll, unfold}}, from {{m|la|ex}} + {{m|la|volvō||roll}}.

Compare typologically {{m+|cs|vývoj}}, {{m+|sh|развој}}, {{m+|ru|разви́ть}}, {{m|ru|развива́ть}}, {{m|ru|разви́ться}}, {{m|ru|развива́ться}}, {{m+|ru|разви́

exaggerate.text: {{bor+|en|la|exaggerātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|exaggerō||to heap up, increase, enlarge, magnify, amplify, exaggerate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|ex-||out, up}} + {{m|la|aggerō|t=to heap up|id=agger|aggerō, aggerāre}}, from {{m|la|agger||a

example.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁em-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|example}}, {{m|enm|exaumple}}, from {{der|en|fro|example}}, {{m|fro|essaumple}}, from {{der|en|la|exemplum|lit=what is taken out|t=sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc.}}; see {{m|en|exempt}}. {{doublet|en|exemplum|sample}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|forebisne}}, from {{ncog|ang|forebȳsn}}; and {{ncog|enm|bisne}}, from {{ncog|ang|bȳsn}}

exceed.text: From {{inh|en|enm|exceden}}, from {{der|en|fro|exceder}}, from {{der|en|la|excēdō|t=to go beyond}}, from {{m|la|ex-||out, forth}} with {{m|la|cēdō|t=to go}}; see {{m|en|cede}} and compare {{m|en|accede}} etc. Partly displaced native {{ncog|ang|ofersteppan}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|overstep}}.

exception.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:exception<ety:bor<xno:excepcioun<ety:from<fro:excepcion<ety:der<la:exceptiō>>>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|exception}}, {{m|enm|excepcioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|excepcioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|excepcion}}, from {{der|en|la|exceptiō}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|except|ion}}.

exchange.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|eschaunge}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|eschaunge}}, from {{der|en|fro|eschange}} (whence modern {{cog|fr|échange}}), from the verb {{m|fro|eschanger}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*excambiō|*excambiāre}} (from {{der|en|la|ex}} with {{der|en|la-lat|cambiō}}). exclusive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kleh₂w-}}
From {{uder|en|la|exclūsīvus}}, from {{m|la|excludere||to shut out, exclude}}, from {{m|la|ex-||out}} + variant form of verb {{m|la|claudere||to close, shut}}.

execute.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{der|en|fro|executer}} (French {{m|fro|exécuter}}), from {{der|en|la|exsecutus}}, past participle of {{m|la|exsequor||to follow (up/through)|pos=particularly in the sense {{m-g|to go through with a deed or punishment}}}}, from {{m|la|ex-||out}} + {{m|la|sequor||to follow}}.

executive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{bor|en|frm|executif}}, from {{der|en|la|executivus}}, from {{der|en|la|exsequi}}, from ex- ‘out’ + sequi ‘follow’.

exhibit.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}}
From {{bor|en|la|exhibitus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|exhibeō||to hold forth, present, show, display}}, from {{m|la|ex||out of, from}} + {{m|la|habeō||to have, hold}}; see [[habit]].

exotic.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|exotique}}, from {{der|en|la|exōticus}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἐξωτικός|t=foreign|lit=from the outside}}, from {{m|grc|ἐξω-|t=outside}}, from {{m|grc|ἐξ|t=out of}}.

expand.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-}}
Recorded in {{inh|en|enm|-}} since 1422 (as {{m|enm|expanden}}, {{m|enm|expaunden}}), from {{der|en|xno|espaundre}}, from {{der|en|la|expandō|t=to spread out}}, itself from {{m|la|ex-||out, outwards}} + {{m|la|pandō||to spread}}. {{doublet|en|spawn}}.

{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=fare}}
From {{inh|en|enm|experiment}}, from {{der|en|fro|esperiment}} ({{cog|fr|expérience}}), from {{der|en|la|experimentum||experience, attempt, experiment}}, from {{m|la|experior||to experience, to attempt}}, itself from {{m|la|ex}} + {{m|la|*perior}}, in turn from {{der|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=fare}}.

expert.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id=fare}}
{{inh+|en|enm|expert}}, {{der+|en|fro|expert|t=experienced|nocap=1}}, {{m|fro|espert}}, from {{der|en|la|expertus}} (contracted from {{m|la|*experitus}}), {{lg|perfect}} {{lg|active voice|active}} {{lg|participle}} of {{m|la|experior||to try}}, from {{pre|la|ex-|*-perior|nocat=1}}.{{ref|name=AHD expert|{{R:AHD|expert|624|2}}}}

explode.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|la:explōdō|tree=1}}
First recorded around 1538, from the {{der|en|la|-}} verb {{m|la|[[explodo|explōdere]]||drive out or off by clapping}}. The meaning was originally [[theatrical]], "to drive an actor off the stage by making noise," hence meaning to "to [[drive out]]" or "to [[reject]]". From {{der|en|frm|explorer}}, from {{der|en|la|explōrō|explōrāre|to investigate, search out}}, itself said to be originally a hunters' term meaning "to set up a loud cry", from {{m|la|ex-||out}} + {{m|la|plōrō|plōrāre|to cry}}, but the second element is also explained as "to make to flow" (from {{m|la|pluō|pluere|to flow}}).<ref name="Etymonline">{{R:Etymonli

{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:explosion|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|fr|explosion}}, from {{der|en|la|explōsio}}, from {{m|la|explōdo||to drive out by clapping}}, from {{m|la|ex-}} and {{m|la|plōdo||to clap or strike}}. For more information see {{m|en|explode}}.

{{root|en|ine-pro|*tḱey-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|exposen}}, from {{der|en|fro|exposer|t=to lay open, set forth}}, from {{der|en|la|expōnō|t=set forth}}, with contamination from {{m|fro|poser|t=to lay, place}}. {{doublet|en|expone|expound}} (via {{der|en|fro|espondre|t=to set forth, explain}}), from the same Latin term.

extent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}}
From {{inh|en|enm|extente}}, from {{der|en|xno|extente}} and {{der|en|fro|estente||valuation of land, stretch of land}}, from {{m|fro|estendre}}, {{m|fro|extendre||extend}} (or from Latin {{m|la|extentus}}), from {{der|en|la|extendere}} (See {{m|en|extend}}.)

external.text:
{{word|en|ine|h₁éǵʰs}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|la-med|externus||outward, external}}, from {{m|la|[[exter]]/[[exterus]]||on the outside, outward}}.

extreme.text: Borrowed into late {{inh|en|enm|-}} from {{der|en|fro|extreme}}, from {{der|en|la|extrēmus}}, the superlative of {{m|la|exter}}.<!--should this be "externus", which means "outside"?-->

{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}
From {{der|en|frm|genereux}}, and its source, {{der|en|la|generōsus|t=of noble birth}}, from {{m|la|genus|t=race, stock}}.

{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}
From {{bor|en|la|genius|t=[[inborn]] [[nature]]; a [[tutelary deity]] of a [[person]] or [[place]]; [[wit]], [[brilliance]]}}, from {{m|la|gignō|t=to beget, produce}}, {{der|en|itc-ola|genō}}, from the {{der|en|ine-pro|-}} root {{m|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}. {{doublet|en|genio}}. ''See also'' [[genus]] and [[genie]].

{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|gentil||courteous, noble}}, from {{der|en|fro|gentil||high-born, noble}}, from {{der|en|la|gentilis||of the same family or clan}}, from {{m|la|gens||[Roman] clan}}. {{doublet|en|gentile|genteel|jaunty}}.

Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|grade||a grade, degree}}, from {{der|en|la|gradus||a step, pace, degree}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*graðus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰradʰ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*gʰredʰ-||to walk, go}}. {{doublet|en|gradus}}.

{{etymon|en|id=instrument|:bor|es:guitarra<id:instrument>|tree=1}}

From {{inh|en|enm|harmful}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*hearmful}} (suggested by {{m|ang|hearmfullīċ||harmful; hurtful}}), equivalent to {{suffix|en|harm|ful|pos=adjective}}.

Cognate with {{cog|de|harmvoll}}, {{cog|da|harmfuld}}, {{cog|sv|harmfull}}.

hobby.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|hoby|t=small horse, pony}}, a variant or alteration of {{m|enm|hobyn|t=a small ambling horse}}, of {{unc|en|title=uncertain and disputed origin}}. According to one theory the term is derived from ''Hobin'', a pet name of {{m|en|Robert}} or {{m|en|Robin}}, at the time frequently used as a [[proper name]] for a workhorse (compare {{m|en|dobbin}}).

herb.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|herbe}}, {{m|enm|erbe}}, from {{der|en|fro|erbe}} (French {{m|fr|herbe}}), from {{der|en|la|herba}}. Initial ''h'' was restored to the spelling in the 15th century on the basis of Latin, but it remained mute until the 19th century and still is for many speakers. {{doublet|en|yerba}}.

hint.text: From {{inh|en|enm|hinten}}, {{m|enm|hynten}}, variant of {{m|enm|henten|t=to lay hold of, catch}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hentan|t=to seize, grasp}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hantijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hantijaną}}. {{doublet|en|hent}}. Related also to {{m|en|hunt}}.

heritage.text: From {{inh|en|enm|heritage}}, from {{der|en|fro|eritage,heritage}} (modern {{cog|fr|héritage}}), ultimately derived (through suffixation) from {{der|en|la|hērēs}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=6071824639}}</ref> {{surf|en|herit|-age}}.

historian.text: From {{inh|en|enm|historian}}, {{m|enm|historien}}, from {{der|en|fro|historien}}, from {{der|en|la|historia|t=story, history}}, equivalent to {{af|en|history|alt1=histor(y)|-ian}}. More at {{m|en|history}}.

hunt.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|hunten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|huntian||to hunt}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*huntōn||to hunt, capture}}, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱent-||to catch, seize}}. Related to {{cog|goh|hunda||booty}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐌿𐌽𐌸𐍃||body of captives}}, {{cog|ang|hūþ||plunder, booty, prey}}, {{cog|ang|hentan||to catch, seize}}. More at {{l|en|hent}}, {{l|en|hint}}.
In some areas read as a collective fo

ideal.text:
From {{der|en|fr|idéal}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|ideālis|t=existing in idea}}, {{surf|en|idea|-al|nocap=1}}, from {{der|en|la|idea|t=idea}}; see {{m|en|idea}}.
In mathematics, the noun [[ring theory]] sense was first introduced by German mathematician {{w|Richard Dedekind}} in his 1871 edition of a text on [[number theory]]. The concept was quickly expanded to [[ring theory]] and later generalis

hypothesis.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}
Recorded since 1596, from {{bor|en|frm|hypothese}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|hypothesis}}, from {{der|en|grc|ὑπόθεσις|t=base, basis of an argument, supposition|lit=a placing under}}, itself from {{m|grc|ὑποτίθημι|t=to set before, suggest}}, from {{m|grc|ὑπό|t=below}} + {{m|grc|τίθημι|t=to put, place}}. Compare {{m|en|hypothec}}.

hotel.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:hôtel|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|fr|hôtel}}, from {{der|en|frm|hostel}}, from {{der|en|fro|ostel}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|hospitālis||hospice, shelter, guesthouse}}, from {{der|en|la|hospitālis||hospitable}}. {{doublet|en|hostel|hospital}}.

holiday.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:halyday|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|halyday}}, {{m|enm|holyday}}, {{m|enm|halidei}}, {{m|enm|haliȝdei}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hāliġdæġ|t=holy day, Sabbath}}, equivalent to {{com|en|holy|day}}. Compare {{cog|fy|hjeldei|t=holiday}}, {{cog|da|helligdag|t=holiday}}, {{cog|no|helligdag|t=holiday}}, {{cog|sv|helgdag|t=holiday, feast}}.

humanity.text:
{{dercat|en|fro|la}}
{{inh+|en|enm|humanyte}}, {{m|enm|humanite}}, {{m|enm|humanitye}}, from {{der|en|fro|humanité}}, from {{der|en|la|hūmānitās}}. {{surf|en|[[human]] ''or'' [[humane]]|-ity}}. Partly displaced {{m|en|mankind}}, from {{w|Old English}} {{m|ang|mancynn|lit=human race}}.

hug.text: From earlier {{m|en|hugge|t=to embrace, clasp with the arms}} (1560), probably representing a conflation of {{m|en|huck|t=to crouch, huddle down}} and {{der|en|non|hugga|t=to comfort, console}}, from {{m|non|hugr|t=mind, heart, thought}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*hugiz|t=mind, thought, sense}}, cognate with {{cog|is|hugga|t=to comfort}}, {{cog|ang|hyġe|t=thought}} (whence {{m|en|high|id=thought}} (E

housing.text: From {{inh|en|enm|housynge}}, {{m|enm|housinge}}, from {{m|enm|housen|t=to house, shelter; receive into one's house}}, equivalent to {{af|en|house|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|housing|t=housing}}, {{cog|ofs|hūsinge}} (whence {{cog|stq|Huzenge}}); compare also {{cog|nl|huizing}}, {{m|nl|behuizing|t=housing}}, {{cog|nds|husing}}, {{m|nds|hüsing|t=housing}}, {{cog|de|Behausung|t=hou

horrible.text: First attested in {{inh|en|enm|-}}The American Heritage® Dictionary of the English Language, Fourth Edition (alternately as {{m|enm|horrible}} and {{m|enm|orrible}})'''Dictionary.com Unabridged''' (v 1·1) in 1303'''Online Etymology Dictionary''', © 2001 Douglas Harper: from {{der|en|fro|-}}

imply.text: From {{inh|en|enm|implien}}, {{m|enm|emplien}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|emplier}}, from {{der|en|la|implico|implicare|to infold, involve}}, from {{m|la|in||in}} + {{m|la|plico|plicare|to fold}}. {{doublet|en|employ|implicate}}.

identity.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:ydemptite<ety:bor<frm:identité>:lbor<la:identitās>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|ydemptite}}, from {{der|en|frm|identité}} and its etymon {{der|en|LL.|idemptitās,identitās}}, from {{m|la|idem|t=the same}} + {{m|la|-tās|pos=suffix forming abstract nouns}} as a {{glossary|calque}} of {{der|en|grc|ταὐτότης|t=sameness}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=idemtitẹ̄|pos=n|id=MED21686.5}}</ref><ref>{{

ideology.text: {{bor+|en|fr|idéologie}}, from {{af|fr|idéo-|-logie|nocat=1}} (equivalent to English {{af|en|ideo-|-logy}}). Cognate with, but not derived from, {{m|en|idea}}. Coined 1796 by {{w|Antoine Destutt de Tracy}}.<ref>{{cite-journal |en |last=Kennedy |first=Emmet |url=http://www.jstor.org/pss/2709242 |title=“Ideology” from Destutt De Tracy to Marx |work=Journal of the History of Ideas |volume=40 |number=

immune.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:-<ety:bor<frm:immun<ety:der<la:immūnis>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|frm|immun}}, from {{der|en|la|immūnis||exempt from public service}}, from {{m|la|in-||not}} + {{m|la|mūnus||service}}.

illegal.text: {{bor+|en|fr|illégal}}, from {{der|en|la-med|illegalis}}, from {{der|en|la|legalis}}, {{surf|en|il-|legal|nocap=1}}. In senses relating to immigration, via {{clip|en|illegal alien|nocap=1}} or {{m|en|illegal immigrant}}.

imitate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eym-}}
{{bor+|en|la|imitātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|imitor||to copy, portray, imitate}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|fr|imiter}}.

incentive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂n-}}
From {{bor|en|la-med|incentīvus||that strikes up or sets the tune}}, from {{m|la|incinō||to strike up}}, from {{m|la|in-||in, on}} + {{m|la|canō||to sing}} + {{suf|en|-ive}}. The formation appears to have been influenced by {{m|la|incendō|t=to set on fire}}.

implicit.text: From {{uder|en|frm|implicite}}, from {{uder|en|la|implicitus}}, past participle of {{m|la|implico||to infold, involve, entangle}}; see [[implicate]].

inability.text: From earlier {{m|en|inhability||disqualification for office}}, equivalent to {{af|en|in-<id:inverse>|ability}}. Compare {{cog|frm|inhabilité}}, {{cog|la-med|inhabilitās}}.

immigrant.text: From {{der|en|la|immigrans}}, present active participle of {{m|la|immigrō|immigrāre|t=to migrate into}}, from {{affix|la|in-|t1=into|migrō|alt2=migrāre|t2=to migrate|nocat=1}}.

individual.text:
{{PIE word|en|dwóh₁}}
From {{der|en|la-med|indīviduālis}}, from {{der|en|la|indīviduum|t=an indivisible thing}}, neuter of {{m|la|indīviduus|t=indivisible, undivided}}, from {{m|la|in}} + {{m|la|dīviduus|t=divisible}}, from {{m|la|dīvidō|t=divide}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hād||person, individual}}.

inevitable.text: From {{bor|en|frm|inevitable}}, from {{der|en|la|inēvītābilis|t=unavoidable}}, from {{m|la|in-}} + {{m|la|ēvītābilis|t=avoidable}}, from {{m|la|evito|ēvītāre|t=to avoid}}, from {{m|la|ē-|t=out}} + {{m|la|vito|vītāre|t=to shun}}.

infant.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₂-|id=speak}}
{{inh+|en|enm|infaunt}}, {{bor+|en|la|īnfantem|nocap=1}}, accusative masculine singular of {{m|la|īnfāns}}, nominal use of the adjective meaning 'not able to speak', from {{m|la|īn-||not}} + {{m|la|fāns}}, present participle of {{m|la|for||to speak}}. The verb is from {{der|en|xno|enfanter}}, from the same Latin source. {{dbt|en|infante}}.

indigenous.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}
{{bor+|en|la-lat|indigenus||native, born in a country}}, from {{m|la|indi-}} ({{m|la|indu-}}), an old derivative of {{m|la|in||in}}, {{m|la||gen-}} the root of {{m|la|gignō||give birth to}}, and English {{af|en|-ous}}. Compare {{m|en|indigene}}, {{noncog|grc|ἐνδογενής|t=born in the house}}, and the separately formed {{glossary|piecewise doublet}} {{piecewise doublet|en|

income.text: From {{inh|en|enm|income}}, perhaps continuing (in altered form) {{inh|en|ang|incyme|t=an in-coming, entrance}}, equivalent to {{pre|en|in-|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Íenkúumen|t=income}}, {{cog|fy|ynkommen|t=income}}, {{cog|nl|inkomen}}, {{m|nl|inkomst|t=income, earnings, gainings}}, {{cog|nds-de|Inkumst|t=income}}, {{cog|de|Einkommen}}, {{m|de|Einkunft|t=income, earnings, competence}}, {{cog

indicate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}}
{{bor+|en|la|indicātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|indicō||to point out, indicate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|in-||in, to|id=in}} + {{m|la|dicō||to declare, (originally) to point}}. See also [[diction]] and [[index]].

initial.text:
{{ety|en|etydate=1526|tree=1|:bor|frm:initial<ety:lbor<la:initiālis>>|:lbor|la:initiālis}}
From {{bor|en|frm|initial}} or directly from its {{der|en|la|-}} etymon {{m|la|initiālis|t=of the beginning, incipient, initial}}, from {{m|la|initium|t=a going in, entrance}}, from {{m|la|ineō|inīre|to go into, enter}}, from {{m|la|in|t=in}} + {{m|la|ire|t=to go}}.

ingredient.text: From {{uder|en|frm|ingredient}}, from {{uder|en|la|ingrediens}}, present participle of {{m|la|ingredior||to go or enter into or onto}}.

induce.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|enducen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|indūcō|indūcere|t=lead in, bring in, introduce}}, from {{m|la|in}} + {{m|la|dūcō||lead, conduct}}. Compare also {{m|en|abduce}}, {{m|en|adduce}}, {{m|en|conduce}}, {{m|en|deduce}}, {{m|en|produce}}, {{m|en|reduce}} etc. Doublet of {{m|en|endue}}.

incredible.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱerd-|*dʰeh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|incredible}}, from {{der|en|la|incrēdibilis||that cannot be believed}}, from {{m|la|in-||not}} + {{m|la|crēdibilis||worthy of belief}}, from {{m|la|crēdō||believe}}, equivalent to {{af|en|in-|credible}}.

incidence.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱh₂d-}}
From {{der|en|frm|incidence}}, from {{der|en|la-med|incidentia||a falling upon}}, from {{der|en|la|incidens}}, present participle of {{m|la|incidere||to fall upon}}, from {{m|la|in||on}} + {{m|la|cadere||to fall}}.

insect.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}}
{{bor+|en|frm|insecte}}, from {{der|en|la|īnsectum}}, from {{m|la|īnsectus|t=cut into, cut up, with a notched or divided body}}, from perfect passive participle of {{m|la|īnsecō||to cut into, to cut up}}, from {{m|la|in-}} + {{m|la|secō||to cut}}, from the notion that the insect's body is "cut into" three sections ([[head]], [[thorax]], [[abdomen]]). {{cal|en|grc|ἔντομον|

instrument.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|instrument}}, from {{der|en|fro|instrument}}, from {{der|en|la|īnstrūmentum||an implement, tool}},
From {{suffix|la|īnstruō|t1=build, construct; arrange|mentum||nocat=1}}.

insurance.text:
From the older form ''[[ensurance]]'', see also ''[[assurance]]''.
{{surf|+af|en|insure|-ance}}.

injury.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂yew-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|injurie}}, from {{der|en|xno|injurie}}, from {{der|en|la|iniūria||injustice; wrong; offense}}, from {{m|la|in-||not}} + {{m|la|ius|iūs, iūris|right, law}}. {{doublet|en|injuria}}.

insight.text: From {{inh|en|enm|insight}}, {{m|enm|insiht|t=insight, mental vision, intelligence, understanding}}, equivalent to {{af|en|in-|sight}}. Perhaps continuing {{inh|en|ang|insiht|t=narrative, argument, account}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*insahtiz|t=account, narrative, argument}}. Compare {{cog|fy|ynsjoch|t=insight}}, {{cog|nl|inzicht|t=insight, awareness, view, opinion}}, {{cog|nds-de|Insicht|t=insight}

innovation.text: {{bor+|en|frm|innovation}}, from {{der|en|fro|innovacion}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|innovatio|innovatio, innovationem}}, from {{der|en|la|innovo|innovo, innovatus}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|innovate|-ion}}.

innocent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*neḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|innocent}}, from {{der|en|fro|innocent}}, {{m|fro|inocent}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|innocēns||harmless, inoffensive}}, from {{m|la|in-||not}} + {{m|la|nocēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|noceō||to hurt}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=8980414922}}</ref> {{surf|en|in-<id:inverse><t:not>|nocent<t:harmful; guilty>}}. Displac

initiate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁ey-}}
{{bor+|en|la|initiātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|initiō||to begin, originate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|initium||a beginning}} + {{m|la|-ō|id=denominative|pos=verb-forming suffix}}, from {{m|la|initus||an entrance, coming in, approach}} + {{m|la|-ium}}, from {{m|la|ineō}} + {{

instance.text: {{bor+|en|frm|instance}}, from {{der|en|la|īnstantia||a being near, presence, also perseverance, earnestness, importunity, urgency}}, from {{m|la|īnstāns||urgent}}; see {{m|en|instant}}.

institution.text: From {{inh|en|enm|institucioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|institution}}, from {{der|en|la|institūtiō}}, from {{m|la|instituō||to set up}}, from {{m|la|in-||in, on}} + {{m|la|statuō|t=to set up, establish}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|institute|ion}}.

insult.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sel-}}
The verb is derived from {{der|en|frm|insulter}} (modern {{cog|fr|insulter|t=to insult}}) or its {{glossary|etymon}} {{der|en|la|īnsultō|īnsultō|t=to spring, leap or jump at or upon; to abuse, insult, revile, taunt}}, the {{glossary|frequentative}} form of {{m|la|īnsiliō|t=to bound; to leap in or upon}}, from {{m|la|in-|pos=''prefix meaning ‘in, inside, within’''}} + {{m|

install.text: From {{inh|en|enm|installen}}, from {{der|en|fro|installer}}, from {{der|en|la-med|īnstallō|t=to install, put in place, establish}}, from {{m|la|in-}} + {{m|la|stallum|t=stall}}, from {{der|en|frk|*stall||stall, position, place}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*stallaz|t=place, position}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*stel-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*stAlǝn-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*stAlǝm-|t=stem, trunk}}. Cognate with {{cog|goh|

parts: t2=join, bind together, connect, entwine, interweave
insert.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ser- (bind)}}
From {{der|en|la|insertus}}, past participle of {{m|la|inserō}}, from {{affix|la|in-|serō|t2=join, bind together, connect, entwine, interweave|id1=in|nocat=1}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ser-|t=to bind, put together, to line up|id=bind}}. Compare [[exsert]].

integrate.text: {{etydate|1450's}} as an adjective, {{etydate|1638|nocap=1}} as a verb; from {{inh|en|enm|integrat|integrat(e)|t=intact, whole}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|integrātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|integrō||to make whole, renew, repair, begin again}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}} and {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-f

initiative.text: From {{der|en|fr|initiative}}, from {{der|en|la-med|*initiativus||serving to initiate}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|initio|initiare|t=to begin, to initiate}}, from {{der|en|la|initium||beginning}}, from {{m|la|ineo||enter, begin}}. {{surf|en|initiate|-ive}}.

invest.text:
{{ety|en|id=spend for benefit|:bor|frm:investir<ety:der<la:investio>>|la-med:investire<ety:der<la:investio>>}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|investir}} or {{bor|en|la-med|investire}}, from {{der|en|la|investio||to clothe, cover}}, from {{m|la|in-||in, on}} + {{m|la|vestio||to clothe, dress}}, from {{m|la|vestis||clothing}}; see {{m|en|vest}}. The sense “to spend money etc.” probably via {{der|en|it|i

internal.text: From {{inh|en|enm|[[internall]], [[internalle]]}}, borrowing from {{der|en|la-new|internālis||of or pertaining to the inner part}}, from {{af|la|internus|-ālis|t1=inward, internal|t2=-al|pos2=adjectival suffix|nocat=1}}. {{surf|+suf|en|intern|al}}.

investigate.text: Recorded since circa 1510, a {{bf|en|investigation|nocap=1}} on the basis of {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}, from {{der|en|la|investīgātiō||a searching into}}, from {{m|la|investīgātus}}, the {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|investīgō}}, equivalent to {{af|en|in-|vestigate}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|undersēċan|lit=to search under or

invisible.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|invisible}}, from {{der|en|fro|invisible}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|invīsibilis}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|unġesewenlīċ}}.

Morphologically {{prefix|en|in<id:inverse>|visible}}. {{piecewise doublet|en|unvisible}}.

interval.text: From {{inh|en|enm|interval}}, {{m|enm|intervalle}}, from {{der|en|fro|intervalle}}, {{m|fro|entreval}}, from {{der|en|la|intervallum|t=space between, interval, distance, interval of time, pause, difference; literally, space between two palisades or walls}}, from {{com|la|inter|t1=between|vallum|t2=palisade, wall|nocat=1}}.

intent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}}
Existing since {{inh|en|enm|entente}}, from {{der|en|fro|entent}} or {{m|fro|entente}}, ultimately from {{der|en|la|intentus}}. Modified later in spelling to align more closely with the Latin word. Compare [[intention]].

intense.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tend-|id=stretch}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|intens}}, {{m|enm|intense|t=ardent, fervent; extreme, great, intense}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=intens(e|pos=adj|id=MED23075}}</ref> borrowed from {{der|en|fro|intense}} (modern {{cog|fr|intense}}), or directly from its {{glossary|etymon}} {{der|en|la|intēnsus|t=strained, stretched tight; intense; attentive; violent; (''rare'') eager, i

introduction.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dewk-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|introduccioun}}, {{m|enm|introduccyon}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|introduction}}, itself a borrowing from {{der|en|la|intrōdūctiōnem}}, accusative of {{der|en|la|intrōdūctiō}}, from {{m|la|intrōdūcō}}. {{surf|en|intro-|dūctiō|lang2=la}} or {{suf|en|introduce|tion}}.

intelligence.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:intelligence|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|intelligence}}, from {{der|en|fro|intelligence}}, from {{der|en|la|intelligentia}}, which is most likely from {{af|la|inter-<t:between>|legere<t:to choose, pick out, read>|nocat=1}}. {{dbt|en|intelligentsia}}.

interview.text:
{{ety|en|:uder|fro:entreveue<ety:from<entreveoir>>|tree=1}}
From {{uder|en|fro|entreveue}} ({{cog|fr|entrevue}}), feminine singular past participle of {{m|fro|entrevëoir}}, from {{m|fro|entre-}} + {{m|fro|vëoir||to see}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|inter-|view}}.

intrinsic.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{uder|en|frm|intrinsèque}}, from {{der|en|la|intrīnsecus||on the inside, inwardly}}, from {{m|la|*intrim}}, an assumed adverbial form of {{m|la|inter||within}} + {{m|la|secus||by, on the side}}.

interpret.text: From {{inh|en|enm|interpreten}}, from {{der|en|fro|enterpreter}}, ({{cog|fr|interpréter}}), from {{der|en|la|interpretor||to explain, expound, interpret}}, past participle {{m|la|interpretatus}}, from {{m|la|interpres||an agent, broker, explainer, interpreter, [[negotiator]]}}, from {{m|la|inter||between}} + {{m|la|-pres}}, probably the root of {{m|la|pretium||price}}; {{m|la|-pres}} is probably c

inventory.text: From {{inh|en|enm|inventorie}}, from {{der|en|la-med|inventorium|inventōrium}}, alteration of {{der|en|la-lat|inventārium}}, from {{der|en|la|inveniō||to find out}}.

juice.text:
{{etymon|en|id=liquid|:inh|enm:jus|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|jus}}, {{m|enm|juis}}, from {{der|en|fro|jus}}, {{m|fro|jous}}, from {{der|en|la|ius|jūs|broth, soup, sauce}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*yéwHs}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*yewH-||to mix (of meal preparation)}}. {{doublet|en|jus|ukha}}. In this sense, mostly displaced native {{noncog|enm|sew|t=juice}}, from {{noncog|ang|sēaw|t=juice, sap}} (> {{non

item.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:item}}
From {{inh|en|enm|item}}, from {{der|en|la|item||also; in the same manner}}. The present English meaning derives from a usage in lists, where the first entry would begin {{m|la|in}} {{m|la|primis}} (“firstly”) or ''imprimis'', and the other entries with {{m|la||item|t=also, moreover}}. Later, the members of lists were referred to as "items".

jeans.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|la:Genua}}

In the context of clothing, the term originally denoted a kind of coarse cotton (known more fully as ''Gene(s) [[fustian]]'') that was associated with Genoa. From {{inh|en|enm|maister}}, {{m|enm|mayster}}, {{m|enm|meister|pos=noun}} and {{m|enm|maistren|pos=verb}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mǣster}}, {{m|ang|mæġster}}, {{m|ang|mæġester}}, {{m|ang|mæġister}}, {{m|ang|magister|t=master}}, from {{der|en|la|magister|t=chief, teacher, leader}}, from {{der|en|itc-ola|magester}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*méǵh₂s}} (as in

material.text: From {{inh|en|enm|material|}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|māteriālis}}, from {{der|en|la|māteria||wood, material, substance}}, from {{m|la|māter||mother}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|andweorc|andweorc, andwork|material, matter}} (from {{ncog|ang|andweorc||matter, substance, material}}). {{doublet|en|materiel}}.

mathematics.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)|*dʰeh₁-}}
First use appears c. 1545. From {{suffix|en|mathematic|pos1=noun|ics}},<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref> from {{inh|en|enm|mathematique}}, {{m|enm|methametik}}, {{m|enm|matematik}}, {{m|enm|matamatik}}, from {{der|en|fro|mathematique}}, from {{der|en|la|mathēmatica||mathematics}}, from {{der|en|grc|μαθηματικός||on the matter of that which is lea

means.text: From {{m|en|mean||method or course of action used to achieve some result}}. Compare {{cog|fr|moyens}}, {{cog|de|Mittel}}.

medal.text: From {{inh|en|enm}}, from {{der|en|frm|medaille}}, {{m|frm|medale}}, from {{der|en|it|medaglia}} (originally "half a [[denarius]]"), from {{der|en|la-eme|medālia}}, feminine derived via dissimilation (/dj–lj/ > /d–lj/) from {{m|la|mediālia}}, neuter plural of {{der|en|la-lat|mediālis|t=middle|pos=adj}}, from {{der|en|la-cla|medius}}.

media.text:
{{lbor|en|la|media}}, the feminine nominative of {{m|la|medius|t=middle|pos=a}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*meðjos}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*médʰyos||between}}. In the sense of a unit of dry measure, via {{bor|en|es|media}}. {{doublet|en|medium|medio|mediate}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmiː.di.ə/|ref1=https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/media|/ˈmɛ.di.ə/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en

mediate.text: The {{glossary|adjective}} is {{etydate|1440s|nocap=1}} in {{w|Middle English}}, the {{glossary|verb}} in 1538; from {{inh|en|enm|mediat|mediat(e)|t=intermediate; intercessory}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la-lat|mediātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|mediō||to divide in the middle; ({{ng|in Medieval Latin}}) to be in the middle, be or become between, m

medical.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:médical|tree=1}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|médical}}, from {{der|en|la-med|medicālis}}, from {{der|en|la|medicus}}. Replaced {{cog|ang|lǣċe||doctor (physician)}}, which is cognate with {{cog|is|læknir||doctor}}.

medicine.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|medicin}}, from {{der|en|frm|medicine}}, from {{der|en|fro|medecine}}, from {{der|en|la|medicīna||the healing art, medicine, a physician's shop, a remedy, medicine}}, feminine of {{m|la|medicīnus||of or belonging to physic or surgery, or to a physician or surgeon}}, from {{m|la|medicus||a physician, surgeon}}. The extended sense of "Indigenous magic" is

meeting.text:
{{ety|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:meeting<alt:meeting, meting><ety:inh<ang:mēting<id:meeting>><ang:ġemēting>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|meeting}}, {{m|enm|meting}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mēting}}, {{m|ang|ġemēting|t=meeting, assembly, association, society}}, equivalent to {{af|en|meet|-ing|id2=gerund noun}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|moeting|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|nl|ontmoeting|t=meeting, encounter}}, {{cog|gml|

mess.text:
Perhaps a corruption of {{der|en|enm|mesh|t=mash}}, compare {{m|en|muss}}, or derived from Etymology 2 "mixed foods, as for animals". Compare also {{cog|ang|mes|t=dung, excrement}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|disorder}} A [[thing]] or group of [[thing]]s in a [[disagreeable]], [[disorganised]], or [[dirty]] [[state]]; hence a bad [[situation]].
#* '''2006 Feb. 3''', Graham Linehan

metal.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:metal|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|metal}}, a borrowing from {{der|en|fro|metal}}, from {{der|en|la|metallum||metal, mine, quarry, mineral}}, itself a borrowing from {{der|en|grc|μέταλλον||mine, quarry, metal}}.

metaphor.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}}
From {{der|en|frm|métaphore}}, from {{der|en|la|metaphora}}, from {{der|en|grc|μεταφορά}}, from {{m|grc|μεταφέρω||to transfer, apply}}, from {{m|grc|μετά||with, across, after}} + {{m|grc|φέρω||to bear, carry}}.

midnight.text: From {{inh|en|enm|midnight}}, from {{inh|en|ang|midniht}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*midjanahts|t=midnight}}, equivalent to {{prefix|en|mid-|night}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Midnoacht|t=midnight}}, {{cog|goh|mittinaht|t=midnight}}, {{cog|da|midnat|t=midnight}}, {{cog|sv|midnatt|t=midnight}}, {{cog|is|miðnætti|t=midnight}}. Compare also {{cog|stq|Middernoacht|t=midnight}}, {{cog|nl|middernacht|t=midnig

migrate.text: {{etydate|1623}}; {{bor+|en|la|migrātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|migrō||to migrate, change, transport}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}.

minority.text: From Late {{inh|en|enm|minoritie}}, from {{der|en|frm|minorité}}, and its source {{der|en|la-lat|minōritās}}, from {{der|en|la|minor}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|minor|ity}}.

miracle.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)mey-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|miracle}}, from {{der|en|fro|miracle}}, from {{der|en|la|mīrāculum||object of wonder}}, from {{m|la|mīror||to wonder at}}, from {{m|la|mīrus||wonderful}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)meyh₂-|t=to smile, to be astonished}}. {{doublet|en|milagro|miraculum}}. Partially displaced native {{m|en|wonder}}, from {{ncog|ang|wundor||miracle, wonder}}.

missile.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}}
From {{bor|en|la|missile||thrown weapon, projectile}}, neuter of {{m|la|missilis||throwable, capable of being thrown}}, from {{m|la|mittere||to send}}.  From 1611.  Compare {{cog|frm|missile|t=projectile}}, from 1636. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|wifer}}.

mixture.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*meyḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|misture}}, from {{der|en|la|mixtūra||a mixing}}, from {{m|la|mixtus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|misceō||mix}}; compare [[mix]].

mobile.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|mōbilis|t=easy to be moved, moveable}}, from {{m|la|moveō|t=move}}. The video-gaming sense was coined by {{w|Richard Bartle}} to describe [[NPC]]s or creatures capable of moving "under their own power" in the 1978 video game ''{{w|MUD1|Multi-User Dungeon}}''. Bartle retracted an earlier claim of his that

moderate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|moderat|alt=moderat(e)||moderate, temperate}}, {{bor+|en|la|moderātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|moderor||to regulate, to restrain, to moderate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la||moder-}}, {{m|la||modes-}}, a stem appearing also in {{m|la|modestus||mo

modern.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*med-}}
From {{der|en|frm|moderne}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|modernus}}; from {{der|en|la|modo||just now}}, originally ablative of {{m|la|modus||measure}}; hence, by measure, "just now". See also {{m|en|mode}}.

modify.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|modifien}}, from {{der|en|frm|modifier}}, from {{der|en|la|modificare||to limit, control, regulate, deponent}}, from {{m|la|modificari||to measure off, set bound to, moderate}}, from {{m|la|modus||measure}} + {{m|la|facere||to make}}; see {{m|en|mode}}.
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}

monitor.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men-|id=think}}
From {{uder|en|la|monitor||warner}}, from perfect passive participle {{m|la|monitus||warning}}, from verb {{m|la|monere||to warn, admonish, remind}}.  Warship sense is from {{w|USS Monitor|USS ''Monitor''}}, the first ship of this type.

monster.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:monstre|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|monstre}}, from {{der|en|fro|monstre}}, {{m|fro|mostre}}, {{m|fro|moustre}}, from {{der|en|la|mōnstrum}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|fīfel}} and {{noncog|ang|þyrs}}.

motion.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-}}
{{inh+|en|enm|mocioun}}, {{m|enm|mocion}}, from {{der|en|xno|motion}}, {{der|en|frm|motion}}, and their {{glossary|etymon}} {{der|en|la|mōtiō|t=movement, motion}}, related to {{m|la|moveo|movēre}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-||to move}}.

mountain.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men-|id=stand out}}
From {{inh|en|enm|mountayne}}, {{m|enm|mountain}}, {{m|enm|montaigne}}, from {{der|en|xno|montaigne|muntaine}}, {{m|fro|montaigne|muntaigne}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|montānia}}, a collective based on {{der|en|la|mōns|montem|t=mountain}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*monti}} (compare {{cog|cy|mynydd||mountain}}, {{cog|sq|mat||bank, shore}}, {{cog|ae|𐬨𐬀𐬙𐬌|t=promontory}

museum.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}}
From {{der|en|la|mūsēum|t=library, study}}, from {{der|en|grc|Μουσεῖον}}, shrine of the [[Muse]]s ({{m|grc|Μοῦσα}}). {{doublet|en|mosaic}}.

musical.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|musical}}, from {{der|en|fro|}}, from {{der|en|la-med|mūsicālis}}, from {{der|en|la|mūsica|t=music}} {{suffix|la||ālis|pos2=suffix forming adjectives|nocat=1}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|music|al}}.

myth.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|grc:μῦθος}}
From {{bor|en|grc|μῦθος||word, humour, companion, speech, account, rumour, fable}}. Attested in English since 1830. {{doublet|en|mythos}}.

natural.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵenh₁-}}
{{inh+|en|enm|natural}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|natural}}, {{m|fro|naturel}}, from {{der|en|la|nātūrālis}}, from {{m|la|nātus}}, the perfect participle of {{m|la|nāscor|t=be born|pos=verb}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|ġecynde}}. {{surf|+suf|en|nature|al|alt1=natur(e)}}.

neat.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|nete}}, {{m|enm|net}}, {{m|enm|nette}}, from {{der|en|xno|neit|t=good, desirable, clean}}, a variant of {{der|en|fro|net}}, {{m|fro|nette|t=clean, clear, pure}}, from {{der|en|la|nitidus|t=gleaming}}, derived from {{m|la|niteo|nitēre|t=to shine}}. {{doublet|en|net|id1=remaining after deductions|nitid}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|nett|t=nice, kind}}. Compare also {{m|en|nait}}.

====A

negative.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁eǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|negative}}, {{m|enm|negatif}}, from {{der|en|fro|negatif}}, from {{der|en|la|negātīvus|t=that denies, negative}}, from {{m|la|negāre|t=to deny}}; see {{m|la|negate}}.

nervous.text:
{{multiple images
|direction = vertical
|image1 = Illustrated lectures on ambulance work (1888) (14761427691).jpg
|caption1 = A diagram of the [[human#Adjective|human]] [[nervous system]] ''({{senseno|en|affecting nerves}})''{{ref|group=n|name=n1|From {{cite-book|author=R. Lawton Roberts|chapter=Lecture I|title=Illustrated Lectures on Ambulance Work|edition=3rd|location=London|publisher=H. K. Lewi

network.text:
{{etymon|en|id=fabric|net<id:mesh>|work<id:employment>|tree=1}}
From {{com|en|net|work}}; the nonliteral sense and its subsenses are extended from the literal sense; they are now the dominant senses. Cognate with {{cog|de|Netzwerk}}.

nevertheless.text: From {{inh|en|enm|nevertheles}}, {{m|enm|never-þe-les}}, {{m|enm|nevere-þe-lesse}}. {{surf|+com|en|never|the|less|t1=not at all}}; compare {{m|en|never the wiser}}.

noise.text: From {{inh|en|enm|noyse}}, {{m|enm|noise}}, from {{der|en|fro|noise|t=a dispute, wrangle, strife, noise}}, of uncertain origin. According to some, from {{der|en|la|nausia}}, {{m|la|nausea|t=disgust, nausea}}; according to others, from {{der|en|la|noxia|t=hurt, harm, damage, injury}}; but neither explanation is satisfactory in regard to either form or sense. Potentially a reduced form of {{der|en|f

notion.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵneh₃-}}
From {{bor|en|la|nōtiō||a becoming acquainted, a taking cognizance, an examination, an investigation, a conception, idea, notion}}, from {{m|la|nōscō||to know}}. Compare {{cog|fr|notion}}. See {{m|en|know}}.

nowhere.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|nowher}}, from {{inh|en|ang|nōhwēr}}, {{m|ang|nāhwǣr}}, from {{m|ang|nā-}} + {{m|ang|hwǣr}}. {{surf|en|no|where}}.

Adjective usage is taken from phrases like ''nowhere on the map'' (signifying the location was too small or too insignificant to be listed), ''nowhere you want to be'', etc.

nuclear.text: From {{der|en|la|nū̆cleus}}, a contraction of the adjective {{m|la|nuculeus}}, masculine of feminine {{m|la|nuculea|t=pertaining to a small nut}} from {{m|la|nucula}} + adjectival suffix {{m|la|[[-eus]], -ea, -eum}}. The {{cog|la|nucula}} + {{m|la|-āris}} adds up to {{m|la|nuculāris}}, a term that in English becomes {{m|en|nucular}}; the {{cog|la|nuculea}} + {{m|la|-āris}}, becomes {{cog|la|nucule

numerous.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*nem-|id=distribute}}
From {{inh|en|enm|numerous}} from {{der|en|la|numerōsus||numerous, abundant; harmonious}}, from {{m|la|numerus||number}}. {{doublet|en|numerose}}. Analyzeable as {{suffix|en|numero-|-ous}}.

object.text:
{{ety|en|id=thing|:der|fro:object<ety:inh<la-med:obiectum>>|tree=1}}

From {{der|en|fro|object}}, from {{der|en|la-med|obiectum||object|lit=thrown against}}, from {{m|la|obiectus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|obiciō||to throw against}}, from {{prefix|en|ob|gloss1=against|sort=ject}} {{m|la|iaciō||to throw}}, as a calque of {{der|en|grc|ἀντικείμενον}}. {{doublet|en|objectum|objet}}.

objective.text: From {{inh|en|enm|obgectyf}}, from {{der|en|frm|objectif}} and its etymon {{der|en|la-med|obiectīvus}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=9609347108}}</ref> {{surf|+suf|en|object|ive}}.

obligation.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leyǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|obligacioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|obligacion}}, from {{der|en|la|obligatio|obligatio, obligationem}}, from {{m|la|obligatum}} (past participle of {{m|la|obligare}}), from {{m|la|ob-||to}} + {{m|la|ligare||to bind}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leyǵ-||to bind}}.

observation.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|observacion}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|observacion}}. Also a borrowing from {{der|en|fr|observation}} and a {{learned borrowing|en|la|observatio|observātiō(n-)|nocap=1}}.
Morphologically {{suffix|en|observe|ation}}.

observe.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ser- (guard)}}
From {{der|en|frm|observer}}, from {{der|en|fro|observer}}, from {{der|en|la|observō||to watch}}, from {{m|la|ob-||before}} + {{m|la|servō||to keep}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ser-||to guard}}. Cognate with {{cog|got|𐍃𐌰𐍂𐍅𐌰||weapons, armour}}, {{cog|ang|searu||device}}.

obtain.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ten-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|obteinen}}, from {{der|en|xno|obtenir}}, {{m|fro|optiner}} et al., and {{der|en|frm|obtenir}}, from {{der|en|la|obtinēre||to gain, achieve, succeed, possess}}, from {{m|la|ob-}} + {{m|la|tenere|tenēre|to hold}}.

obvious.text: 16th century, from {{af|en|la:obvius<t:being in the way so as to meet, meeting, easy to access, at hand, ready, obvious>|-ous}}, from {{m|la|ob-||before}} + {{m|la|via||way}}.<ref>{{R:Century|page=4070|column=1|year=1895}}</ref>

occasion.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱh₂d-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|occasioun}}, from {{der|en|frm|occasion}}, from {{der|en|fro|occasiun}}, from {{der|en|la|occāsiō|occāsiōnem}}, noun of action from perfect passive participle {{m|la|occāsus}}, from verb {{m|la|occidō}}, from prefix {{m|la|ob-||down", "away}} + verb {{m|la|cadō||fall}}.

occupation.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}}
From {{inh|en|enm|occupacioun}}, borrowed from {{der|en|frm|occupacion}}, {{m|frm|occupation}}, from {{der|en|la|occupātiō}}, {{m|la|occupātiōnis}}, from {{m|la|occupo|occupō|occupy, seize}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize||to seize, grab}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=3113593753}}</ref> {{surf|en|occupy|-ation}}.

occupy.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}}
From {{inh|en|enm|occupien}}, {{m|enm|occupyen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|occuper}}, from {{der|en|la|occupō|occupāre|t=to take possession of, seize, occupy, take up, employ}}, from {{m|la|ob||to, on}} + {{m|la|capiō||to take}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kap-<id:seize>||to seize, grab}}. {{doublet|en|occupate}}, now obsolete.

occur.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-}}
Originally "meet (in argument)", borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|occurrer}}, from {{der|en|la|occurrō||run to meet, run against, befall, present itself}} from prefix {{m|la|ob-||against}} + verb {{m|la|currō||run, hurry, move}}.

origins.term: t=odd (not even); leftover after division into pairs

odd.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|odde}}, {{m|enm|od|t=odd (not even); leftover after division into pairs}}, from {{der|en|non|oddi|t=odd, third or additional number; triangle}}, from {{m|non|oddr|t=point of a weapon}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*uzdaz|t=point}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wes-|t=to stick, prick, pierce, sting}} + {{m|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-|t=to set, place}}.

Cognate to {{cog|is|oddi|t=triangle, point of land,

offend.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷʰen-}}
From {{uder|en|frm|offendre}}, from {{uder|en|la|offendō||strike, blunder, commit an offense}}, from {{m|la|ob-||against}} + {{m|la|*fendō||strike}}.

offset.text: From {{pre|en|off|set}}, used to construct the noun form of the verb {{m|en|set off|to set off}}. Compare {{cog|enm|ofsetten|t=to encumber, harass, beset, besiege}}, from {{cog|ang|ofsettan|t=to press, oppress, overwhelm, crush}}.

ongoing.text: From {{affix|en|on|going}}, related to the phrasal verb {{m|en|go on}}.

opening.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|openynge}}, {{m|enm|openande}}, {{m|enm|openand}}, from {{inh|en|ang|openiende}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*opanōndī}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*upanōndz}}, present participle of {{m|ang|*upanōną|t=to open}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|open|-ing|id2=participial}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|iepenjend}}, {{cog|nl|openend}}, {{cog|de|öffnend}}, {{cog|sv|öppnande}}, {{cog|is|opnandi}}.

====Verb=

opinion.text: From [[Wikipedia:English language|English]] {{suf|en|opine|ion}}, from {{der|en|enm|opinion}}, {{m|enm|opinioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|frm|opinion}}<!--note, have to specify a language here to avoid a self-link-->, from {{der|en|la|opīniō}}, from {{m|la|opīnor||to opine}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|wēna}}.

opponent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tḱey-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|oppōnēns||opposing}}, present active participle of {{m|la|oppōnō||to oppose}}.

oppose.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*tḱey-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|opposen}}, from {{der|en|fro|opposer}}, from {{der|en|la|ob||before, against}} + {{der|en|la-med|pono||to put}}, taking the place of {{der|en|la|oppono|opponere|to oppose}}.

opposite.text: {{inh+|en|enm|opposit}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|oposite}}, from {{uder|en|la|oppositus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|oppōnō||to oppose}}. Compare {{m|en|oppose}}.

option.text: From {{der|en|fr|option}}, from {{der|en|la|optiō|t=choice; option; act of choosing}}, from {{m|la|optō|t=to choose, select}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|opt|-ion}}.

oral.text:
{{PIE word|en|h₁óh₃s}}

Early 17th century borrowing from {{bor|en|la-lat|ōrālis}}, from {{af|la|ōs|-ālis|t1=the mouth|t2=-al|pos2=adjectival suffix|nocat=1}}.

ordinary.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}
From {{der|en|xno|ordenarie}}, {{m|fro|ordenaire}} et al., {{der|en|frm|ordinaire}}, and their source, {{der|en|la-med|ordinarius}}, noun use of {{der|en|la|ōrdinārius||regular, orderly}}, from {{m|la|ordo|ōrdō|order}}.

organ.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:organe|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|organe}}, from {{der|en|fro|organe}} and {{der|en|ang|organ}}, both from {{der|en|la|organum}}, from {{der|en|grc|ὄργανον||an instrument, implement, tool, also an organ of sense or apprehension, an organ of the body, also a musical instrument, an organ}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*werǵ-}}. {{doublet|en|organon|organum|orgue}}.

origin.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃er-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|origine}}, {{m|enm|origyne}} (early 15th c.), from {{der|en|la|origo|orīgō, orīginem|t=beginning, source, birth, origin}}, derived from {{m|la|orior||t=to rise}}. Possibly borrowed into English via {{der|en|frm|origine}}, though this attested slightly later. {{doublet|en|origo}} and related with {{m|en|orient}}. {{displaced|ang|frymþ}}.

original.text: From {{inh|en|enm|original}}, from {{der|en|fro|original}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|orīginālis|t=primitive, original}}, from {{der|en|la|orīgō|t=beginning, source, origin}}, equivalent to {{af|en|origin|-al}}; see [[origin]].

otherwise.text: From {{inh|en|enm|otherwise}}, {{m|enm|othre wise}}, from {{inh|en|ang|on ōþre wīsan|lit=in (on) other/different manner}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|other|wise}}. Compare {{cog|fy|yn oarwei|t=otherwise}}, {{cog|is|öðruvísi|t=different}}.

overall.text: From {{inh|en|enm|overall}}, {{m|enm|overal}}, from {{der|en|ang|ofer eall}}, {{m|ang|ofer ealle|t=over all}}, equivalent to {{compound|en|over|all}}. Compare {{cog|stq|oural}}, {{m|stq|uural||everywhere}}, {{cog|fy|oeral||everywhere}}, {{cog|nl|overal||everywhere}}, {{cog|nds-de|overall}}, {{m|nds-de|överall||everywhere; all over}}, {{cog|de|überall||all over; everywhere}}, {{cog|da|overalt||ever

overcome.text: {{inh+|en|enm|overcomen}}, {{inh+|en|ang|ofercuman<t:to overcome, subdue, compel, conquer, obtain, attain, reach, overtake>|nocap=1}}. {{surf|en|over-|come}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|overkomen}}, {{cog|de|überkommen}}, {{cog|da|overkomme}}, {{cog|sv|överkomma}}.

oversee.text: From {{inh|en|enm|overseen}}, {{m|enm|ouverseen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ofersēon|t=to observe, oversee; to overlook, neglect}}, equivalent to {{af|en|over-|see}}.

package.text: Equivalent to {{suffix|en|pack|-age}}. Possibly influenced by Anglo-{{uder|en|la|paccagium}} or {{uder|en|fro|pacquage}}.

palace.text: From {{inh|en|enm|paleys}}, from {{der|en|fro|palais}}, which comes from {{der|en|la|palātium}}, from {{m|la|Palātium}}, in reference to the [[Palatine]] ({{w|Palatine Hill}}), one of the seven hills of Rome, where the aristocracy of the Roman [[republic|Republic]]—and later, Roman emperors—built large, splendid residences.<ref>{{w|Palatine#Derivative_terms}}</ref><ref>https://web.archive.org/web/

panel.text: From {{inh|en|enm|panel|t=piece of cloth, saddle pad, pane of glass, piece of ice, part, division, jury list, jury members}}, from {{der|en|xno|panel}}, {{m|fro|panelle|t=piece of cloth, saddle cushion}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*pannellus}}, diminutive of {{der|en|la|pannus|t=cloth, rag, garment}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peh₂n-||fabric}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|fana|t=a piece of cloth, patch, banner

origins.term: by the seat of one's pants

pants.text:
{{etymon|en|pantaloons<id:garment>|id=garment|tree=1}}
Shortened from {{m|en|pantaloons||trousers}}: borrowed from {{der|en|fr|pantalon}}, itself derived from {{der|en|it|Pantalone}}, one of the principal characters found in ''commedia dell'arte'', who wore tight trousers. {{doublet|en|pantsu}}. The verb is from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=4578744069}}</ref>

parade.text: From {{bor|en|fr|parade||an [[ostentatious]] [[display]], a [[military]] [[display]]}}, from {{m|fr|parer||to [[beautify]], [[prepare]], [[take pride]] in}} + {{m|en|-ade}} probably under influence from earlier {{der|en|it|parata||[[preparation]], a [[military parade]], an [[ostentatious]] [[display]]}} and {{der|en|la|magnō}} {{m|la|parātū||with [[great]] [[preparation]]}}. Various senses similar

parallel.text: From {{bor|en|frm|parallèle}} and its etymon {{bor|en|la|parallēlus,parallēlos}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.'', ''adj.'', and ''adv.''|noformat=1|id=8954533823}}</ref> The verb is from the noun.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=5087416642}}</ref> See also [[para-]] and [[allo-]].

park.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:park|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|park}}, from {{der|en|fro|parc|t=livestock pen}}, from {{der|en|la-med|parcus}}, {{m|la|parricus}}, from {{der|en|frk|*parruk|*parrik|t=enclosure, pen, fence}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|perk|t=enclosure; flowerbed}}, {{cog|goh|pfarrih}}, {{m|goh|pferrih|t=enclosure, pen}}, {{cog|ang|pearroc|t=enclosure}} (whence modern {{cog|en|paddock}}), {{cog|non|p

parliament.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:parlement|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|parlement}}, from {{der|en|xno|parliament}}, {{m|fro|parlement}}, {{m|fro|parliment}} and {{der|en|fro|parlement||[[discussion]], [[meeting]], [[negotiation]]; [[assembly]], [[council]]}}, from {{m|fro|parler||to [[speak]]}} + {{m|fro|-ment||{{l|en|-ment}}|pos=suffix forming nouns from verbs, usually indicating an action or state resulting fro

partial.text: From {{inh|en|enm|partiall}}, {{m|enm|parcial}}, from {{der|en|fro|parcial|t=biased or particular}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|partiālis|t=of or pertaining to a [[part]]}}, from {{der|en|la|pars|t=part}}.

partner.text: From {{inh|en|enm|partener}}, {{m|enm|partiner}}, alteration (due to {{cog|enm|part}}) of {{cog|enm|parcener}}, from {{der|en|fro|parçonier}}, {{m|fro|parçonneour|t=joint heir}} from {{m|fro|parçon|t=partition}}, from {{der|en|la|partītiōnem}}, singular accusative of {{m|la|partītiō|t=portion}}. The word may also represent {{cog|fro|part tenour|t=part holder}}. Compare also {{noncog|enm|partifere|

passive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|passyf}}, {{m|enm|passyve}}, from {{der|en|frm|-}}, {{der|en|fr|passif}}, from {{der|en|la|passivus||serving to express the suffering of an action; in late Latin literally capable of suffering or feeling}}, from {{m|la|passus}}, past participle of {{m|la|patior|pati|to suffer}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peh₁-||to hurt}}; compare {{m|en|patient}

patch.text: From {{inh|en|enm|pacche|patche}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Perhaps an alteration of earlier {{cog|enm|placche|t=patch, spot, piece of cloth}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*plæċċ}}, {{m|ang|*pleċċ|t=a spot, mark, patch}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*plakkju}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*plakjō|t=spot, stain}}. For the loss of ''l'' compare {{m|en|pat}} from {{noncog|enm|platten}}. Germanic cognates would then i

patrol.text: From {{bor|en|fr|patrouille}}, from {{der|en|fro|patrouille}}, {{m|fro|patouille|t=a night-watch|lit=a tramping about}}, from {{m|fro|patrouiller}}, {{m|fro|patouiller}}, {{m|fro|patoiller|t=to paddle or pudder in water, dabble with the feet, begrime, besmear}}, from {{m|fro|patte}}, {{m|fro|pate|t=paw, foot of an animal}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*patta||paw, foot}}, from {{der|en|frk|*patta|t=paw,

pattern.text: From earlier {{m|en|patten}}, {{m|en|paterne}}, from {{inh|en|enm|patron||patron; example}}, from {{der|en|fro|patron}}, from {{der|en|la-med|patrōnus||patron}}. {{doublet|en|padrone|patron|Patronus|patroon}}.

peer.text:
{{etymon|en|id=look|:inh|enm:peren<id:peer><ety:inh<ang:*pȳran>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|peren}}, {{m|enm|pyren}}, {{m|enm|piren|t=to peer, gaze}}, perhaps from {{inh|en|ang|*pȳran|t=to look, peer}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pūrijan|t=to look}}, related to {{cog|stq|pierje|t=to look}}, {{cog|nds-nl|piren|t=to look}}, {{cog|vls|pieren|t=to look with narrowed eyes, squint at}}, {{cog|nl|pieren|t=to

pence.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|enm:peny<alt:penies>|tree=1}}
14th century contraction of {{m|enm|penies||pennies}}, collective plural of {{m|enm|penny}}.<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref>

penny.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:peny|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|peny}}, from {{inh|en|ang|peniġ}}, {{m|ang|penniġ}}, {{m|ang|penning|t=penny}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*panning}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*panningaz}}, of uncertain origin (see that page for theories). {{doublet|en|pfennig|fening}}.

perceive.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|perceyven}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|percevoir}}, {{m|fro|perceveir}}, from {{der|en|la|percipiō}}, past participle {{m|la|perceptus||take hold of, obtain, receive, observe}}, from {{m|la|per||by, through}} + {{m|la|capiō||to take}}; see {{m|en|capable}}. Compare {{m|en|conceive}}, {{m|en|deceive}}, {{m|en|receive}}.

percentage.text: From {{m|en|percent}}, from {{der|en|la|per centum||for every hundred}}, + {{af|en|-age|pos1=suffix indicating a rate}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=3947178937}}</ref>

perception.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|percepcioun}}, from {{der|en|frm|percepcion}}, from {{der|en|la|perceptiō||a receiving or collecting, perception, comprehension}}, from {{m|la|perceptus||perceived, observed}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|percipiō||to perceive, observe}}; see [[perceive]].

perfect.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|perfit}}, from {{der|en|fro|parfit}} (modern: {{m|fr|parfait}}), from {{der|en|la|perfectus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|[[perficio|perficere]]||to finish}}, from {{m|la|per-||through, thorough}} + {{m|la|[[facio|facere]]||to do, to make}}. The spelling was modified in the 15th century to conform to its Latin etymon. {{doublet|en|parfait|per

period.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:periode<ety:bor<frm:periode<ety:bor<la-med:periodus>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|enm|periode}}, from {{der|en|frm|periode}}, from {{der|en|la-med|periodus}}, from {{der|en|grc|περίοδος||circuit, orbit, a recurring interval of time, path around}}, from {{m|grc|περι-||around}} + {{m|grc|ὁδός||way}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|tide||interval, period, season}}, from {{cog|ang|tīd||time

perspective.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|perspective|perspective, perspectif}}, attested since 1381, from {{der|en|fro|-}} or {{der|en|frm|-}}, from the first word of the {{der|en|la-med|perspectiva|perspectiva ars|science of optics}}, the feminine of {{der|en|la|perspectivus||of sight, optical}}, from {{m|la|perspectus}}, the past participle of {{m|la|perspicere||to inspect, look through}}, i

pet.text: Originally northern dialectal, from {{bor|en|sco|pet|t=an animal that has been tamed and is kept as a pet; a darling or favourite; a petted or spoiled child}}, probably from {{der|en|gd|peata|t=pet, tamed animal, spoiled child}}, from {{der|en|mga|petta}}, {{m|mga|peta|t=pet, lap-dog}}, of {{unc|en|title=uncertain}} origin, possibly from a pre-Indo-European {{der|en|qfa-sub}}.<ref>{{R:sga:Schrijve

phenomenon.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|la-lat:phaenomenon|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|la-lat|phaenomenon|t=appearance}}, from {{der|en|grc|φαινόμενον|t=thing appearing to view}}, neuter present middle participle of {{m|grc|φαίνω|t=I show}}.

physician.text: From {{inh|en|enm|fisicien|}}, from {{der|en|fro|fisicïen||physician}} (modern {{cog|fr|physicien||physicist}}), from {{m|fro|fisique||art of healing}}, from {{der|en|la|physica||natural science}}, from {{der|en|grc|[[φυσική]] [[ἐπιστήμη]]||knowledge of nature}}, from {{m|grc|φυσικός||pertaining to nature}}. Displaced native {{ncog|enm|leche|læche, leche}}, archaic {{m+|en|leech|id=physician|gloss

pillow.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|pilwe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|pyle}}, {{m|ang|pylu||pillow}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pulwī|t=pillow}}, from {{der|en|la|pulvīnus|t=cushion}}, derived from {{m|la|pulvis|t=dust}}, for the filler of a pillow. {{doublet|en|pulvinus}}.

Cognate with {{cog|stq|Peel||pillow}}, {{cog|gsw|Pfulme||pillow}}, {{cog|nl|peluw||a long, narrow pillow}}, {{cog|de|Pfühl||a big and soft pillow}}, {{c
