From {{inh|en|enm|picche}}, {{m|enm|piche}}, {{m|enm|pich}}, from {{inh|en|ang|piċ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pik}}, from {{der|en|la|pix}}. Cognate with {{cog|grc|πίσσα||pitch, tar}}, {{cog|la|pīnus||pine}}. More at {{m|en|pine}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Pik|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|nl|pek|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|nds-de|Pick|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|de|Pech|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|

plant.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:plante<ety:inh<ang:plante>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|plante}}, from {{inh|en|ang|plante||young tree or shrub, herb newly planted}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*plantu}}, from {{der|en|la|planta||sprout, shoot, cutting}}. Broader sense of "any vegetable life, vegetation generally" is from {{cog|fro|plante}}. {{doublet|en|clan}} (borrowed through Celtic languages) and {{doublet|en|pla

plastic.text:
{{etymon|en|:der|la:plasticus|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|la|plasticus||of molding}}, from {{der|en|grc|πλαστικός|}}, from {{m|grc|πλάσσω|t=to mold, form}}. {{doublet|en|plastique}}.

plead.text: From {{inh|en|enm|pleden}}, {{m|enm|plaiden}}, from {{der|en|fro|plaider||to plead, offer a plea}}, from {{m|fro|plait}}, from {{der|en|la-med|placitum||a decree, sentence, suit, plea, etc.", in Classical {{der|en|la|-}}, "an opinion, determination, prescription, order; literally, that which is pleasing, pleasure}}, neuter of {{m|la|placitus}}, past participle of {{m|la|placeō||to please}}. Cognat

pleasant.text: From {{inh|en|enm|plesaunte}}, from {{der|en|fro|plaisant}}. {{surf|en|please|-ant}}. Related to {{cog|nl|plezant||full of fun or pleasure}}. Partly displaced {{ncog|ang|wynsum}}, which became {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|winsome}}.

pleasure.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-}}
From Early Modern English {{m|en|pleasur}}, {{m|en|plesur}}, alteration (with ending accommodated to {{af|en|-ure|nocat=1}}) of {{inh|en|enm|plaisir||pleasure}}, from {{der|en|fro|plesir}}, {{m|fro|plaisir||to please}}, infinitive used as a noun, conjugated form of {{m|fro|plaisir}} or {{m|fro|plaire}}, from {{der|en|la|placeō|t=to please, to seem good}}, from the {{der

plot.text: From {{inh|en|enm|plot}}, {{m|enm|plotte}}, from late {{inh|en|ang|plot|t=a plot of ground}}, of {{unc|en|title=uncertain}} origin. Perhaps from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*plataz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*platjaz|t=a patch}}; or alternatively, perhaps from a rebracketing of {{m+|ang|landsplott|land-splott|t=small portion, or plot, of ground}} taken as {{m|ang||landes-plot|t=plot of land}}. Compare {{cog|gml|plet|t=p

plug.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|nl:plug}}
From {{bor|en|nl|plug}}, from {{der|en|dum|plugge|t=peg, plug}}, from {{der|en|odt|*pluggi}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*plugi}}. Further origin {{unk|en|title=unknown}}. Possibly from {{der|en|gem-pro|*plugjaz}}, but the word seems originally restricted to northern continental [[West Germanic]].  Perhaps ultimately from the same source as {{cog|nl|plag|t=cut-out sod}}, itself

pocket.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:pocket<ety:bor<xno:pochete<alt:poket>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|pocket||bag, sack}}, from {{der|en|xno|fro|poket}}, {{der|en|fro-nor|poquet}}, {{m|fro|poquete}}, diminutive of {{m|fro|poque}}, {{m|fro|poke||bag, sack}} (compare modern Norman {{m|no|pouquette}} and modern French {{m|fr|pochette}} from Old French {{m|fro|pochete}}, from {{m|fro|puche}}), from {{der|en|frk|*po

polish.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*pel-|id=drive}}
From {{inh|en|enm|polishen}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}} ''poliss-'', stem of some of the conjugated forms of {{m|fro|polir}}, from {{der|en|la|polio|polīre|to polish, make smooth}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pelh₂-||to drive, strike, thrust}}, from the notion of fulling cloth.

pollution.text: From {{inh|en|enm|pollucioun}}, {{m|enm|pollucion|t=desecration, impurity}}, from {{der|en|xno|pollutiun}}, {{der|en|frm|pollution}}, {{m|frm|pollucion}}, and their source, post-classical {{der|en|la|pollūtiō||defilement, desecration; nocturnal emission}} (4th century), from the participial stem of {{m|la|polluō||to soil, defile, contaminate}}, from {{m|la|por-||before}} + {{m|la|-luō|t=to smear}}

pop.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:pop//poppe<ety:from<enm:poppen>>|id=sound|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|pop}}, {{m|enm|poppe|t=a blow; strike; buffet}} (> {{cog|enm|poppen|pos=verb|t=to strike; thrust}}), of {{onom|en|nocap=1}} origin – used to describe the sound, or short, sharp actions. The physics sense is part of a facetious sequence "[[snap]], [[crackle]], pop", after the mascots of ''Rice Krispies'' cereal.

population.text: {{bor+|en|la-lat|populatio||a people, multitude}}, as if a noun of action from Classical {{der|en|la|populus}}, equivalent to {{af|en|populate|-ion}}. {{dbt|en|poblacion}}.

portfolio.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|it:portafoglio}}
{{bor+|en|it|portafoglio}}; cognate with {{cog|fr|portefeuille||folder, wallet}}, from {{der|en|la|portāre||to carry}} and {{m|la|folium||sheet}}. The meaning "collection of responsibilities" came by extension in the 1930s.

portion.text: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:porcioun|tree=1}} {{dercat|en|ine-pro}} From {{inh|en|enm|porcioun}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|porcion|}}, accusative of {{der|en|la|portiō|alt=	portiōnem|t=a share, part, portion, relation, proportion}}, from {{m|la|portiō}}, akin to {{m|la|pars||part}}; see {{m|en|part}}. Compare {{m|en|proportion}}.

pose.text: From {{inh|en|enm|pose}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ġeposu|t=cold in the head; catarrh|lit=(the) sneezes; (the) snorts|g=p}}, from {{der|en|ang|pos}}, {{m|ang|ġepos|t=sneeze, snort}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pos}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*pusą|t=sneeze, snort}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*pusōną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*pusjaną|t=to snort, blow}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*pus-|t=to blow, breathe hard}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*

positive.text:
{{ety|en|:der|fro:positif<ety:der<la:positivus>>|tree=+}}
From {{der|en|fro|positif}}, from {{der|en|la|positivus}}, from the past participle stem of {{m|la|ponere|t=to place}}. Compare {{m|en|posit}}.

pour.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|pouren|t=to pour}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Perhaps from {{der|en|fro-nor|purer|t=to sift (grain), pour out (water)}}, from {{der|en|la|pūrō|t=to purify}}, from {{m|la|pūrus|t=pure}}. Compare {{cog|dum|afpuren|t=to pour off, drain}}.

{{m|en||To pour}} displaced several Middle English verbs:
* {{m|enm|schenchen}}, {{m|enm|schenken|t=to pour}}, from {{noncog|ang|sċenċan|t=to

poverty.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂w-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|poverte}}, from {{der|en|fro|poverté|}} (Modern French {{m|fr|pauvreté}}), from {{der|en|la|paupertās}}, from {{m|la|pauper||poor}} + {{m|la|-tas||noun of state suffix}}. Cognates include {{m|en|pauper}}, {{m|en|poor}}.

precious.text: {{inh+|en|enm|precious}}, {{lg|loanword|borrowed}} from {{der|en|fro|precios|t=valuable, costly, precious, beloved, also affected, finical}}, from {{der|en|la|pretiōsus|t=of great value, costly, dear, precious}}, from {{m|la|pretium|t=value, price}}; see {{m|en|price}}.

predict.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deyḱ-}}
Early 17th century, from {{bor|en|la|praedicō||to mention beforehand}} (perfect passive participle {{m|la|praedictus}}), from {{m|la|prae-||before}} + {{m|la|dīcō||to say}}. Equivalent to Germanic {{m|en|forespeak}}, {{m|en|foretell}}, and {{m|en|foresay}}.

pregnant.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|preignant}}, from {{der|en|fro|preignant}}, {{m|fro|pregnant}}, also {{m|fro|prenant}} (compare archaic Modern French {{m|fr|prégnant}}), and their source, {{der|en|la|praegnāns||pregnant}}, probably from {{m|la|prae-||pre-}} + {{m|la||*gnāscī}}, an archaic form of {{m|la|nascor|nāscī|to be born}}. Displaced {{noncog|ang|bearnēacen}} (literally "child-enlarged").

====Adjective==

preliminary.text: {{bor+|en|la-new|praelīmināris}}, formed from {{m|la|prae-|t=before}} + {{m|la|līmen|t=threshold}} + {{m|la|-āris|pos=adjectival suffix}}; compare {{cog|la|līmināris||of or belonging to a threshold}}. Compare {{bor|en|fr|préliminaire}}.

prepare.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-}}
Partially a {{back-formation|en|preparation|nocap=1}}; and partially borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|preparer}}, from Classical {{der|en|la|praeparo|praeparāre|t=make ready in advance}}, from {{m|la|prae-|t=pre-}} + {{m|la|paro|parāre|t=make ready}}. Compare {{cog|enm|preparaten|t=to prepare}}.

prescription.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|prescripcion}}, from {{der|en|la|praescriptio||[[preface]]; [[pretext]]; [[something]] [[written]] [[ahead of time]]}}, from {{m|la|prae-||[[pre-]], [[before]]}} + {{m|la|scribo|scribere|to [[write]]}} + {{m|la|-tio||[[-tion]], ''[[form]]ing [[noun]]s''}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|prescribe|tion}}.

presence.text: Through {{uder|en|fro|presence}}, from {{uder|en|la|praesentia||a being present}}, from {{m|la|praesentem}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|andweardnes}}.

presentation.text: From {{uder|en|fro|presentation}} (French {{m|fr|présentation}}), from {{uder|en|la|praesentātiōnem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|praesentātiō||representation, exhibition}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|present|ation}}.

preserve.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ser- (guard)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|preserven}}, from {{der|en|fro|preserver}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} {{m|la|prēservāre||keep, preserve}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|prēserven|v.|MED34513|26 February 2020|date=2018}}</ref> from {{der|en|la-lat|-}} {{m|la|praeservāre||guard beforehand}}, from {{affix|la|prae|pos1=adverb|t1=before|servāre|t2=maintain, keep|nocat=1}}. Displaced native {{no

primary.text: {{bor+|en|la|prīmārius||of the first (rank); chief, principal; excellent}}, from {{m|la|prīmus}} (first; whence the {{cog|en|-}} adjective {{m|en|prime}}) + {{m|la|-ārius}} (whence the {{cog|en|-}} suffix {{m|en|-ary}}); compare the {{cog|fr|primaire}}, {{m|fr|primer}}, and {{m|fr|premier}}. {{dbt|en|premier}}.

principle.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|principle}}, from {{der|en|fro|principe}}, from {{der|en|la|prīncipium||beginning, foundation}}, from {{m|la|prīnceps||first}}. {{surf|la|prīmus|t1=first|-ceps|t2=catcher|nocat=1}}; the former ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*preh₂-||before}}; see also {{m|en|prince}}.

private.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:privat<alt:privat(e)><ety:der<la:prīvātus>>}}
From {{inh|en|enm|privat|alt=privat(e)|t=individual, exclusive, private}}, from {{der|en|la|prīvātus||bereaved, deprived, set apart from, release}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|prīvō||to bereave, deprive, release}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=adjective|pos1=adjective-forming suffix}} for more)

privilege.text: From {{inh|en|enm|privilege}}, from {{der|en|xno|privilege}} and {{der|en|fro|privilege}}, from {{der|en|la|prīvilēgium||ordinance or law against or in favor of an individual}}, from {{m|la|prīvus||private}} + {{m|la|lex|lēx, lēg-|law}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|frēols||privilege, immunity}}.

procedure.text: From {{bor|en|fr|procédure}}, from {{der|en|fro|-}}, from {{der|en|la|procedo|procedere|to go forward, proceed}}; see [[proceed]].

proceed.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*ḱyesdʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|proceden}}, from {{der|en|fro|proceder}}, from {{der|en|la|prōcēdō||to go forth, go forward, advance}}, from {{m|la|prō||forth}} + {{m|la|cēdō||to go}}; see [[cede]].

production.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:produccioun<ety:bor<fro:production<ety:der<la:prōductiō>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|produccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|production}}, from {{der|en|la|productio|prōductiō, prōductiōnem|a lengthening, prolonging}}. Equivalent to {{suf|en|produce|tion}}. See {{m|en|produce}}.

profession.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:professioun<ety:bor<xno:professioun<ety:bor<fro:profession>>>>|:af<surf>|profess|-ion|tree=1}}

From {{inh|en|enm|professioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|professioun}}, {{der|en|fro|profession||declaration of faith, religious vows, occupation}}, from {{der|en|la|professiō||avowal, public declaration}}, from the participle stem of {{m|la|profitērī||to profess}}. {{surf|en|profess|-ion}}.

professor.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰeh₂-|id=speak}}
From {{inh|en|enm|professor,professour}}, from {{der|en|xno|proffessur}} and its etymon {{der|en|la|professor||declarer, person who claims knowledge}}, from the {{glossary|past participle}} {{glossary|stem}} of {{m|la|profiteor||profess}}.<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=prō̆fessour|pos=n|id=MED34811}}</ref><ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=2223629015}}</ref> {{surf|en|pro

profile.text: From {{bor|en|fr|profil}}, from {{der|en|it|profilo||a border}}, later also {{m|it|proffilo||a side-face, profile}}, from {{der|en|la|pro||before}} + {{m|it|filo||a line, stroke, thread}}, from {{m|la|filum||a thread}}; see {{m|en|file}}. {{doublet|en|purfle}}.

profit.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*dʰeh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|profit}}, from {{der|en|fro|profit}} (Modern {{cog|fr|profit}}), from {{der|en|la|prōfectus||advance, progress, growth, increase, profit}}, from {{m|la|proficiō||to go forward, advance, make progress, be profitable or useful}}. {{doublet|en|profect}}.

prohibit.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*gʰeh₁bʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|prohibiten}}, from {{der|en|la|prohibeō|t=to fend off, prevent, prohibit}} (through past participle {{m|la|prohibitus}}).

prominent.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*men-|id2=stand out}}
From obsolete {{der|en|fr|prominent}} (compare {{m|fr|proéminent}}), from {{der|en|la|prōminēns}}, present active participle of {{m|la|prōmineō|t=jut out, to project}}, from {{m|la|prō|t=before, forward}} + {{m|la||mineō}} (in compounds, “[[jut]], [[project]]”).

promise.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}}
From {{inh|en|enm|promis|promis, promisse}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|promesse}}, from {{der|en|la-med|prōmissa}}, {{der|en|la|prōmissum|t=a promise}}, feminine and neuter past participles of {{m|la|prōmittō|t=to send forth, to say beforehand, to promise}}, from {{m|la|pro||forth}} + {{m|la|mittere||to send}}; see {{m|en|mission}}. Compare {{m|en|admit}}, {{m|e

promote.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|la:prōmōtus|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|la|prōmōtus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|prōmoveō||move forward, advance}}.

prompt.text: The adjective is from {{inh|en|enm|prompte}}, from {{der|en|frm|prompt}} and its etymon {{der|en|la|prōmptus||visible, apparent, evident}}, past participle of {{m|la|prōmō||to take or bring out or forth, produce, bring to light}}, from {{m|la|prō||forth, forward}} + {{m|la|emō||to take, acquire, buy}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''adv.''|noformat=1|id=1059477500}}</ref> {{doublet|en|pront

property.text: From {{inh|en|enm|propertee}}, {{m|enm|properte}}, {{m|enm|propirte}}, {{m|enm|proprete}}, borrowed from {{der|en|xno|-}} and {{der|en|fro|propreté}}, {{m|fro|proprieté||propriety, fitness, property}}, from {{der|en|la|proprietās||a peculiarity, one's peculiar nature or quality, right or fact of possession, property}}, from {{m|la|proprius||special, particular, one's own}}. Equivalent to {{suffix|

proportion.text:
{{dercat|en|ine-pro}}
From {{inh|en|enm|proporcion}}, from {{der|en|fro|proportion}}, from {{der|en|la|prōportiō|t=comparative relation, proportion, symmetry, analogy}}, from {{m|la|pro|t=for, before}} + {{m|la|portio|t=share, part}}; see {{m|en|portion}}. {{surf|en|pro-|portion}}.

propose.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*tḱey-}}{{word|en|ine|*h₂epó}}
From {{inh|en|enm|proposen}}, from {{der|en|xno|proposer|pos=v}}, {{m|fro|propos|pos=n}}, {{der|en|frm|proposer|pos=v}}, {{m|frm|propos|pos=n}}, from {{der|en|la|propono|prōpōnō, prōpōnere}}, with conjugation altered based on {{m|fro|poser}}. {{doublet|en|propound}}.

prospect.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|prospecte}}, from {{der|en|la|prōspectus|t=view, sight, prospect; panorama}}, from {{m|la|prōspiciō|t=to look forward}} + {{m|la|-tus|pos=suffix forming action nouns}}, from {{m|la|pro||before, forward}} + {{m|la|speciō}}, {{m|la|spiciō|t=to look, to see}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=3574110376}}</ref> {{surf|en|pro-|-spect}}. {{doublet|en|prospectus|p

protein.text: From {{con|en|proto-|ein}}. Suggested by {{w|Jöns Jacob Berzelius}} in a letter to {{w|Gerardus Johannes Mulder}}, from {{bor|en|fr|protéine}} and {{der|en|de|Protein}}, both coined based on {{der|en|grc|πρωτεῖος||primary}}, from {{m|grc|πρῶτος||first}}.<ref>{{R:New English Dictionary}}</ref>

protocol.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|[[protocolle]], [[protocole]]||document, record}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|protocollum||the first sheet of a volume (on which contents and errata were written)}}, from {{der|en|gkm|πρωτόκολλον||first sheet glued onto a manuscript}}, from {{m|grc|πρῶτος||first}} + {{m|grc|κόλλα||glue}}.

psychology.text: From {{bor|en|fr|psychologie}}, from {{der|en|la-ren|psychologia}}, from {{der|en|grc|ψυχή|t=soul}} + {{m|grc|-λογία||study of}}, equivalent to {{confix|en|psycho-|-logy}}. The Latin term is believed by some to have been coined in a lost treatise by Croatian humanist {{w|Marko Marulić}} (1450–1524), but this is disputed by other scholars. It is {{etydate|1570s|nocap=1}}, at which time it was appar

publicity.text: From {{der|en|fr|publicité}}, From {{der|en|la-med|pūblicitātem}}, accusative singular of {{m|la|pūblicitās}}, from {{der|en|la|pūblicus||public, general}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|public|ity}}.

publish.text: From {{inh|en|enm|publicen}} (by analogy with {{m|en|banish}}, {{m|en|finish}}), from {{der|en|fro|publier}}, from {{der|en|la|publicare||to make public, show or tell to the people, make known, declare, also (and earlier) confiscate for public use}}, from {{m|la|publicus||pertaining to the people, public}}; see {{m|en|public}}.

pump.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|pumpe}}, possibly from {{der|en|dum|pompe|t=pipe, water conduit}} or {{der|en|gml|pumpe|t=pump}}, probably ultimately {{onomatopoeic|en|title=imitative}}. 

Compare {{cog|nl|pompen}}, {{cog|de|pumpen}}, and {{cog|da|pompe}}; also {{cog|es|bomba|t=pump}}.

{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q134574}}A device for moving or compressing a liquid or gas.
#: {{ux|en|This '''pump'

purchase.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|purchasen}}, from {{der|en|xno|purchacer||seek to obtain}} from {{m|fro|pur-}} (from {{der|en|la|pro-}}) + {{m|fro|chacier|chac(i)er|to chase, pursue}}. Compare {{cog|fro|porchacier||to follow, to chase}}, which has given {{cog|fr|pourchasser||to chase without relent}}.

pursue.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*sekʷ-|id2=follow}}
From {{inh|en|enm|pursuen}}, from {{der|en|xno|pursure}}, {{m|fro|poursuire}} etc., from {{der|en|la|prōsequor}} (though influenced by {{m|la|persequor}}). {{doublet|en|prosecute}}.

pursuit.text: From {{inh|en|enm|pursuyte}}, from {{der|en|fro|poursuite}}, from the verb {{m|fro|porsuir||to pursue}}.

qualification.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|qualification}} in the 1540s, which in turn derives from {{der|en|la-med|quālificātiō}}. {{surf|en|qualify|-ification|alt1=qual(ify)}}.

quality.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kʷ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|qualite}}, from {{der|en|fro|qualité}}, from {{der|en|la|quālitās|quālitās, quālitātem}}, from {{m|la|quālis||of what kind}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷo-||who, how}}. Cicero coined {{m|la|qualitas}} as a calque to translate the {{cog|grc|-}} word {{m|grc|ποιότης||quality}}, coined by Plato from {{m|grc|ποῖος||of what nature, of what kind}}.

quarter.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:quarter|id=fourth}}
From {{inh|en|enm|quarter}}, from {{der|en|xno|quarter}}, from {{der|en|la|quartarius}}, from {{m|la|quartus}}. Compare {{cog|es|cuarto||room, quarters; quarter}}. {{doublet|en|quartier}}.

{{en-noun|~}}

questionnaire.text:
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:questionnaire|tree=++}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|questionnaire}}, from {{uder|en|la-lat|quaestionarius}}, from {{m|la|quaestio}} (English {{m|en|question}}) + {{m|la|-arius}}, from {{m|la|quaerō||to question}} (English {{m|en|query}}).

quote.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:quoten<ety:bor<fro:coter<ety:der<la-med:quotāre<ety:from<la:quotus>>>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|quoten}}, {{m|enm|coten|t=to mark (a book) with chapter numbers or marginal references}}, from {{der|en|fro|coter}}, from {{der|en|la-med|quotāre|t=to distinguish by numbers, number chapters}}, itself from {{der|en|la|quotus|t=which, what number (in sequence)}}, from {{m|la|quot

rack.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|rakke}}, {{m|enm|rekke}}, from {{der|en|dum|rac}}, {{m|dum|recke}}, {{m|dum|rec}} ({{cog|nl|rek}}), see {{m|nl|rekken}}.

{{en-noun}}

radical.text:
{{PIE word|en|wréh₂ds}}
{{inh+|en|enm|radical}}, from {{der|en|la|rādīcālis|t=of or pertaining to the root, having roots, radical}}. Compare {{m|en|grassroots}}.

rail.text:
{{etymon|en|id=straight|:inh|enm:rail<ety:inh<ang:regol>:bor<fro:reille<ety:inh<la:rēgula>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|enm|rail}}, {{m|enm|rayl}}, {{m|enm|*reȝel}}, {{m|enm|*reȝol}} (found in {{m|enm|reȝolsticke||a ruler}}), partly from {{der|en|ang|regol||a ruler, straight bar}} and partly from {{der|en|fro|reille}}; both from {{der|en|la|regula||rule, bar}}, from {{m|la|regō||to rule, to guide, to

random.text:
{{etymon|en|id=haphazard|randon<ety:inh<enm:randoun>>}}
From earlier {{m|en|randon}}, from {{inh|en|enm|randoun}}, {{m|enm|raundon}}, from {{der|en|fro|randon}}, from {{m|fro|randir|t=to run, gallop}} (whence French {{m|fr|randonnée||long walk, hike}}), from {{der|en|frk|*randiju|t=a run, race}} or {{der|en|non|rend|t=a run, race}}, both from {{der|en|gem-pro|*randijō}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*rinnaną|

rank.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|rank|t=strong, proud}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ranc|t=proud, haughty, arrogant, insolent, forward, overbearing, showy, ostentatious, splendid, bold, valiant, noble, brave, strong, full-grown, mature}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*rank}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*rankaz|t=straight}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-|t=straight, direct}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|rank|t=s

rapid.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor<conj:and>|frm:rapide<ety:der<la:rapidus>>|la:rapidus|tree=1}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|rapide}} and its etymon {{bor|en|la|rapidus}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'', ''adv.'', and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=9625407388}}</ref>

rare.text: From {{inh|en|enm|rare}}, from {{der|en|fro|rare}}, {{m|fro|rere|t=rare, uncommon}}, from {{der|en|la|rārus|t=loose, spaced apart, thin, infrequent}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁reh₁-|t=friable, thin}}. Displaced native {{m+|en|geason|t=rare, scarce}} (from {{ncog|enm|gesen}}, from {{ncog|ang|gǣsne}}); and largely displaced {{ncog|enm|seld|t=rare, uncommon}} (from {{ncog|ang|selden}}) and {{ncog|enm

rat.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*Hreh₃d-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|raat}}, {{m|enm|rat}}, {{m|enm|ratt}}, {{m|enm|ratte}}, {{m|enm|rotte}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ræt}}, {{m|ang|rætt}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*ratt}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*rattaz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*rattō|t=rat}}, of uncertain origin, possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*Hreh₃d-|t=to gnaw, scrape, scratch}}. However, the rat may have been unknown in Northern Europ

rear.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|reren|t=to raise}}, from {{inh|en|ang|rǣran||to raise, set upright, promote, exalt, begin, create, give rise to, excite, rouse, arouse, stir up}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*raiʀijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*raizijaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*raisijaną|t=to cause to rise, raise}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁rey-||to lift oneself, rise}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|rere||to construct, build, rear}

receipt.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|receyt}}, recorded since c. 1386 as "statement of ingredients in a potion or medicine," from {{der|en|xno|-}} or {{der|en|fro-nor|receite|t=receipt, recipe}} (1304), altered (by influence of {{m|fro|receit||he receives}}, from {{cog|la|recipit}}) from {{der|en|fro|recete}}, from {{der|en|la|receptus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|recipiō}

reception.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|recepcion,reception}}, from {{der|en|frm|reception}}, from {{der|en|la|receptiō|alt=receptiōn-||the act of receiving; reception}}, from {{m|la|recipiō||receive}}, from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|capiō||to hold}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=6819545210}}</ref> Equivalent to {{suf|en|receive|tion}}.

recipe.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|récipé}}, from {{der|en|la|recipe}}, second person singular imperative of {{der|en|la|recipiō||receive}}.

recipient.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|récipient}}, from {{der|en|la|recipiēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|recipiō||to receive}}.

reference.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰer-}}
From {{bor|en|frm|référence}}, from {{der|en|la-med|referentia}}, nominative neuter plural of {{m|la|referēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|referō||return, reply|lit=carry back}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|refer|ence}}.

reform.text: From {{inh|en|enm|reformen}}, from {{der|en|fro|reformer}}, from {{der|en|la|reformo|reformo, reformare}}. As a noun since 1660s, from {{der|en|fr|réforme}}.

religion.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:religioun|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|religioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|religion}}, from {{der|en|la|religiō||scrupulousness, pious misgivings, superstition, conscientiousness, sanctity, an object of veneration, cult-observance, reverence}}. Most likely from the {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂leg-}} with the meanings preserved in [[Latin]] {{m|la|dīligere}} and {{m|la|legere}} (“to read repe

register.text: From {{der|en|la-med|registrum}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|regesta||list, items recorded}}, from {{der|en|la|regero|regerō|to record, to carry back}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|gero|gerō|t=to carry, bear}}. Compare {{cog|la|registoria||a treasurer}}. Some senses influenced by association with unrelated {{noncog|la|rego|regō|to rule}}.

relevant.text: From {{bor|en|sco|relevant}} meaning "legally pertinent," used in Scottish legal circles starting in the early 1500s, and first used in English in the 1700s. Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|relevāns|relevāns, relevāntem}}, present active participle of {{m|la|relevō||lift up again, lighten, relieve}}, from {{m|la|re-||again}} + {{m|la|levō||lift}}.

regulate.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|regulatus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|regulō||to direct, rule, regulate}} (see {{m|en|-ate|id=verb|pos=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|regula||rule}}, from {{m|la|regō||to keep straight, direct, govern, rule}}. Compare {{m|en|regle}}, {{m|en|rail}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|metegian}}.

reject.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|rejecten|}}, from {{der|en|la|reiectus}}, past participle of {{m|la|reicio|reicere|to throw back}}, from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|iacio|iacere|to throw}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|āweorpan|lit=to throw out}}.

request.text: From {{inh|en|enm|request}}, from {{der|en|fro|requeste}} ({{cog|fr|requête}}), from {{der|en|la-vul|*requaesita}}, from {{der|en|la|requīsīta}}, feminine of {{m|la|requīsītus||requested, demanded}}, past participle of {{m|la|requīrō||require, ask}}, composed of {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|quaerō||to seek, look for}}, of uncertain origin, but possibly from {{der|en|itc-pro|*kʷaizeō}}, from {{der|en|ine-

reputation.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*pewH-}}
14c. "credit, good reputation", from {{inh|en|enm|reputacion,reputacioun,reputation,reputatioun}}, from {{der|en|xno|reputacion,reputacioun}}, {{der|en|frm|reputation}} ({{cog|fr|réputation}}), and their etymon {{der|en|la|reputātiō|reputātiōnem|consideration, thinking over}}, noun of action from past participle stem of {{m|la|reputō||reflect upon, reckon, count over}},

rescue.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|rescouen}}, from {{der|en|fro|rescoure}}, {{m|fro|rescurre}}, {{m|fro|rescorre}}; from {{der|en|la|-}} prefix {{m|la|re-||re-}} + {{m|la|excutiō|excutere|t=to shake or drive out}}, from {{m|la|ex||out}} + {{m|la|quatiō||to shake}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|nerian}}.
{{wp}}

reluctant.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*lewg-}}
{{lbor|en|la|reluctāns}} (whence {{suf|en|-ant}}), present participle of {{m|la|reluctor||to struggle against, oppose, resist}}, from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|luctor||to struggle}} (whence {{af|en|re-}}.

representative.text: From {{inh|en|enm|representative}}, from {{der|en|frm|representatif}} and its etymon {{der|en|la-med|repraesentātīvus}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=6753272964}}</ref> {{surf|en|represent|-ative}}; See [[representation]]. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|spala||a representative}}.

rely.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leyǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|relien}}, from {{der|en|fro|relier||fasten, attach, rally, oblige}}, from {{der|en|la|religo||fasten, bind fast}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|ligo}}.

remind.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*men- (think)}}
From mid 17th century, equivalent to {{af|en|re-|mind|t2=to remember}}. Probably suggested by obsolete {{m|en|rememorate}} with the same sense. Displaced {{ncog|ang|myndgian}}.

remove.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:removen<ety:bor<xno:remover<ety:from<fro:removoir>>>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|removen}}, from {{der|en|xno|remover}}, {{m|fro|removeir}}, from {{der|en|fro|remouvoir}}, from {{der|en|la|removeo|removēre}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|moveo|movēre|to move}}, equivalent to {{affix|en|re-|move}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|āfierran}}.

residence.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sed-}}
{{inh+|en|enm|residence}}, from {{der|en|fro|residence}}, from {{der|en|la-med|residentia}}, from {{m|la|residēns}}, present participle of {{m|la|resideō}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|reside|-ence}}. {{dbt|en|residencia}}.

revenue.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʷem-}}
Recorded in English from 1433, "income from property or possessions", from {{uder|en|frm|revenue}}, from {{uder|en|fro|||a return}} (modern French {{m|fr|revenu}}), the prop. feminine past participle of {{m|fro|revenir||come back}} (=modern French), from {{uder|en|la|revenire||to return, come back}}, from {{affix|la|re-|t1=back|venire|t2=to come|nocat=1}}.

restaurant.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|fr:restaurant|tree=1}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|restaurant}}, present participle of the verb {{m|fr|restaurer}}, corresponding to {{der|en|la|restaurans|restaurans, restaurantis}}, present participle of {{m|la|restauro||to restore}}, from the name of the 'restorative' soup served in the first establishments.

revelation.text: From {{inh|en|enm|revelacioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|revelacion}}, from {{der|en|la|revēlātiō||disclosure}}, from {{m|la|revēlō||to disclose}}, {{m|la|re||again}} + {{m|la|vēlō||to cover}}; {{surf|en|revelate|-ion|nocap=1}}.

reveal.text: From {{inh|en|enm|revelen|revēlen|id=to reveal}}, from {{der|en|fro|reveler}}, from {{der|en|la|revēlāre|t=to reveal, uncover}}, from {{m|la|re-|t=back, again}} + {{m|la|vēlāre|t=to cover}}, from {{m|la|vēlum||a cloth, covering, curtain, veil, awning, sail}} (whence also {{cog|en|veil}}, {{cog|en|unveil}}, {{cog|en|voile}}, {{cog|ru|вуаль}}, {{cog|ru|завуали́ровать||to veil}} (compare typologicall

resign.text:
From {{uder|en|xno|resigner}}, {{uder|en|frm|resigner}}, and its source, {{uder|en|la|resignāre||to unseal, annul, assign, resign}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|signāre||to seal, stamp}}. {{piecewise doublet|en|re-sign}}.
[[File:Nixon Farewell.jpg|thumb|{{w|Richard Nixon}} '''resigning''' from the U.S. presidency. As of 2024, Richard Nixon is the only U.S. President to '''resign''' from office.]]

review.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weyd-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|revewe}}, {{m|enm|reveue}}, from {{der|en|fro|reveue|reveüe}}, {{m|fro|revue}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|revue}}), feminine form of {{m|fro|reveu|reveü}}, past participle of {{m|fro|reveoir}} (French: {{m|fr|revoir}}), from {{der|en|la|revideō}}, from {{m|la|re-}} +{{m|la|videō||see, observe}} (English: {{m|en|video}}). Equivalent to {{prefix|en|re|view}}.

resistance.text: From earlier {{m|en|resistence}}, from {{inh|en|enm|resistence}}, from {{der|en|fro|resistence}}, from {{der|en|la|resistentia}}. Morphologically {{suffix|en|resist|-ance}}.

response.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:respounse<ety:bor<fro:respuns>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|respounse}}, {{m|enm|respons}}, from {{der|en|fro|respons}}, {{m|fro|respuns}}, {{m|fro|responce}}, ultimately from the {{der|en|la|respōnsum}}, a nominal use of the neuter form of {{m|la|respōnsus}}, the perfect passive participle of {{m|la|respondeō}}, from {{m|la|re||again}} + {{m|la|spondeō||promise}}. {{doublet|en

responsibility.text: From {{suffix|en|responsible|ity}}. Although the components are of French origin, the compound appears to have been formed in English.  Later-attested {{cog|fr|responsabilité}} is modeled on the English word, and {{cog|it|responsabilità}} is in turn modeled on the French.

retain.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*wert-|*ten-}}
From Late {{inh|en|enm|reteinen}}, {{m|enm|retein|t=to continue to keep, retain; to continue to possess; to possess; to contain; to draw back, retire; to hold back, restrain; to keep in mind, remember; to take back, repossess; to appoint; to engage in one’s service, employ, hire}}{{nb...|retainen, retayne, reteign, reteigne, reteine, retene, retenne, reteyene, rete

respond.text: From {{inh|en|enm|respounden}}, from {{der|en|fro|respondre}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|respondō}}, from {{der|en|la|respondeō}}. Cf. Modern {{cog|fr|répondre}}.

restrict.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*streyg-}}
{{bor+|en|la|restrictus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|restringō||draw back tightly; restrain, restrict}}, from {{m|la|re-||back, again}} + {{m|la|stringō||press, tighten, compress}}. {{doublet|en|ristretto}} as an adjective.

rock.text:
{{etymon|en|id=stone|:inh|enm:rokke|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|rocke}}, {{m|enm|rokke|t=rock formation}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*rocc|t=rock}}, as in {{cog|ang|stānrocc|t=high stone rock, peak, obelisk}}, and also later from {{der|en|xno|roche|roque}}, (compare Modern {{cog|fr|roc}}, {{m|fr|roche}}, {{m|fr|rocher}}), from {{der|en|la-med|rocca}} (attested 767), of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin, sometimes said

rival.text: {{lbor|en|la|rīvālis|lit=person using the same stream as another}}. {{surf|en|la:rīvus|-al}}.

royal.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|royal}}, from {{der|en|fro|roial}} (Modern French {{m|fr|royal}}), from {{der|en|la|rēgālis}}, from {{m|la|rēx||king}}. {{doublet|en|regal|t1=befitting a king|real|t2=unit of currency|ariary|riyal}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|real}}, {{cog|it|reale}}, {{cog|ca|reial}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|cynelīċ}}.

reward.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*wer-|id=heed}}
From {{inh|en|enm|reward}}, {{m|enm|rewarde}}, from {{der|en|fro|reward||reward}} (compare {{cog|fro|regard}}, whence modern French {{m|fr|regard}}, and also English {{m|en|regard}} through Middle French), from {{m|fro|rewarder||to reward}} (compare {{cog|fro|reguarder}}), from {{m|fro|re-}} + {{m|fro|warder||to guard, keep}} (compare {{cog|fro|guarder}}); the Ang

revise.text: Borrowed from {{bor|en|frm|réviser}}, from {{der|en|la|revīsō}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|vīsō||examine}}, frequentative of {{m|la|videō||see}}.

revolution.text: {{inh+|en|enm|revolucion}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|revolucion}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|revolūtiō||the act of revolving; revolution}}, from {{der|en|la|revolvō||roll back, revolve}}.

routine.text:
{{ety|en|:ubor|fr:routine|text=+|tree=1}} {{surface analysis|en|route|-ine}}. Further from {{der|en|la|rupta via}}.

Compare typologically {{m|en|travel}} << {{m+|la|tripālium}}, whence also {{m|en|travail}}, note the inverse semantic vector from a subjective state (toil) to an objective action (journey). Also compare {{m+|cs|běžný}} (< {{m|cs|běžet}}), {{m+|ru|обихо́д}}, {{m|ru|обихо́дный}} (akin

salary.text: From {{inh|en|enm|salarie}}, from {{der|en|xno|salarie}}, from {{der|en|fro|salaire}}, from {{der|en|la|salārium||wages}}, the neuter form of the adjective {{m|la|salārius||related to salt}}, from {{m|la|sal||salt}}. {{PIE word|en|sḗh₂l}}
From {{inh|en|enm|sauce}},<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> from {{der|en|fro|sause}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*salsa}}, noun use of the feminine of {{der|en|la|salsus||salted}}, past participle of {{m|la|saliō||to salt}}, from {{m|la|sal}}.<ref> [https://web.archive.org/web/20190421182905/http://thetastermagazine.com/tag/sauce/ "Pure Sauce 4.12.14"]. From {{inh|en|enm|reule}}, {{m|enm|rewle}}, {{m|enm|rule}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|riule}}, {{m|fro|reule}}, from {{der|en|la|regula||straight stick, bar, ruler, pattern}}, from {{m|la|regō||to keep straight, direct, govern, rule}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃réǵeti||to straighten; right}}, from the root {{m|ine-pro|*h₃reǵ-}}; see {{m|en|regent}}. {{doublet

sack.text:
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:sak}}
From {{inh|en|enm|sak}}, {{m|enm|sek}}, {{m|enm|sach}}, {{m|enm|zech|t=bag, sackcloth}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sacc|t=sack, bag}} and {{m|ang|sæċċ|t=sackcloth, sacking}}; both from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sakku}}, from late {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sakkuz|t=sack}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|saccus|t=large bag}}, from {{der|en|grc|σάκκος|t=bag of coarse cloth}}, from {{der|en|sem}}, possibly

{{ety|en|:der|frm:satellite}}
From {{der|en|frm|satellite}}, from {{der|en|la|satelles||attendant}}. Ultimately perhaps of {{uder|en|ett|-}} origin.

science.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:science<id:knowledge>|id=collective discipline}}
From {{inh|en|enm|science}}, {{m|enm|scyence}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|science}}, {{m|fro|escience}}, from {{der|en|la|scientia||[[knowledge]]}}, from {{m|la|sciēns}}, the [[Appendix:Glossary#present participle|present participle]] stem of {{m|la|scire||to [[know]]}}.

Partially displaced native {{ncog|ang|sċēara||scissors, shears}}, whence {{m|en|shears}}. {{doublet

{{ety|en|:inh|enm:scrue|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|screw}}, {{m|enm|scrue|t=screw}}; apparently, despite the difference in meaning, from {{der|en|fro|escroue|t=nut, cylindrical socket, screwhole}}, from {{der|en|la|scrōfa||female pig}} through comparison with the corkscrew shape of a pig's penis. There is also the {{cog|fro|escruve|t=screw}}, from {{der|en|odt|*scrūva}} {{gloss|"screw"; whence {{c

score.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:score|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|score}}, {{m|enm|skore}}, {{m|enm|schore}}, from {{inh|en|ang|scoru||notch; tally; score}}, from {{der|en|non|skor}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skurō||incision; tear; rift}}, which is related to {{m|gem-pro|*skeraną||to cut}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)ker-||cut}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|skora}}, {{cog|sv|skåra}}, {{cog|da|skår}}. Relate

From {{inh|en|enm|scateren}}, {{m|enm|skateren}}, also {{m|enm|schateren}},

* or from {{inh|en|ang|*sceaterian}}, probably akin to a dialect of {{der|en|non|-}}, possibly ultimately related to {{der|en|ine-pro|*skey-||to cut, split, shatter}}.

Compare {{cog|dum|scheteren||to scatter}},

section.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sek-}}
From {{der|en|enm|seccioun}}, from {{der|en|fro|section}}, from {{der|en|la|sectiō||cutting, cutting off, excision, amputation of diseased parts of the body, etc.}}, from {{m|la|sectus}}, past participle of {{m|la|secāre||to cut}}. More at {{l|en|saw}}.

seal.text:
[[File:Hydrurga leptonyx.JPG|thumb|A seal ({{senseno|en|Q3192954}}) (in this instance, a [[leopard seal]])]]
From {{inh|en|enm|sel|id=pinniped}}, from an inflectional form of {{inh|en|ang|seolh}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*selh}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*selhaz}} (compare {{cog|sco|selch}},''[[selkie]]'', {{cog|frr|selich}}, {{cog|dum|seel}}, {{m|dum|zēle}}, {{cog|goh|selah}}, {{cog|da|sæl}}, {{cog|gm

scan.text:
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:scanne|tree=1}}
From late {{inh|en|enm|scanne|t=to mark off verse to show metrical structure}}, from earlier {{m|enm|scanden}}, from {{der|en|la-lat||scandere|t=to scan verse}}, from Classical {{m+|la|scandō|t=to climb, rise, mount}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skend-||to jump, dart, climb, scale, scan}}.

secondary.text: From {{inh|en|enm|secundarie}}, from {{der|en|la|secundārius||of the second class or quality}}, from {{m|la|secundus}} (whence the {{cog|en|second}}) + {{m|la|-ārius}} (whence the English suffix {{m|en|-ary}}), equivalent to {{af|en|second|-ary}}; compare the {{cog|fr|secondaire}}, the {{cog|it|secondario}}, the {{cog|oc|secundari}}, the {{cog|pt|secundario}}, and the {{cog|es|secundario}}.

schedule.text:
{{inh+|en|enm|cedule}}, from {{der|en|frm|cedule}} (whence {{cog|fr|cédule}}), from {{der|en|fro|cedule}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|schedula||papyrus strip}}, diminutive of {{der|en|la|scheda}}, from {{der|en|grc|σχέδη||papyrus leaf}}, from {{der|en|grk-pro|*skʰíďďō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*skid-yé-ti}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*skeyd-||to divide, split}}. {{doublet|en|cedula|cedule}}.

This word was histo

scheme.text:
From late {{inh|en|enm|scheame}}, from {{der|en|la-med|schēma|t=figure, form}}, from {{der|en|grc|σχῆμα|t=form, shape}}, from {{m|grc|ἔχω|t=to hold}}. {{doublet|en|schema}}. Compare {{m|en|sketch}}.
{{root|en|ine-pro|*seǵʰ-}}

sculpture.text: From {{inh|en|enm|sculpture}}, from {{der|en|fro|sculpture}}, from {{der|en|la|sculptūra||sculpture}}, from {{m|la|sculpō||to cut out, to carve in stone}}.

scandal.text: From {{der|en|frm|scandale||indignation caused by misconduct or defamatory speech}}, from {{der|en|la-ecc|scandalum||that on which one trips, cause of offense|lit=stumbling block}}, from {{der|en|grc|σκάνδαλον||a trap laid for an enemy, a cause of moral stumbling}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*skand-||to jump}}. Cognate with {{cog|la|scandō||to climb}}. First attested from {{cog|fro-nor|escandle}}, but

scratch.text:
From {{inh|en|enm|scracchen}}, of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Potentially a blend of {{der|en|enm|scratten|t=to scratch}} and {{m|enm|cracchen|t=to scratch}}. Ultimately {{onomatopoeic|en|nocap=1}}. More at {{m|en|scrat}} and {{m|en|cratch}}.

Compare {{ncog|ang|scrama}}, {{ncog|non|skråma}}, {{ncog|de|Schramme||scratch}}, which may be related.

shallow.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kelh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|schalowe|t=not deep, shallow}}; apparently related to {{cog|enm|schalde}}, {{m|enm|schold}}, {{m|enm|scheld}}, {{m|enm|schealde|t=shallow}}, from {{cog|ang|sċeald|t=shallow}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skal-}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kelh₁-|t=to parch, dry out}}.<ref>{{R:ine:IEW|927}}</ref> Related to {{cog|nds|Scholl|t=shallow water}}. See also {{l

settle.text:
From a merger of two verbs:
* {{inh|en|enm|setlen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|setlan|t=to settle, seat, put to rest}}, from {{der|en|ang|setl||seat}} (compare {{cog|nl|zetelen||to be established, settle}}) and
* {{inh|en|enm|sahtlen}}, {{m|enm|seihtlen|t=to reconcile, calm, subside}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sahtlian}}, {{m|ang|ġesehtlian|t=to reconcile}}, from {{der|en|ang|saht}}, {{m|ang|seht|t=settlement, a

sequence.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sekʷ-|id=follow}}
From {{inh|en|enm|sequence}},<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> from {{der|en|fro|sequence|t=a sequence of cards, answering verses}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|sequentia|t=a following}}, from {{der|en|la|sequēns|t=following}}, from {{m|la|sequī|t=to follow}}; see {{m|en|sequent}}.

secure.text: {{bor+|en|la|sēcūrus||of persons, free from care, quiet, easy; in a bad sense, careless, reckless; of things, tranquil, also free from danger, safe, secure}}, from {{m|la|sē-||without}} + {{m|la|cūra||care}}; see [[cure]]. {{doublet|en|sure}} and the now obsolete or dialectal {{doublet|en|sicker|t1=certain, safe|notext=-}}.

series.text:
{{etymon|en|:bor|la:seriēs|tree=1}}
Attested from the 1610s;<ref>{{R:Etymonline|series}}</ref> {{bor+|nocap=1|en|la|seriēs}}, from {{m|la|sero|serere|t=to join together, bind}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ser-|t=to bind, put together, to line up|id=bind}}. Related to {{m|en|desert}}, {{m|en|insert}}, {{m|en|sermon}}, and {{m|en|sorcerer}}.

senior.text:
{{word|en|ine|sénos}}
From {{inh|en|enm|senior}}, from {{der|en|la|senior||older}}, comparative form of {{m|la|senex||old}}; see {{m|en|senate}}. {{doublet|en|seigneur|seignior|senhor|señor|senyor|signore|sir|sire}}.

select.text:

thorough.text:
{{root|en|ine-pro|*terh₂-}}

The word developed a syllabic form in cases where the word was fully stressed: when it was used as an adverb, adjective, or noun, and less commonly when used as a preposition.
